Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 1:

Explanation of the words:

Al-nas (mankind): humanity. Its singular is insan, though the word nas is not derived from it.

Ittaqu rabbakum (fear your Lord): fear Him lest He punish you, so comply with His command and avoid what He forbids.

Min nafsin wahidatin (from a single soul): this is Adam, peace be upon him.

Wa khalaqa minha zawjaha (and from it He created its mate): He created Hawwa' (Eve) from Adam, from his rib.

Wa baatha (and He spread forth): He dispersed and scattered throughout the earth, from Adam and his wife, men and women in great numbers.

Tasa'aluna bihi (by whom you ask one another): like a man's saying to his brother, "I ask you by God to do such-and-such for me."

Wal-arham (and the wombs): arham is the plural of rahm (womb, kinship). What is meant by being mindful of the ties of kinship is maintaining them and not severing them.

Raqiban (watchful): al-raqib is the Guardian, the All-Knowing.

Meaning of the noble verse:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, addresses His servants with a general expression that includes both the believer and the disbeliever: "O mankind," and commands them to fear Him, mighty and majestic, which means guarding against His punishment in this world and the next by complete submission to Him outwardly and inwardly through Islam. He describes Himself, exalted is He, as their Lord who created them from a single soul, which is Adam, whom He created from clay, and from that soul He created its mate, which is Hawwa'. He, exalted is He, dispersed from the two of them, that is, spread throughout the earth, many men and likewise women. Then He repeated the command to piety, since it is the foundation of the matter: there is no perfection or happiness without adhering to it, saying: "And fear God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs," meaning: fear God your Lord in whom your hearts have believed, so that when one of you wanted something from his brother he would say, "I ask you by God to give me such-and-such." "And fear the wombs, lest you sever them, for in severing them there is great corruption and grave disorder that afflicts your lives and spoils them for you." He, exalted is He, threatened them if they did not comply with His command to piety and did not maintain the ties of kinship, saying: "Indeed God is ever watchful over you," observing your deeds, counting them, guarding them, and recompensing you for them. "O mankind, so fear Him."

Guidance from the noble verse:

From the guidance of the noble verse:

1- The excellence of this verse: when the Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon concerning a matter, he would recite the verse of Al 'Imran, "O you who believe, fear God as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims" [Qur'an 3:102], and recite this verse, then the verse of al-Ahzab, "O you who believe, fear God and speak words of appropriate justice. He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment" [Qur'an 33:70-71], then say, "Amma ba'd" and mention his need.

2- The importance of the command to fear God, since it is repeated twice in one verse, at its beginning and at its end.

3- The obligation of maintaining the ties of kinship and the prohibition of severing them.

4- Observing human brotherhood among people and considering it in dealings.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 4, verses 2–4**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Al-yatama (اليتامى):** the plural of *yatim*, whether male or female. It refers to one whose father has died while he or she has not yet reached puberty.

**Wa la tatabaddalu al-khabitha bi al-tayyib (ولا تتبدَّلوا الخبيث بالطيب):** *al-khabith* is the unlawful and *al-tayyib* is the lawful. Here, what is meant is the bad and the good.

**Hawban kabiran (حوباً كبيراً):** *al-hawb* is a great and momentous sin.

**An la tuqsitu (أن لا تقسطوا):** that you not act justly.

**Mathna wa thulatha waruba' (مثنى وثلاث ورباع):** meaning two, or three, or four, since it is not lawful to exceed four wives.

**Adna alla ta'ulu (أدنى أن لا تعولوا):** nearer to not committing injustice by failing to be equitable among wives.

**Saduqatihinna nihlah (صدقاتهن نحلة):** *sadaqat* is the plural of *sadaqa*, which means the dower and bridal gift. *Nihlah* means an obligatory duty.

**Hanian (هنيئاً):** *al-hani'* is that which is enjoyed when eaten.

**Mari'an (مريئاً):** *al-mari'* is that whose outcome is good, in that it leaves no evil effects.

**The meanings of the verses:**

When Allah, the Exalted, commanded the maintenance of kinship ties and forbade severing them in the previous verse, He commanded in this verse the guardians of orphans to give the orphans their wealth when they reach the age of maturity and their sound judgment becomes evident. So Allah, the Exalted, said: "And give the orphans their property." He forbade them, as a prohibition, to exchange the good property of the orphans for their own bad property. So Allah, the Exalted, said: "And do not substitute the bad [of your own] for the good [of theirs]," meaning the bad of your property for the good of theirs, because that harms the orphan in his wealth. He also forbade them to mix the orphans' property with their own, because that is consuming an orphan's property unjustly. So Allah, the Exalted, said: "And do not consume their property with your own." He gave the reason for this, that it is a great sin, so the Mighty and Majestic said: "Indeed, it [the consuming] is ever a great sin." *Hawb* means sin. This is the meaning of the first verse [2]:

﴿And give the orphans their property, and do not substitute the bad [of your own] for the good [of theirs], and do not consume their property into your own. Indeed, that is ever a great sin.﴾

As for the second verse [3], Allah, the Exalted, guided the guardians of orphan girls: if they fear that they will not be just towards them when one of them marries his ward, He directed them to marry from among the women other than their wards whatever is lawful for them, two, three, or four, meaning two by two, or three by three, or four by four, each according to his ability. This is better than marrying the ward, whose right would then be violated, though her right is more emphatic because of her kinship. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted:

﴿And if you fear that you will not be just concerning orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women, two, three, or four.﴾

And His saying:

﴿But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry] one, or what your right hands possess.﴾

He, the Exalted, means: if a believer fears that he will not be equitable among his wives because of his weakness, then let him be content with one and not add others to her, or let him take concubinage with his slave-woman if he has one, for this is nearer to his not being unjust and wronging his wives. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry] one, or what your right hands possess. That is more suitable that you not incline towards injustice.﴾

In the third and final verse, Allah, the Exalted, commands the believers to give women their dowers as an obligation from Him, which He has imposed upon the man for his wife. It is not lawful for him or for anyone else to take anything from it except with the wife's consent. If she gives it willingly, there is no fault in eating from the dower, based on His saying, the Exalted:

﴿And if they give you willingly of it anything, then consume it with satisfaction and ease.﴾

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Every unlawfully gained property is bad, and every lawful property is good.
2. It is not lawful for a man to exchange a good portion of his ward's property for inferior property of his own, such as taking a fat sheep and giving him a lean one, or taking good dates and giving him poor, worthless ones.
3. It is not lawful to mix an orphan's property with the guardian's property and consume them together, because that involves consuming the orphan's property wrongfully.
4. It is permissible to marry more than one wife, up to four, provided there is assurance against partiality and injustice.
5. Women's dowers are obligatory, and it is forbidden to consume them without the willing consent of the dower's owner. This applies equally to the husband, who is the intended party in the verse, and to the father and relatives.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 5–6:

Explanation of the words:

La tu'tu (لا تؤتوا): do not give.

Al-sufaha' (السفهاء): plural of safih (سفيه), one who does not manage wealth well.

Qiyaman (قياماً): al-qiyam is that by which a thing is sustained. God, exalted is He, made wealth a qiyam, meaning that people's livelihoods and their worldly and also religious interests are sustained by it.

Qawlan ma'rufan (قولاً معروفاً): that is, a speech by which their hearts are content, so that they are not angered or saddened.

Wabtalu al-yatama (وابتلوا اليتامى): that is, test them so that you may know whether they have become capable of managing wealth well.

Balaghu al-nikah (بلغوا النكاح): that is, the age of marriage, which is puberty.

Ansetum (آنستم): you perceived right judgment (rushd) in their conduct.

Israfan wa-bidaran (إسرافاً وبداراً): israf is spending beyond necessary need, and bidar is hastening and rushing to eat from it before it is handed over to the orphan after he attains rushd.

Falyasta'fif (فليستعفف): that is, let him abstain (ya'uff, meaning he refrains) from eating from his ward's property.

Falya'kul bil-ma'ruf (فليأكل بالمعروف): that is, to the extent of necessary need.

Wa-kafa billahi hasiban (وكفى بالله حسيبا): a witness over the two parties, so call witnesses against them.

Meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues with God's guidance of His believing servants to what is good for them in this world, and to their salvation and success in the Hereafter. God the Exalted says in the first verse [5]: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property which God has made for you a means of support; but provide for them from it and clothe them and speak to them with kindly words.﴾ He forbade them to give their property, which is the means of their livelihood, to the foolish, whether a woman, a child, or a man characterized by foolishness, which is lack of insight into financial matters and ignorance of the successful ways of managing them, lest they spend it on other than its proper purposes or ruin it by any kind of waste, such as extravagance and the like. He commanded them to provide for them from it and clothe them. He said "from it" (fiha) and did not say "from them" (minha), indicating that wealth should be developed in trade, industry, or agriculture, so that the capital remains and the living comes only from the profit. He also commanded them to speak to their foolish dependents, who were denied the property, with kindly words, such as a good promise and a good word. This is what the first verse contains. As for the second verse [6], God commanded them to test orphans when they reach the age of rushd or come close to puberty, by giving them some property and asking them to sell or buy. If they find good management in them, they hand over their property to them and call witnesses against them, so that none of them may say one day, "You did not give me my property." ﴿And God suffices as a reckoner﴾, that is, as a witness and a vigilant guardian. The Mighty and Majestic forbade them to eat the orphans' property by extravagance and hastening (before they grow up), meaning: do not eat your orphans' property, O guardians and custodians, by way of extravagance, which is spending beyond the necessary need; and hastening is rushing before the foolish one attains rushd and the property is handed over to him. Then He guided them to the most upright and sound way in this matter, saying: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain; and whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner﴾. The rich guardian must refrain from the orphan's property and not eat any of it at all. The poor guardian may eat reasonably, by borrowing from it and then repaying it when he has means. If the guardian is poor, he may work for wages like other workers; if he is rich, he should work without pay, seeking reward, and his reward is with God, and God does not waste the reward of those who do good.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The legitimacy of restricting the foolish person's control over his property for his own benefit.

2- The recommendation to develop wealth in lawful channels, as indicated by ﴿and provide for them from it﴾.

3- The obligation to test the foolish person before handing his property to him, since property is not handed over except after rushd is established.

4- The obligation to call witnesses when handing property to the orphan after he reaches maturity and rushd.

5- The absolute prohibition of consuming the orphan's property and the property of the foolish person.

6- A guardian of an orphan who is rich must not eat anything from the orphan's property; if he is poor, he may borrow and repay when he is able. If the orphan's property requires a hired worker to manage it, the guardian may take a fair wage (ujrat al-mithl).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 7–10:

Explanation of the words:

Nasib (nasīb): the portion decreed in the Book of God.

Al-walidan (al-wālidān): the father and the mother.

Al-aqrabun (al-aqrabūn): plural of qarib (relative), meaning here the heir by cause, by marriage, or by clientage (walā').

Nasiban mafrudan (naṣīban mafrūḍā): a determined portion, obligatory and binding.

Uli al-qurba (ūlū al-qurbā): the people of kinship who do not inherit because of their distance from the direct lines of descent (ʿamūdayn al-nasab).

Farzuquhum minhu (fārzuqūhum minhu): give them something from which they may be provided for.

Qawlan ma'rufan (qawlan maʿrūfan): speech free of humiliation, reproach, or annoyance (taʾfīf).

Al-khashyah (al-khashyah): fear in a place of safety.

Qawlan sadidan (qawlan sadīdan): right, correct justice.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 11:

Explanation of the words:

Yuwsikum: he enjoins upon you (ya'hadu ilaykum).

Fi awladikum: concerning your children; the word walad applies to both male and female.

Hazz (share): the hazz is a portion or allotment.

Nisa': daughters, whether grown or young.

Thuluthay ma taraka: a third is one of three, and two-thirds is two of three.

Al-sudus (a sixth): one of six.

In kana lahu walad: whether male or female; or if he has a son's son, male or female, the ruling is one.

Fa-in kana lahu ikhwah: two or more.

Min ba'di wasiyyah: that is, the debt is paid first, then the bequest, and the remainder is divided among the heirs.

La tadrun: you do not know.

Fari'dah: God has prescribed this as an obligation upon you.

Alim hakim: All-Knowing of His creation and what is good for them; All-Wise in His disposal of the affairs of His creation and His management for them.

Meaning of the noble verse:

This noble verse [11] — ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children: a male's share is like the share of two females﴾ etc., and the one after it [12], which is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave﴾ etc., were revealed to detail the ruling of verse [7], which contained the legislation of inheritance among Muslim relatives. In the first verse [11], Exalted is He legislates the inheritance of children together with parents. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾, meaning concerning the affairs of your children; ﴿a male's share is like the share of two females﴾, meaning: if a man dies and leaves male and female children, the estate is divided on the basis that the male receives the equivalent of the share of two females. So if he leaves a son, a daughter, and three dinars, the son takes two dinars and the daughter takes one dinar. If he leaves two or more daughters and no male with them, then two or more daughters receive two-thirds, and the remainder goes to the 'asabah, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿If they are women more than two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾. If he leaves one daughter, she has half and the remainder goes to the 'asabah, which is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if she is one, then for her is half﴾. If the deceased leaves his two parents, meaning his mother and father, and leaves children, male or female, then each of his two parents has a sixth and the remainder goes to the children. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has a child﴾, meaning a male or a female. If the deceased has no child and no son's child, then his mother has a third. If he has two or more siblings, then his mother has a sixth. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if he has siblings, then for his mother is a sixth﴾, meaning that she drops from a third to a sixth; this is called hajb (exclusion), so the siblings of her deceased son exclude her from a third to a sixth. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿After any bequest he makes or debt﴾, means that the division of the estate in the manner that He, Exalted, has explained occurs after the settlement of the deceased's debt and the execution of what he bequeathed, if it is a third or less; this is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿after any bequest he makes or debt﴾. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Your fathers and your sons — you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾ means: carry out this prescribed bequest as God has taught you, and do not try to favour one over another, for these heirs are your fathers and your sons, and you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit in this world and the Hereafter.

Therefore, divide the estate as God has taught you, without favouritism, for God Himself is the Divider and the Giver. He is All-Knowing of His creation and of what benefits or harms them, All-Wise in His management of their affairs. So let the matter be entrusted to Him, and let one be content with His division, for it is the division of the All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Guidance from the noble verse:

Among the guidance of the noble verse:

1- God Himself has undertaken the division of inheritances, so it is not lawful for anyone to change any part of them.

2- The two (dual) are treated as a plural.

3- The ruling for a son's son is the ruling for the son himself regarding hajb.

4- The father is an 'asib; he may take his fixed share together with the holders of fixed shares, and what remains he inherits by 'asabah, based on his saying ﷺ: "Give the fixed shares to their people, and whatever remains goes to the nearest male."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 12:

Explanation of the words:

Azwajukum (your spouses): here al-azwaj means the wives.

Walad (child): what is meant here is the son of the loins, whether male or female, and the child of a child is like it.

Rub' (a quarter): one of four.

Kalalah (a person with neither ascendants nor descendants): kalalah is when a deceased person dies leaving neither child nor parent, and his heirs are his maternal siblings.

Lahu akh aw ukht (he has a brother or a sister): that is, from the mother.

Ghayra mudarr (without causing harm): by them, i.e. the bequest and the debt, to any of the heirs.

Halim (forbearing): he does not hasten to punish for disobedience.

Meaning of the noble verse:

The verse before this one was concerned with inheritance through lineage, and this one came to explain inheritance through marriage. Those who inherit through marriage are the husband and the wives. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child.﴾ So if a woman dies, leaving wealth and no child or child's child, male or female, then her husband has half of her estate. If she leaves a child or a child's child, male or female, then her husband has a quarter of her estate and no more, according to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave.﴾ This applies after the settling of any debt, if the deceased owed a debt, and after the execution of the bequest, if the deceased made a bequest, according to His saying: ﴿after any bequest they make or debt.﴾

This is the husband's share. As for the wife's share from her husband, it is a quarter if the husband leaves no child or child's child, male or female. If he leaves a child or a child's child, then the wife has an eighth. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And for them is a quarter of what you leave if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt.﴾

If the deceased husband has two or more wives, they share the quarter equally if the deceased has no child; and if he has a child, they have the eighth, which they share equally. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if a man leaves an estate as kalalah, or a woman,﴾ i.e. one who leaves an estate as kalalah likewise. The deceased kalalah is one who has neither parent nor child. He is inherited by his maternal siblings, as in this verse, or by his full siblings (from both father and mother), as in the verse of kalalah at the end of this surah. If he has a brother from the mother, he has a sixth; likewise if he has a sister, she has a sixth. If there are two or more, they have a third, according to His saying: ﴿And if a man leaves an estate as kalalah, or a woman, and he has a brother or a sister, then each one of them has a sixth.﴾ If they are more than that, they are partners in the third, after a bequest that is made or a debt, without causing harm — such as bequeathing more than a third, or acknowledging a debt when he owes no debt, out of envy or hatred toward the heirs and nothing else. If this becomes clear, the bequest is not executed, the debt is not settled, and the whole estate is divided among the heirs.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A bequest from Allah.﴾ That is, He has enjoined this upon you, O believers, as a bequest; so it is worthy of respect and compliance. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of your intentions and circumstances, and of what harms you and what benefits you, so submit to His division and obey Him therein. He is Forbearing, not hastening to punish, so let not His forbearance deceive you: His seizure is severe and His punishment painful.﴾

Guidance of the verse

From the guidance of the verse:

1- Explanation of the husband's inheritance from his wife, and of the wife's and wives' inheritance from their husbands.

2- Explanation of the inheritance of the kalalah, who leaves neither parent nor child, so that only his siblings inherit him, surrounding him as a crown surrounds the head; hence he is called kalalah.

3- Disregarding a bequest or debt when it is known that its purpose is only to harm the heirs.

4- The great importance of inheritance shares, so it is obligatory to know them and to carry them out as Allah has enjoined.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 15–18:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Allati* (the ones who): plural of *allati*, a relative pronoun for the feminine singular; *allati* is the plural form for feminine plurals.

*Al-fahisha* (the immorality): what is meant here is fornication (*zina*).

*Min nisa'ikum* (from your women): the chaste women (*muhsanat*).

*Sabilan* (a way): a path out of the prison of the houses.

*Ya'tiyanaha* (they commit it): the pronoun refers back to *al-fahisha* mentioned earlier.

*Fa-a'ridu 'anhuma* (then turn away from them): leave off harming them after their repentance has become evident.

*Al-tawba* (repentance): the root meaning of *tawba* is return; its reality is regret for committing an ugly act together with abandoning it and resolving never to return to it.

*Al-su'* (evil): everything that harms the self; what is meant here is evil deeds.

*Bi-jahala* (out of ignorance): not with deliberate intent, persistence, and indifference.

*I'tadna* (We have prepared): We have readied and made ready.

*Alimán* (painful): causing intense pain.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When God, exalted is He, mentioned His limits and the penalty for transgressing them, He here mentioned one of His acts of disobedience, which is the immorality of fornication, and set a limit for it: confinement in the houses until death, or until He reveals another ruling that releases them from confinement. This applies to the chaste women. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who commit immorality among your women, bring against them four witnesses from among you﴾, meaning from among the Muslims, who testify that so-and-so has committed fornication with so-and-so. ﴿Then confine them to the houses until death takes them or God makes for them a way.﴾ As for the unmarried women, who are the virgins, God, exalted is He, said concerning them: ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them﴾, meaning with light beating, rebuke and reproach, along with confinement for the women. As for the men, they are not confined; rather, it is sufficient to harm them until they repent and reform. At that point they are pardoned and the harm against them ceases. This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them. And if they repent and reform, leave them alone. Indeed, God is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.﴾

Not much time passed after these two prescriptions before the Merciful fulfilled what He had promised and made for them a way. It is authentically related that the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting among his companions when God revealed to him the final ruling on the crime of fornication. He (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me. God has made a way for them: the previously married (*thayyib*) with the previously married: a hundred lashes and stoning with stones; and the virgin with the virgin: a hundred lashes and exile for a year." What is meant by "the previously married with the previously married" is that if a previously married person commits fornication with a previously married person, and likewise a virgin with a virgin. By this, the first limit concerning women and men together was lifted, and the second remained in force. As for the flogging of the two virgins, it was prescribed in the verse of Surat al-Nur: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer—flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ [Verse: 2]. As for the stoning of the married, the Sunnah had already established it, for Ma'iz and al-Ghamidiyya were stoned by the command of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and it is a limit that stands until the Day of Resurrection. This is what the first two verses, [15] and [16], indicate.

As for the two verses after them, [17] and [18], God, exalted is He, informed that those who deserve repentance, and for whom repentance is established from God, are the sinners who commit disobedience out of ignorance, and then repent soon, not postponing repentance or delaying it. As for those who commit evil deeds knowingly and persistently, and do not repent immediately after falling into sin, no repentance is guaranteed for them. They may die without repentance, like those who do evil and do not repent until one of them falls ill, sees the signs of death, and becomes certain that he is about to die, then says, "I repent now," as the disbelievers do when they repent at the moment of witnessing death; their repentance is never accepted.

This is the meaning of the two noble verses. The first: ﴿Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom God turns in forgiveness﴾, meaning He accepts their repentance, because He knows the weakness of His servants, and He is Wise, placing everything in its fitting place. Among that is the acceptance of the repentance of those who disobeyed Him out of ignorance, not out of obstinacy, arrogance, and defiance, and who then repented soon, not prolonging the period of their sins. The second: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾. Likewise, it is not for those who persist in disbelief: when death comes to one of them, he says, "I have repented," like Pharaoh, for when he witnessed drowning he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims." God replied to him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus: 91]. And His words, ﴿For those We have prepared a painful punishment﴾ refer to everyone who dies without repentance, having committed major sins, or having died in disbelief and polytheism. However, the believing monotheist will leave the Fire through his faith, while the disbeliever will remain in it forever. We seek refuge in God from the Fire and from the state of its people.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1- The great ugliness of the sin of fornication.

2- Explanation of the penalty for fornication before its abrogation by the verse of Surat al-Nur, and the ruling of the Messenger (ﷺ) on stoning the married man and woman.

3- The repentance that God bestows is for one who committed sins out of ignorance, not out of knowledge and persistence, and then repented within a short time.

4- Those who postpone repentance and delay it are feared to die before repenting while still in that state, and so they will be among the people of the Fire. One of them may repent, but this is rare and uncommon, and his repentance is accepted if he has not witnessed the signs of death, based on the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Indeed God accepts the repentance of a servant as long as he has not reached the death rattle." Related by al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others, and its chain is good (*hasan*).

5- The repentance of one whose soul has rattled in his throat and whose signs of death have appeared is not accepted; likewise the disbeliever, a fortiori, has no repentance accepted by faith once he witnesses the signs of death, just as the repentance of Pharaoh was not accepted.

Likewise, it is not for those who persist in disbelief: when death comes to one of them, he says, "I have repented," like Pharaoh, for when he witnessed drowning he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims." God replied to him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus: 91]. And His words, ﴿For those We have prepared a painful punishment﴾ refer to everyone who dies without repentance, having committed major sins, or having died in disbelief and polytheism. However, the believing monotheist will leave the Fire through his faith, while the disbeliever will remain in it forever. We seek refuge in God from the Fire and from the state of its people.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1- The great ugliness of the sin of fornication.

2- Explanation of the penalty for fornication before its abrogation by the verse of Surat al-Nur, and the ruling of the Messenger (ﷺ) on stoning the married man and woman.

3- The repentance that God bestows is for one who committed sins out of ignorance, not out of knowledge and persistence, and then repented within a short time.

4- Those who postpone repentance and delay it are feared to die before repenting while still in that state, and so they will be among the people of the Fire. One of them may repent, but this is rare and uncommon, and his repentance is accepted if he has not witnessed the signs of death, based on the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Indeed God accepts the repentance of a servant as long as he has not reached the death rattle." Related by al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others, and its chain is good (*hasan*).

5- The repentance of one whose soul has rattled in his throat and whose signs of death have appeared is not accepted; likewise the disbeliever, a fortiori, has no repentance accepted by faith once he witnesses the signs of death, just as the repentance of Pharaoh was not accepted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 19–21:

Explanation of the words:

Karhan (كرها): without their consent.

Al-ʿadl (العضل): restraining harshly, as if holding by the muscles (ʿadal) or from the muscles.

Bi-baʿḍi mā ātaytumūhunna (ببعض ما آتيتموهن): i.e., from the dowries.

Al-fāḥisha (الفاحشة): an ugly trait, severely ugly, such as adultery (zina).

Mubayyina (مبيّنة): manifest and clear, not merely an accusation or a slander.

Al-maʿrūf (المعروف): what the Shariʿa has recognized as obligatory, recommended, or permissible.

Qinṭāran (قنطارا): i.e., a quantity of gold or silver as a dowry (mahr) and bridal gift (ṣadāq).

Buhtānan wa-ithman (بهتانا وإثما): i.e., lying and fabrication, and a sin (ithm) whose prohibition is beyond doubt, because it is injustice.

Afḍā baʿḍukum ilā baʿḍ (أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض): i.e., one spouse has reached the private parts (ʿawra) of the other, and the wife likewise.

Mīthāqan ghalīẓ (ميثاقا غليظ): this is the contract, and the husband's statement: "Retain her with kindness or release her with goodness."

Meaning of the verses:

This verse contains: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾, which abolishes what was common among people before Islam of the injustice inflicted on women. A man, when his father died, would inherit the wife (of his father) from the eldest of his sons by another wife; if he wished, he would marry her and take her dowry, and if he wished, he would keep her until she gave him whatever property he demanded from her. So God Almighty revealed His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾, and thus that pre-Islamic ruling was nullified by this noble verse, and a woman whose husband died would observe her waiting period (ʿidda) in her husband's house; when her waiting period ended she would go wherever she wished, and she would have her own property and what she inherited from her husband as well. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not restrain them in order to take back part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. This is another ruling: it is forbidden for a husband, when he dislikes his wife, to harass and harm her until she ransoms herself from him with part of her dowry, since among the meanings of ʿadl is harassment and harm. This applies unless the wife commits the fornication of adultery, or rises above her husband, rebels against him, and diminishes his right to obedience and to fair companionship. But if she commits a manifest immorality with no doubt about it, or she shows clear rebellion (nushūz), then the husband may harass her until she ransoms herself from him with her dowry or more, until he divorces her. This is due to His saying: ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. Then God Almighty commanded His believing servants to live with their wives in accordance with what is right (maʿrūf), which is justice and kindness, saying: ﴿And live with them in kindness﴾. If it were supposed that one of you disliked his wife while she had not committed a clear immorality, then let him be patient with her and not divorce her, for perhaps God will place in her remaining in his marriage much good for him, as a result of his patience with her and his fear of God regarding her and others. He may be granted a child from her who benefits him, and that dislike may leave his soul and love and affection take its place. The meaning is that God Almighty guided the believer: if he dislikes his wife, he should be patient and not divorce, because of the good outcome in that, since divorce without a cause is neither proper nor pleasing to the Lawgiver. How many a matter a servant dislikes and yet is patient with, and God places much good in it. This is what the first verse [19] contains.

As for the two verses after it, they contain: the prohibition of taking anything from a woman's dowry when the husband divorces her, not because she committed immorality nor because of her rebellion, but out of his desire to divorce her in order to marry another. In this case it is not lawful for him to harm her so that she ransoms herself from him with anything, even a little; and even if he had given her a qinṭār, it is not lawful for him to take from it a single fils, let alone a dinar or a dirham. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But if you desire to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a qinṭār, do not take back from it anything﴾. ﴿Would you take it in slander and as a clear sin?﴾ — i.e., by injustice without right, and by lying, fabrication, and a manifest sin, i.e., a great wrong. Then God said, rebuking those who do this: ﴿And how could you take it, while you have gone in to one another?﴾ — i.e., by intercourse, since the husband had only made lawful her private part by that dowry; so how could he then reclaim it or any part of it by slander and manifest sin? God said: ﴿And how could you take it, while you have gone in to one another?﴾. And His saying: ﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant (mīthāqan ghalīẓan)﴾, meaning the marriage contract, which is a firm covenant. The husband says: "I have married her on the principle: retain her with kindness or release her with goodness." Where, then, is release with goodness, if he harasses her until she yields to him part or all of her dowry? This is what He disapproved of by His saying: "And how could you take it?", for it is a rhetorical question of denial.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The abolition of the Jahiliyya law by which a husband's son inherits his father's wife.

2- The prohibition of restraining a wife in order to extract a ransom with the dowry or otherwise.

3- Encouragement to patience.

4- The permissibility of taking a ransom from the wife with the dowry or more or less, if she commits a manifest immorality with no doubt about it, such as adultery or rebellion.

5- The permissibility of a high dowry, even reaching a qinṭār, though ease in it is more blessed.

6- The obligation to observe covenants and fulfil them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 22–23:

Explanation of the words:

"And do not marry those whom your fathers married": do not marry the wife of a father or a grandfather.

"Except what has already passed": except what occurred before this prohibition.

"Indeed, it was an indecency": that is, marrying the wives of one's fathers is a grave indecency.

"Hatred": detested and abhorred by the Lawgiver and by everyone of sound nature.

"And evil is the way": that is, the marrying of fathers' wives is an evil path to take.

"Your mothers" (ummahatukum): the plural of umm (mother). The mother is forbidden, and likewise the grandmother, however far up she is.

"And your daughters' daughters" (rabaibukum): the rabaib is the plural of rabiba, who is the daughter of one's wife.

"And the wives of your sons" (halail abna'ikum): the halail is the plural of halila, who is the wife of a son by birth (from the loins).

The meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues to explain the legal rulings related to inheritance, marriage, and the treatment of women. In these two verses Allah the Exalted mentions the persons forbidden for marriage by lineage, by nursing, and by marital affinity. He begins with the prohibition of the wife of a father, however far up he is, saying: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married﴾. He did not say "whom," so that the prohibition would include the wife of the father and the custom that was followed among them in the Jahiliyyah. Therefore He said "except what has already passed" in the Jahiliyyah, for it is pardoned in Islam after one abandons it and does not remain in it. By this wording, the wife of a father and of a grandfather is forbidden to the son and the grandson, even if the father did not have intercourse with her. Then He mentioned the prohibitions by lineage, so He mentioned mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brothers' daughters, and sisters' daughters. These are seven persons forbidden by lineage. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brothers' daughters, and your sisters' daughters﴾. Then He mentioned the prohibitions by nursing, saying: ﴿And your mothers who nursed you, and your milk-sisters﴾. Whoever nursed from a woman five feedings while he was within the age of two years, she becomes forbidden to him, and her mothers, her daughters, and her sisters become forbidden to him; likewise the daughters of her husband, his sisters, and his mothers. Some have said that what is forbidden by nursing is what is forbidden by lineage. Then Allah the Exalted mentioned the prohibitions by marital affinity, saying: ﴿And the mothers of your wives﴾. The mother of a man's wife is forbidden to him merely by his contracting marriage with her daughter; the mother becomes forbidden. He also said: ﴿And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship﴾. The stepdaughter is the daughter of the wife: when a man marries a woman and consummates the marriage, it is not lawful for him to marry her daughter. But if he has only contracted the marriage and not consummated it, then the daughter is lawful to him, because of His saying: ﴿of your women with whom you have consummated marriage; but if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you﴾, that is, no sin and no fault.

Among the prohibitions by marital affinity is the wife of a son, whether or not he consummated the marriage with her, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, meaning not an adopted son. As for a son through nursing, his wife is like the wife of a son by birth, because the milk by which he was nourished is the cause, so he is like a child of the loins. Also among the prohibitions by marital affinity is the sister of one's wife: whoever marries a woman, it is not lawful for him to marry her sister until she dies or he divorces her and her waiting period ends, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and that you combine two sisters﴾, except what has already passed in the Jahiliyyah, for it is pardoned on condition that one does not remain in it.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of the marriage customs of the Jahiliyyah, except those that agree with Islam, and especially the wives of fathers: the wife of a father is forbidden to the son, even if the father did not consummate the marriage with her and divorced her or died leaving her.

2- The explanation of those forbidden by lineage, who are seven: mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brothers' daughters, and sisters' daughters.

3- The explanation of those forbidden by nursing, who are the same as those forbidden by lineage: the nursling is forbidden to marry his nursing mother and her daughters, her sisters, her paternal and maternal aunts, and the daughters of his brother and the daughters of his sister.

4- The explanation of those forbidden by marital affinity, who are also seven: the wife of a father, whether or not he consummated the marriage; the mother of one's wife, whether or not the marriage was consummated with her daughter; the stepdaughter, when one has consummated the marriage with her mother; the wife of a son by birth, whether or not the son consummated the marriage; likewise the wife of a son through nursing; and the sister of one's wife, as long as her sister is under him and he has not separated from her by divorce or death. And "the married women" (al-muhsanat) among women, that is, those who were married before their divorce or the death of their husbands and the completion of their waiting period.

As for a son through nursing, his wife is like the wife of a son by birth, because the milk by which he was nourished is the cause, so he is like a child of the loins. Also among the prohibitions by marital affinity is the sister of one's wife: whoever marries a woman, it is not lawful for him to marry her sister until she dies or he divorces her and her waiting period ends, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and that you combine two sisters﴾, except what has already passed in the Jahiliyyah, for it is pardoned on condition that one does not remain in it.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of the marriage customs of the Jahiliyyah, except those that agree with Islam, and especially the wives of fathers: the wife of a father is forbidden to the son, even if the father did not consummate the marriage with her and divorced her or died leaving her.

2- The explanation of those forbidden by lineage, who are seven: mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brothers' daughters, and sisters' daughters.

3- The explanation of those forbidden by nursing, who are the same as those forbidden by lineage: the nursling is forbidden to marry his nursing mother and her daughters, her sisters, her paternal and maternal aunts, and the daughters of his brother and the daughters of his sister.

4- The explanation of those forbidden by marital affinity, who are also seven: the wife of a father, whether or not he consummated the marriage; the mother of one's wife, whether or not the marriage was consummated with her daughter; the stepdaughter, when one has consummated the marriage with her mother; the wife of a son by birth, whether or not the son consummated the marriage; likewise the wife of a son through nursing; and the sister of one's wife, as long as her sister is under him and he has not separated from her by divorce or death. And "the married women" (al-muhsanat) among women, that is, those who were married before their divorce or the death of their husbands and the completion of their waiting period.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 24–25:

Explanation of the words:

al-Muhsanat (المحصنات): the plural of muhsanah, here meaning married women.

Illa ma malakat aymanukum (إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم): women owned through captivity (sabi), purchase, or similar means.

Ma wara'a dhalikum (ما وراء ذلكم): that is, beyond these, i.e., beyond what has been forbidden to you.

Ghayra musafihin (غير مسافحين): al-musafih is the fornicator (al-zani), for al-sifah is zina (fornication).

Ajurahunna fariḍah (أجورهن فريضة): their dowries (mahr) as an obligatory gift (nihlah).

Tawlan (طولاً): ample means and ability to pay the dowry.

Al-muhsanat: the chaste women (al-'afifat).

Ajurahunna: their dowries (mahr).

Wa la muttakhidhat akhdan (ولا متخذات أخدان): al-khadin is the close friend who commits illicit intercourse with a woman secretly under the guise of friendship.

Fa idha uhsinna (فإذا أحصن): by becoming Muslim or by marriage, for ihsan occurs through either of them.

Al-'anat (العنت): al-'anat is harm to one's religion and body.

The meaning of the two verses:

The context continues to explain what is forbidden in marriage and what is permitted. In the first verse [24], after listing the prohibited women by affinity, the Exalted turns to married women, saying ﴿And [prohibited are] the married women﴾, i.e., those who have husbands, so it is not lawful to marry them except after separation from the husband by divorce or death, and also after the completion of the waiting period (iddah). The Exalted also made an exception among married women for those owned by right hand, who are women taken captive in lawful war, i.e., jihad in the way of Allah. It is possible that her husband did not die in the war, and since her connection has been severed from the abode of war, from her husband and her people, and she has become a slave, Allah the Exalted, out of mercy toward her, permitted her marriage to whoever among the believers owns her.

For this reason it is reported that the verse was revealed concerning the captives of Awtas, an engagement that took place after the battle of Hunayn, in which the Muslims took captive women and children. The believers were scrupulous about approaching those women, among whom were married women, so they were permitted to approach them after one of them had embraced Islam and had been cleansed by one menstrual cycle (istibra'). Before her Islam, she is not lawful, because she is a polytheist. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And [prohibited are] the married women among the women, except those whom your right hands possess﴾, and His words: ﴿the decree of Allah upon you﴾ mean that what Allah has forbidden of marriages He has prescribed for the Muslims as a binding writ and an obligation that may not be neglected or taken lightly. Kitaba Allah is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar).

As for His words: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾, i.e., what lies beyond those forbidden by blood relation, by nursing, and by affinity, on the condition that a man does not exceed four wives, as is evident from His words at the beginning of the surah: ﴿two, three, or four﴾ [al-Nisa: 3]. And His words: ﴿that you seek [them] with your wealth, as chaste men, not as fornicators﴾ mean: there is no blame upon you in seeking with your wealth women other than those forbidden to you, so that you marry whatever is good for you while being chaste and not fornicating. This is accomplished when the marriage is completed with its conditions: the guardian (wali), the dowry (sadaq), the formula (sighah), and the witnesses, for a marriage conducted without these conditions is fornication, i.e., zina. And His words: ﴿So for what you have enjoyed of them, give them their dowries as an obligation﴾ mean: whoever marries a woman and consummates with her, i.e., has intercourse with her, the full dowry becomes due to her. As for one with whom the enjoyment was not completed, by divorcing her before consummation, she has only half of the stated dowry; if no dowry was stated for her, she has only the provision (mut'ah). Thus the meaning of His words ﴿for what you have enjoyed of them﴾ is: you have consummated with them and entered upon them.

And His words: ﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾ mean: if a man has given his wife what makes her private part lawful to him, namely the full dowry, then there is no blame on either of them thereafter if the woman remits some of her dowry to her husband, or defers it, or gives him all of it or part of it, since it is then hers and she is its owner, as previously mentioned: ﴿And if they willingly give you something of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾ [al-Nisa: 4].

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ are meant to make the believers understand that Allah the Exalted is aware of their circumstances and wise in His legislation for them, so let them adhere to His law, its concessions, and its firm obligations, for it is founded upon mercy and justice, and what an excellent legislation that is which stands on the basis of mercy and justice.

This is what the first verse [24] contains. As for the second verse, His words: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women...﴾, it contains a demonstration of Allah's mercy toward His believing servants, for He granted a concession to one who cannot marry free women due to lack of means, while fearing al-'anat, which is harm to his religion through fornication, or harm to his body through the execution of the hadd punishment upon him: he is permitted to marry a slave woman on condition that she be a believer, that he marry her with the permission of her owner, that he give her her dowry, and that this be done on the basis of ihsan, which is marriage with its conditions and not fornication, which is open zina, indicated by the phrase ﴿not fornicating﴾, nor secret illicit relations, indicated by the phrase ﴿nor taking secret lovers﴾, i.e., close friends. This is the meaning of His words ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women﴾, i.e., financial ability to marry the chaste women, i.e., the virtuous ones, of ﴿your believing slave girls﴾, i.e., of your believing female slaves, not disbelieving ones, outwardly; as for the inward, its knowledge belongs to Allah, and therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your faith﴾. His words ﴿some of you are from others﴾ contain consolation for the believer who marries a slave woman out of necessity, for faith removes the distinctions among believers. His words: ﴿So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their dowries according to what is reasonable, [as] chaste, not fornicating, nor taking lovers﴾ contain a statement of the conditions that are indispensable, which we have mentioned above.

His words: ﴿And when they become chaste﴾, i.e., the slave women, by marriage and by Islam, ﴿and if they commit a flagrant act﴾, i.e., commit zina, then upon them is a punishment that is half of what is upon free married women, which is fifty lashes and exile for six months, because if a free woman commits zina while a virgin, she is flogged a hundred lashes and exiled for a year. As for stoning, which is death, it cannot be halved, so the believers understood from the halving of the punishment that it is flogging and not stoning, and this is a consensus without any disagreement. His words: ﴿That is for one who fears al-'anat among you﴾ mean: I have permitted this to you for one who fears for himself zina, when he is unable to marry a free woman due to his poverty and need. His words: ﴿And that you be patient...﴾, i.e., patience in celibacy, is better for you than marrying slave women. His words ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ mean: Forgiving to those who repent, Merciful to the believers, and for this reason He granted them a concession to marry slave women when fearing al-'anat, and guided them to what is better than it, which is patience. So to Allah belongs all praise, and to Him belongs the favor.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of a married woman until her husband separates from her by divorce or death, and until her waiting period is completed.

2- The permissibility of marrying a woman owned by right hand, even if her husband is alive in the abode of war, when she embraces Islam, because Islam separates them.

3- The obligation of dowries, and the permissibility of a woman giving her husband part of her dowry.

4- The permissibility of marrying slave women for one who fears al-'anat and lacks the ability to marry free women.

5- The obligation of enforcing the hadd punishment upon a slave woman who commits zina if she becomes chaste through marriage and Islam.

6- Patience in celibacy is better than marrying slave women, as Allah guides to this.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 4, Verses 26–28**

**Explanation of the words:**

*﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾*: God desires to make clear to you, through what He has forbidden and permitted to you, what will perfect you and make you happy in your worldly life and your Hereafter.

*Sunan (ways) of those before you*: the paths of those before you, among the prophets and the righteous, so that you may follow their way, be purified, perfected, and succeed as they did.

*﴿And turn to you in forgiveness﴾*: He returns you from the misguidance of the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) to the guidance of Islam.

*﴿Those who follow their desires﴾*: from among the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and the fornicators.

*﴿That you deviate with a tremendous deviation﴾*: that you turn aside from the path of purity and clarity to the path of corruption and turbidity, by committing the prohibited acts of marriage and others, so that you stray far from righteous guidance.

*﴿And man was created weak﴾*: he cannot refrain from women, so God has granted them leave to marry believing young women.

**The meaning of the verses:**

When God forbade what He forbade of marriages and permitted what He permitted, He gave the reason for that by His words ﴿Allah desires﴾, meaning: by what He has legislated, He makes clear what benefits you and what harms you, so that you take the beneficial and leave the harmful. Just as He desires to guide you to the ways of the righteous who came before you, prophets and believing righteous people, so that you may walk in them and be perfected and happy in both lives, He also desires, by what He has made clear to you, ﴿to turn to you in forgiveness﴾, meaning He returns you from the misguidance of the jahiliyyah to the guidance of Islam, so that you live in purity and righteousness. He, exalted is He, knows what benefits and harms you and is wise in His management of you, so thank Him by adhering to His obedience and keeping away from His disobedience.

This is what the first verse [26] contains. As for the second verse [27], it contains the information that God, by what He has explained of the lawful and unlawful in marriage and other matters, desires to bring the believers out of the life of corruption and wrongdoing they lived before Islam into a life of purity and righteousness under a just and merciful legislation. And those who follow their desires, from among the fornicators, the Jews, the Christians, and the rest of those who deviate from the ways of guidance, desire that the believers deviate as they do, so that they immerse themselves in pleasures and bestial appetites until they become like them, with no superiority over them. At that point they have no right to lead or guide them.

This is the meaning of the second verse. As for the third [28], God has informed us that by permitting believers who are unable to marry free women to marry believing young women, He desires thereby to lighten and ease matters for the believers, out of mercy and compassion for them, because He knows the weakness of man and his inability to refrain from women, owing to the inclination toward the female that He has placed in him for the preservation of the species and for lofty wisdoms. God said: ﴿God desires to lighten your burden, and man was created weak﴾.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The favour of God upon us in giving the reasons for the rulings, so that our souls are reassured and we act with an open heart and a willing spirit.

2. The favour of God upon the believers in guiding them to the ways of the righteous and the path of the successful who came before them.

3. The favour of God in purifying the believers from impurities and the misguidance of the jahiliyyahs.

4. The revelation of the human soul: fornicators desire that all people be fornicators, and deviants wish that people deviate as they do. Likewise, everyone immersed in wickedness, evil, or corruption wishes that all people were like him, just as the pure and righteous person wishes to purify and reform all people.

5. The weakness of man before his instincts, especially the sexual instinct.

As for the third [28], God has informed us that by permitting believers who are unable to marry free women to marry believing young women, He desires thereby to lighten and ease matters for the believers, out of mercy and compassion for them, because He knows the weakness of man and his inability to refrain from women, owing to the inclination toward the female that He has placed in him for the preservation of the species and for lofty wisdoms. God said: ﴿God desires to lighten your burden, and man was created weak﴾.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The favour of God upon us in giving the reasons for the rulings, so that our souls are reassured and we act with an open heart and a willing spirit.

2. The favour of God upon the believers in guiding them to the ways of the righteous and the path of the successful who came before them.

3. The favour of God in purifying the believers from impurities and the misguidance of the jahiliyyahs.

4. The revelation of the human soul: fornicators desire that all people be fornicators, and deviants wish that people deviate as they do. Likewise, everyone immersed in wickedness, evil, or corruption wishes that all people were like him, just as the pure and righteous person wishes to purify and reform all people.

5. The weakness of man before his instincts, especially the sexual instinct.

**Explanation of the Words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Amanu* (آمنوا): they affirmed (sadaqu) Allah and the Messenger.

*Bil-batil* (بالباطل): without a right that makes it permissible to consume it.

*Tijara* (تجارة): trade, buying and selling, so that the owner of the goods may take the money and the owner of the money may take the goods; thus there is no falsehood (batil).

*Taqtulu anfusakum* (تقتلوا أنفسكم): that is, you take each other's lives.

*Udwanan wa zulman* (عدواناً وظلماً): transgression in which one is a wrongdoer.

*Nuslihi naran* (نصليه ناراً): We will cause him to enter the Fire of Hell, where he will be burned.

**The Meaning of the Two Verses (Ma'na al-Ayatayn):**

The context continues to explain what is lawful and unlawful regarding wealth, honour and lives. In this verse [29], Allah, exalted is He, addresses His believing servants by the title of faith, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and forbids them from consuming their wealth among themselves in falsehood, through theft, deceit, gambling, usury, and the other numerous forms of prohibition, saying: ﴿Do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, meaning without a permissible exchange or the goodwill of the owner. Then He makes an exception for what is obtained through trade founded on the principle of mutual consent between the two parties to the sale, based on the hadith, "Sale is only by mutual consent" and "The two parties to a sale have the option (of cancelling) as long as they have not parted," so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿except that it be a trade by mutual consent among you﴾. There is then no harm in consuming it, for it is lawful for you. This is what this verse contains. It also contains the prohibition of the believers killing one another, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾. The prohibition includes a person killing himself and killing his Muslim brother, because the Muslims are like one body; whoever kills a Muslim among them is as if he had killed himself. Allah, exalted is He, gave us the reason for this prohibition, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, and therefore He has forbidden you to kill one another.

This is what the first verse [29] contains. As for the second verse [30], it contains a severe warning of being burned in the Fire and roasted therein for everyone who kills a believer with transgression and wrongdoing, that is, deliberately, persistently, and in pure injustice. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, that is, the killing, ﴿in transgression and wrongdoing – We will drive him into a Fire﴾, and that roasting and burning in the Fire ﴿is ever, for Allah, easy﴾, because of His perfect power, exalted is He. The one threatened with this punishment cannot, under any circumstances, avert it from himself.

1. The sanctity of the Muslim's property, and that any unlawfully acquired property is forbidden, whether it is obtained by theft, deceit, gambling, or usury.

2. The permissibility of trade, its encouragement, and the refutation of the ignorant Sufis who forbid earning a living on the pretext of reliance upon Allah (tawakkul).

3. Establishing the principle: "Sale is only by mutual consent, and the two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not parted."

4. The prohibition of a Muslim killing himself or other Muslims, because they are one community.

5. The severe warning against one who kills a soul with transgression and wrongdoing, by being burned in the Fire.

6. If the killing is not transgression, as when it is accidental, or is not wrongdoing, as when it is deliberate but rightful, such as killing one who killed his father, son or brother, then this severe warning does not apply.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 31:

Explanation of the words:

"An tajtanibu" (if you avoid): tabtaʿidu (you keep far away), because ijtinab (avoidance) is leaving a thing aside, far from it, not approaching it or drawing near to it.

"Kaba'ira ma tunhawna ʿanhu" (the major sins that you are forbidden): al-kaba'ir (the major sins) are the opposite of al-saghair (the minor sins). The greatness of a sin is known by its prescribed limit (hadd) and not by counting. A major sin is therefore whatever Allah and His Messenger have threatened for, or whose doer they have cursed, or for which a legal penalty (hadd) has been prescribed to be carried out upon the one who commits it. Authentic hadith have mentioned many major sins, and it is incumbent upon the believer to know them in order to avoid them.

"Nukaffir" (We will remove): nughattii (we cover) and nastur (we conceal), so that they are not called to account for and we do not hold them accountable for them.

"Mudkhalan kariman" (a noble entrance): the noble entrance here is Paradise, the abode of the God-fearing.

Meaning of the noble verse:

The Almighty, may His majesty be exalted, bestows His favour, and His bounty and sovereignty are great, upon the believers of this Muslim community. He has promised them a true promise that whoever among them avoids the major sins, He will remove their minor sins from them, admit them into Paradise, the abode of peace, and clothe them in garments of good pleasure. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden﴾, that which I and My Messenger forbid you. ﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, which are less than the major sins, namely the minor sins, ﴿and admit you to a noble entrance﴾, which is Paradise. To Allah belongs all praise and grace. For this reason this verse is among the glad tidings of the Qur'an for this community.

Guidance from the verse:

Among the guidance of the verse:

1- The obligation to keep far from all major sins, and to be patient in that until death.

2- Sins are of two kinds, major and minor. Therefore it is obligatory to know them, in order to avoid their major and minor forms as far as possible. Whoever slips should repent, for the one who repents from a sin is as one who has no sin.

3- Paradise is entered only by those of purified and pure souls, through their avoidance of the defilements of major sins, transgressions, and grave immoralities.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 4, verses 32–33:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-la tatamannaw (And do not wish for): al-tamanni (wishing) is longing and desire for the attainment of a thing, and its particles are "layta" (would that) and "law" (if only). If the desire is that the thing wished for be removed from a person so that it comes to the one wishing, then it is envy (hasad).

Ma faddala Allahu bihi ba'dakum (what Allah has favoured some of you with): that is, what Allah has favoured any one of you with, giving him knowledge, wealth, status or authority.

Naseebun mimma iktasabu (a share of what they have earned): that is, a portion and a lot of reward and punishment according to obedience and disobedience.

Mawali (heirs/kinsmen): the mawali are those who take charge of the estate and inherit from the deceased among relatives.

Aqadat aymanukum (your oaths have bound): that is, you have sworn allegiance to them and become brothers with them, confirming this by handshake and oath.

Fa-atoohum naseebahum (then give them their share): of support, bequest and help, since they are not heirs.

The meaning of the two verses:

Whether or not it is authentically reported that Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight and have a reward like the reward of men," then Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. And those who wish, out of envy and otherwise, how many of them there are. From here, Allah the Exalted in this noble verse [32] forbade His believing servants from wishing for what Allah the Exalted has favoured some of them with over others, giving this one and withholding from that one for wisdoms that required it, and among the most evident of them is the trial of gratitude and patience. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has favoured some of you over others﴾ — of knowledge, wealth, health, status or authority. And He informed that His way in reward and punishment is acquisition and action. So whoever wants the reward and recompense should act by what necessitates that, of faith and righteous deeds, and should not merely wish for it; and whoever fears punishment and deprivation should refrain from shirk and sins, and should not merely wish for salvation. Likewise, whoever wants wealth and status should work for it by its established means and not merely wish, for wishing, as it is said, is the merchandise of the foolish (al-nawka), i.e., the fools. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned﴾, returning the matter to His way concerning it, which is human acquisition. Like His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Al-Zalzalah: 7–8]. Then Allah the Exalted explained another way of attaining what is desired, which is supplicating to Allah the Exalted, so He said: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾. Whoever asks his Lord and persists in asking, certain of being answered, will be given; He will enable him to take the means, will turn away obstacles from him, and will give him without cause if He wills, for He is over all things capable. Indeed, among the legislated means is supplication and sincerity in it.

This is what the first verse contains. As for the second verse [33], Allah the Exalted informs, affirming a legal ruling already mentioned in the context, namely that both men and women have heirs who inherit from them when they die. So He said: ﴿And for every one We have appointed heirs (mawali)﴾, that is, relatives who inherit from him when he dies, whether they are men or women. As for those who are mawali only by oath or brotherhood, that is, they are not of those related by blood (ulu al-arham), then it is obligatory to give them their share of support and help.

And a bequest to them of something, since they have no portion in inheritance, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another﴾ [Al-Anfal: 75]. And since the distribution and division of wealth is something souls yearn for, and injustice or wrong may occur in it, Allah the Exalted informed that over all things He is Witness, so nothing of the affairs of people is hidden from Him; therefore let them fear Him and not disobey.

So He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him; so fear Him, obey Him, and do not disobey Him.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The ugliness of wishing and abandoning action.

2- The prohibition of envy.

3- The virtue of supplication, and that it is among the means by which the desired is attained.

4- Affirmation of the principle of inheritance in Islam.

5- Whoever has made a covenant with someone by oath or made someone a brother must give him the right of support and assistance, and he may bequeath to him up to less than one-third; as for inheritance, he has no right to it, because that ruling has been abrogated (naskh).

6- The obligation of being mindful of Allah the Exalted, since He is All-Knowing of everything and Witness over everything.
