Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 34–35:

Explanation of the words:

Qawwamun (قوامون): plural of qawwam, meaning one who stands over a thing with care, protection and reform.

Bima faddala Allahu ba'dahum (بما فضل الله بعضهم): namely, that Allah made the man more complete in his intellect, his religion and his body, so that he is fit for qawwama (guardianship).

Wa bima anfaqu min amwalihim (وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم): this is another factor by which qawwama (guardianship) over women is established for men, for the man, by giving the dowry (mahr) and by bearing the maintenance (nafaqah) of the woman, has more right to qawwama, which is leadership.

As-salihat (الصالحات): plural of salihah, meaning she who fulfils the rights of Allah the Exalted and the rights of her husband.

Qanitat (قانتات): obedient to Allah and to their husbands.

Hafizat lil-ghayb (حافظات للغيب): guarding their private parts (furuj) and their husbands' property.

Nushuzahunna (نشوزهن): nushuz means rising above the husband and not obeying him.

Fa'izuhunna (فعظوهن): by encouraging obedience and warning against disobedience.

Fa la tabghu 'alayhinna sabilan (فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلاً): that is, do not seek a way by which you can reach striking them after they have obeyed you.

Shiqaq baynahuma (شقاق بينهما): shiqaq means dispute and enmity, to the point that each one stands on an opposing side.

Hakaman (حكماً): hakam means a judge; and the muhakkam is one who is appointed to consider and decide matters.

The meaning of the two verses:

It is related regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse that Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (may Allah be pleased with him) was angered by his wife, so he struck her. Her guardian complained about him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), seeking retaliation (qisas). So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has made one of them to excel the other, and because they spend from their wealth﴾. The guardian of the woman said: "We wanted one thing, and Allah wanted another, and what Allah wills is best." And he accepted the judgment of Allah the Exalted, which is that the man, so long as he is qawwam over the woman, cares for her, guides her and reforms her, by means of an intellect more complete than hers and a knowledge generally more abundant than hers, and he is more far-sighted than her in considering the beginnings and ends of matters. In addition to that, he has paid a dowry which she did not pay, and has undertaken expenses of which she has undertaken none. Therefore, when leadership over her became his due, and it is a lawful leadership, he had the right to strike her in a manner that does not disfigure a limb or break a bone, so that his striking of her is like the striking of a disciplinarian towards one he disciplines and trains. After establishing this authority of the husband over his wife, Allah the Exalted commanded the honouring of women, kindness towards them and gentleness with them because of their weakness, and He praised them, saying: ﴿So the righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾, and they are those who fulfil the rights of Allah the Exalted by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger (ﷺ), and the rights of their husbands of obedience, esteem and respect. ﴿Qanitat﴾: that is, obedient to Allah the Exalted and to the husband. ﴿Hafizat lil-ghayb﴾: that is, guarding the husband's property and honour, according to the hadith: "And when he is absent from her, she guards him in herself and in his property." ﴿Bima hafiza Allah﴾: that is, by Allah's guarding of them and His help to them, for if they were left to themselves they would be unable to guard anything, however little. Within the context of the speech there is an indication of an implied omission which is understood: that the praise of them by Allah the Exalted obliges the man to honour the righteous woman, to be kind to her and gentle with her because of her weakness. This is what I mentioned first, and I have drawn attention to it here so that it may be known that it is among the implications of this noble verse; and more than one of the early scholars (al-salaf) have mentioned it.

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz, admonish them, and abandon them in the beds, and strike them. Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them.﴾ He, the Exalted, guides husbands to the manner of treating a wife when she commits nushuz, that is, rises above her husband and does not render to him the rights that are due to him by virtue of the contract between them. So He says: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz﴾: that is, their rising, by signs and indications that have appeared to you, such as when he commands her and she does not obey, calls her and she does not answer, and forbids her and she does not desist. Then follow with them the following course: ﴿admonish them﴾ first. Admonition is reminding her of the right the husband has over her which must be fulfilled, and what follows from neglecting it of the wrath and punishment of Allah the Exalted, and what may result from her neglect in the form of his striking her or divorcing her. Admonition is encouragement with the reward of the righteous, obedient women, and warning against the punishment of the corrupt, disobedient women. If admonition benefits her, well and good; otherwise the second step is that the husband abandons her in the bed: he does not speak to her while he sleeps with her on one bed, and he turns his back to her, so he does not speak to her nor have intercourse with her, and he should be patient in this until she returns to obedience to him and to Allah their Lord together. If she persists and abandonment in the bed does not work with her, then the third step is that he strikes her with a striking that is not severe, which does not disfigure a limb or break a bone. Finally, if she obeys her husband, then it is no longer lawful for the husband thereafter to seek a way to harm her, neither by striking nor by abandonment, because of His saying: ﴿Then if they obey you﴾: that is, the husbands; ﴿do not seek﴾: that is, do not look for ﴿a way against them﴾ to harm them, by fabricating causes and inventing pretexts and justifications to harm them. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Exalted, Great﴾ is a conclusion to the speech that makes whoever wishes to rise above others by the power he has been given aware that Allah is higher than him and greater, so let him fear Allah and abandon his haughtiness and pride.

This is what these great verses contain [34]. As for the second verse [35], it contains another social ruling, namely that if a dispute (shiqaq) arises between a husband and his wife, so that the man is on one side and the woman on another side, with no meeting between them, no harmony, and no agreement, because of the difficulty of the situation: the path to resolving this problem is what Allah the Exalted has guided to, namely that the wife's guardian sends a judge (hakam) from his side, and the husband's guardian sends a judge from his side; or the husband himself sends a judge and the wife also sends a judge from her side; or the judge sends them; all of these are permissible, because of His saying: ﴿So send an arbiter﴾, addressing the Muslims, on condition that the arbiter be just, knowing and perceptive, so that he can judge with justice. The two arbiters first study the case with both parties to the dispute, and they become acquainted with the causes of the dispute and with what is in the hearts of the spouses of contentment and love, and of dislike and anger. Then they come together to reconcile them (islah dhat al-bayn). If that is possible, well and good; otherwise they separate them with the consent of the spouses. With the knowledge that, if injustice of one of them is established, both of them must demand the removal of the injustice: if the husband is the wrongdoer, then he must remove his injustice and discharge what is due upon him; and if the woman is the wrongdoer, then she must remove her injustice or ransom herself with money, by which her husband may grant her khul' (divorce). This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two of them﴾, and fear here means a firm expectation of what has appeared of signs and shown of indications, so that the situation is addressed before it becomes severely critical. ﴿Then send an arbiter from his people and an arbiter from her people﴾, because they are more knowledgeable of the state of the spouses than others. And His saying: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation﴾: this refers to the two arbiters; ﴿Allah will cause them to agree﴾: that is, if their intention is reform, and uniting the spouses, and removing the dispute and discord between them, then Allah the Exalted helps them in their task, blesses their endeavour, and crowns it with success.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 34–35:

Explanation of the words:

Qawwamun (قوامون): plural of qawwam, meaning one who stands over a thing with care, protection and reform.

Bima faddala Allahu ba'dahum (بما فضل الله بعضهم): namely, that Allah made the man more complete in his intellect, his religion and his body, so that he is fit for qawwama (guardianship).

Wa bima anfaqu min amwalihim (وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم): this is another factor by which qawwama (guardianship) over women is established for men, for the man, by giving the dowry (mahr) and by bearing the maintenance (nafaqah) of the woman, has more right to qawwama, which is leadership.

As-salihat (الصالحات): plural of salihah, meaning she who fulfils the rights of Allah the Exalted and the rights of her husband.

Qanitat (قانتات): obedient to Allah and to their husbands.

Hafizat lil-ghayb (حافظات للغيب): guarding their private parts (furuj) and their husbands' property.

Nushuzahunna (نشوزهن): nushuz means rising above the husband and not obeying him.

Fa'izuhunna (فعظوهن): by encouraging obedience and warning against disobedience.

Fa la tabghu 'alayhinna sabilan (فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلاً): that is, do not seek a way by which you can reach striking them after they have obeyed you.

Shiqaq baynahuma (شقاق بينهما): shiqaq means dispute and enmity, to the point that each one stands on an opposing side.

Hakaman (حكماً): hakam means a judge; and the muhakkam is one who is appointed to consider and decide matters.

The meaning of the two verses:

It is related regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse that Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (may Allah be pleased with him) was angered by his wife, so he struck her. Her guardian complained about him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), seeking retaliation (qisas). So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has made one of them to excel the other, and because they spend from their wealth﴾. The guardian of the woman said: "We wanted one thing, and Allah wanted another, and what Allah wills is best." And he accepted the judgment of Allah the Exalted, which is that the man, so long as he is qawwam over the woman, cares for her, guides her and reforms her, by means of an intellect more complete than hers and a knowledge generally more abundant than hers, and he is more far-sighted than her in considering the beginnings and ends of matters. In addition to that, he has paid a dowry which she did not pay, and has undertaken expenses of which she has undertaken none. Therefore, when leadership over her became his due, and it is a lawful leadership, he had the right to strike her in a manner that does not disfigure a limb or break a bone, so that his striking of her is like the striking of a disciplinarian towards one he disciplines and trains. After establishing this authority of the husband over his wife, Allah the Exalted commanded the honouring of women, kindness towards them and gentleness with them because of their weakness, and He praised them, saying: ﴿So the righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾, and they are those who fulfil the rights of Allah the Exalted by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger (ﷺ), and the rights of their husbands of obedience, esteem and respect. ﴿Qanitat﴾: that is, obedient to Allah the Exalted and to the husband. ﴿Hafizat lil-ghayb﴾: that is, guarding the husband's property and honour, according to the hadith: "And when he is absent from her, she guards him in herself and in his property." ﴿Bima hafiza Allah﴾: that is, by Allah's guarding of them and His help to them, for if they were left to themselves they would be unable to guard anything, however little. Within the context of the speech there is an indication of an implied omission which is understood: that the praise of them by Allah the Exalted obliges the man to honour the righteous woman, to be kind to her and gentle with her because of her weakness. This is what I mentioned first, and I have drawn attention to it here so that it may be known that it is among the implications of this noble verse; and more than one of the early scholars (al-salaf) have mentioned it.

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz, admonish them, and abandon them in the beds, and strike them. Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them.﴾ He, the Exalted, guides husbands to the manner of treating a wife when she commits nushuz, that is, rises above her husband and does not render to him the rights that are due to him by virtue of the contract between them. So He says: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz﴾: that is, their rising, by signs and indications that have appeared to you, such as when he commands her and she does not obey, calls her and she does not answer, and forbids her and she does not desist. Then follow with them the following course: ﴿admonish them﴾ first. Admonition is reminding her of the right the husband has over her which must be fulfilled, and what follows from neglecting it of the wrath and punishment of Allah the Exalted, and what may result from her neglect in the form of his striking her or divorcing her. Admonition is encouragement with the reward of the righteous, obedient women, and warning against the punishment of the corrupt, disobedient women. If admonition benefits her, well and good; otherwise the second step is that the husband abandons her in the bed: he does not speak to her while he sleeps with her on one bed, and he turns his back to her, so he does not speak to her nor have intercourse with her, and he should be patient in this until she returns to obedience to him and to Allah their Lord together. If she persists and abandonment in the bed does not work with her, then the third step is that he strikes her with a striking that is not severe, which does not disfigure a limb or break a bone. Finally, if she obeys her husband, then it is no longer lawful for the husband thereafter to seek a way to harm her, neither by striking nor by abandonment, because of His saying: ﴿Then if they obey you﴾: that is, the husbands; ﴿do not seek﴾: that is, do not look for ﴿a way against them﴾ to harm them, by fabricating causes and inventing pretexts and justifications to harm them. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Exalted, Great﴾ is a conclusion to the speech that makes whoever wishes to rise above others by the power he has been given aware that Allah is higher than him and greater, so let him fear Allah and abandon his haughtiness and pride.

This is what these great verses contain [34]. As for the second verse [35], it contains another social ruling, namely that if a dispute (shiqaq) arises between a husband and his wife, so that the man is on one side and the woman on another side, with no meeting between them, no harmony, and no agreement, because of the difficulty of the situation: the path to resolving this problem is what Allah the Exalted has guided to, namely that the wife's guardian sends a judge (hakam) from his side, and the husband's guardian sends a judge from his side; or the husband himself sends a judge and the wife also sends a judge from her side; or the judge sends them; all of these are permissible, because of His saying: ﴿So send an arbiter﴾, addressing the Muslims, on condition that the arbiter be just, knowing and perceptive, so that he can judge with justice. **Explanation of the Words**

*"Worship Allah" (اعبدوا الله):* The address is to the believers. "Worship" (اعبدوا) means: obey Him in His commands and prohibitions, with the utmost humility, love, and glorification of Him, may He be exalted.

*"Do not associate anything with Him" (لا تشركوا به شيئاً):* That is, do not worship anyone alongside Him in any form of worship by which Allah the Exalted is worshipped by His servants, such as supplication, awe (khashyah), sacrifice (dhabh), vowing (nadhr), bowing (ruku'), prostration (sujud), and others.

*"Those near in kinship" (ذوي القربى):* Those who have blood relations.

*"The wayfarer" (وابن السبيل):* The traveler, whether he seeks hospitality or not.

*"The neighbor who is near" (والجار ذي القربى):* The one who is related by lineage or by marriage.

*"The neighbor who is a stranger" (الجار الجنب):* The non-relative, whether he is a believer or a disbeliever.

*"The companion at your side" (الصاحب بالجنب):* The wife, and the close companion who stays with you, such as the student and the fellow traveler.

*"What your right hands possess" (وما ملكت أيمانكم):* The bondsmen and bondswomen, male and female slaves.

*"Arrogant and boastful" (مختال فخور):* Ikhtiyal is vanity in one's gait; fakhr and iftikhar are boasting of one's lineage, descent, and wealth, by enumerating and mentioning them.

*"They are stingy" (يبخلون):* They withhold what is obligatory to give of what is good, in every respect.

*"They conceal" (ويكتمون):* They deny what Allah has given them of knowledge and wealth, despite His bounty upon them.

*"A companion" (قريناً):* The qarin is the one who stays constantly with his companion and never parts from him, as if he were tied to him with a qarn, that is, a rope.

*"And what would be upon them" (وماذا عليهم):* That is, what harm would it do them, or what misfortune would befall them, if they believed?

**The Meaning of the Verses**

The noble context continues with the guidance of the believers and the explanation of the legal rulings for them, so that they may act upon them, be perfected, and be happy. In the first verse [36], Allah the Exalted commands the believers to worship Him and affirm His oneness (tawhid) in that worship, and to show kindness to parents, by obeying them in what is right, doing good to them, and warding off harm from them. Likewise, He commands kindness to relatives, orphans, the needy, and neighbors in general, whether they are relatives or strangers; to the close companion who never parts from one, such as a wife, a fellow traveler, a co-worker, a student, or a seeker of knowledge, and similar associations that are rarely severed, for all of these are included in the term "companion at the side." Likewise the wayfarer, and what the right hand possesses of a female or male slave. Those mentioned are more emphatically owed kindness, though kindness is a good that is extended to all people, as Allah says: ﴿And speak to people kindly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 83], and He says: ﴿And do good; indeed, Allah loves those who do good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 195]. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is arrogant and boastful﴾ indicates that withholding kindness, which is restraining harm and extending what is good, results from the traits of stinginess and pride, and both are among the worst of character traits. This is what the first verse [36] indicates.

As for the second verse [37], it contains, in connection with the condemnation of stinginess and pride, a denunciation of the stinginess of some of the People of the Book and their concealment of the truth, which also results from their stinginess. Allah says: ﴿Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, that is, of wealth and knowledge. They concealed the descriptions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his attributes which are indicated in the Torah and the Gospel; they were stingy with their wealth and commanded others to be stingy with it, for they used to say to the Ansar: "Do not spend your wealth on Muhammad, for we fear poverty for you." The predicate of the relative pronoun "those who" is omitted, its implied sense being "they are the true disbelievers," which is indicated by His saying: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. This is what the second verse [37] contains.

As for the third [38] and fourth [39] verses, the first of them describes the state of another group, other than the Jews, namely the hypocrites. Allah says: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾, that is, ostentatiously before them, so that they may ward off blame and gain praise. ﴿And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾, because they are disbelieving polytheists, and they only displayed Islam out of taqiyyah (concealment of belief under compulsion); therefore their spending was only for show and nothing more. His saying: ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is the companion﴾ means: Satan is an evil companion for him. This clause, ﴿And whoever has Satan...﴾, indicates the omitted predicate of the relative pronoun, and it suffices from mentioning it, as in the first relative clause. It may be estimated as: "Satan, their companion, is the one who made disbelief in Allah and the Last Day appealing to them."

This is what the fourth verse [39] contains, which is His saying: ﴿And what would be upon them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ It contains a rebuke and reproach to those hypocrites who spend to be seen by people, and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, because of Satan's seduction of them and his constant company with them. Allah says: ﴿And what would be upon them﴾, that is, what harm would it do them, or what injury would reach them, in this world or the next, if they had truly believed in Allah and His Messenger and spent in the way of Allah from what Allah had provided them? In the address there is a divine call to them to correct their faith and uprightness by leaving the circle of hypocrisy into which the companion (Satan), may the curses of God be upon him, had led them. Therefore, Allah did not mention any threat to them, but said: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾. In this there is a warning to them about the evil of their state if they persist in their hypocrisy, for Allah's knowledge of them necessitates punishing them if they do not repent.

**Guidance from the Verses**

1. Establishing ten rights and commanding their immediate fulfillment: worshipping Allah alone, kindness to parents, and to all those mentioned in the first verse.

2. Condemnation of vanity arising from pride, and condemnation of boasting, and an explanation of Allah's dislike of both.

3. The prohibition of stinginess and the command against it, and the prohibition of concealing knowledge, especially religious knowledge.

4. The prohibition of riya' (showing off in worship) and condemnation of its practitioner.

5. Condemnation of evil companions for what they command and invite their companions to, to the point that it was said:

Therefore, Allah did not mention any threat to them, but said: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾. **Guidance from the Verses**

1. Establishing ten rights and commanding their immediate fulfillment: worshipping Allah alone, kindness to parents, and to all those mentioned in the first verse.

2. Condemnation of vanity arising from pride, and condemnation of boasting, and an explanation of Allah's dislike of both.

3. The prohibition of stinginess and the command against it, and the prohibition of concealing knowledge, especially religious knowledge.

4. The prohibition of riya' (showing off in worship) and condemnation of its practitioner.

5. Condemnation of evil companions for what they command and invite their companions to, to the point that it was said:
؎ Do not ask about the man, ask about his companion,
   for every near one takes on the traits of the one he associates with.

**Explanation of the Words**

*"Worship Allah" (اعبدوا الله):* The address is to the believers. "Worship" (اعبدوا) means: obey Him in His commands and prohibitions, with the utmost humility, love, and glorification of Him, may He be exalted.

*"Do not associate anything with Him" (لا تشركوا به شيئاً):* That is, do not worship anyone alongside Him in any form of worship by which Allah the Exalted is worshipped by His servants, such as supplication, awe (khashyah), sacrifice (dhabh), vowing (nadhr), bowing (ruku'), prostration (sujud), and others.

*"Those near in kinship" (ذوي القربى):* Those who have blood relations.

*"The wayfarer" (وابن السبيل):* The traveler, whether he seeks hospitality or not.

*"The neighbor who is near" (والجار ذي القربى):* The one who is related by lineage or by marriage.

*"The neighbor who is a stranger" (الجار الجنب):* The non-relative, whether he is a believer or a disbeliever.

*"The companion at your side" (الصاحب بالجنب):* The wife, and the close companion who stays with you, such as the student and the fellow traveler.

*"What your right hands possess" (وما ملكت أيمانكم):* The bondsmen and bondswomen, male and female slaves.

*"Arrogant and boastful" (مختال فخور):* Ikhtiyal is vanity in one's gait; fakhr and iftikhar are boasting of one's lineage, descent, and wealth, by enumerating and mentioning them.

*"They are stingy" (يبخلون):* They withhold what is obligatory to give of what is good, in every respect.

*"They conceal" (ويكتمون):* They deny what Allah has given them of knowledge and wealth, despite His bounty upon them.

*"A companion" (قريناً):* The qarin is the one who stays constantly with his companion and never parts from him, as if he were tied to him with a qarn, that is, a rope.

*"And what would be upon them" (وماذا عليهم):* That is, what harm would it do them, or what misfortune would befall them, if they believed?

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 40–42:

Explanation of the words:

Al-zulm (injustice): placing a thing in other than its proper place.

Mithqal dharrah (the weight of an atom): al-mithqal (weight) is derived from thiql (heaviness), so everything that is weighed has weight. The dharrah (atom) is the smallest particle in existence, to the point that it has been said it is the floating mote (al-habaa') or the head of an ant.

Al-hasanah (good deed): a beautiful act of kindness.

Yudaa'ifuha (He multiplies it): He intends by it its double.

Min ladunhu (from Himself): from His own presence.

Ajran 'azheeman (a great reward): a great recompense and a mighty reward.

Al-shahid (the witness): the one who testifies to a thing because of his knowledge of it.

Yawaddu (he loves): he desires.

Tusawwa bihimu al-ard (they will be made level with the earth): they will become dust like it.

Wa laa yaktumuna Allaha hadeethan (and they will not conceal from Allah any statement): that is, they will not hide any speech.

The meaning of the verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, had commanded in the preceding verses to worship Him and to show kindness to those of His servants who were mentioned, and had commanded spending in His cause, and had censured miserliness, arrogance, boasting, and concealing knowledge, and this required a recompense according to its kind, good or evil, He mentioned in this verse [40]: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (even) the weight of an atom; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾. He mentioned His justice in recompense and His mercy. He informed that at the reckoning He does not wrong His servant the weight of the smallest thing, an atom, by diminishing from his good deeds a single good deed, nor increasing his evil deeds by a single evil deed. And if a single good deed is found with a believer, He multiplies it by multiples known to Him alone, and gives from Himself, without any compensation, a great reward whose value cannot be measured. So to Allah belongs all praise and favour. This is what the first verse [40] contains.

As for the second verse [41]: since He, exalted is He, mentioned recompense and reckoning, which the context indicates, He mentioned what points to the terror of the Day of Reckoning and the gravity of the matter in it. So He addressed His Messenger ﷺ saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ The meaning of the noble verse is: how will the state of the people of disbelief, evil and corruption be when Allah, exalted is He, brings a witness from every nation to testify against it concerning what it obeyed and what it disobeyed, so that the reckoning is completed according to the clear proofs and the witnesses, and the recompense according to disbelief and faith, and sins and acts of obedience. And We bring you, O Messenger, O beloved Prophet ﷺ, as a witness against these, that is, against your nation ﷺ, those who believed in him and those who disbelieved, since he testifies that he conveyed his message and discharged his trust ﷺ. This is what the second verse contains.

As for the third verse [42]: since He, exalted is He, mentioned what points to the terror of the Day of Resurrection in verse [41], He mentioned an example of that terror, which is that those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger wish that they were levelled with the earth, becoming dust, so that they would not be reckoned with nor be recompensed with Hell. And that on that Day they will not conceal from Allah any speech, since their limbs will speak and testify against them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿On that Day﴾, that is, the day when a witness is brought from every nation, ﴿those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them﴾, so that they would become dust like it. Their intention is that they be levelled with the earth and become dust. The expression is in the form of "I put my head into the cap," whereas the original is "I put the cap onto my head." And His words ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ are an report of their inability to conceal anything from Allah, exalted is He, because their limbs will testify against them after their mouths are sealed, as Allah, exalted is He, said in Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿Today We seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:65].

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the justice of Allah, exalted is He, His mercy, and His abundant bounty.

2- Clarification of the terror of the Day of Resurrection, to the extent that the disbeliever will wish that the earth were levelled over him so that he would become dust.

3- The Messenger of Allah ﷺ's knowledge of the effects of testimony upon the servant on the Day of Resurrection. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him one day: "Recite the Qur'an to me." I said: "Shall I recite it to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "I love to hear it from someone else." So I recited ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord﴾ until I reached this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, and the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were shedding tears, and he said: "That is enough (hasbuka), it has sufficed you of what you have recited to me."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 43:

Explanation of the words:

"لا تقربوا" (la taqrabu): do not approach, i.e. do not draw near to it, a metaphor for entering into it; or, do not approach its mosques.

"سكارى" (sukara): plural of sakran, one who has drunk an intoxicant so that it has veiled and covered his mind.

"تعلموا ما تقولون" (ta'lamu ma taqulun): so that the intoxication may leave you by keeping the drinking far from the time of prayer. This was before the prohibition of wine and all intoxicants.

"ولا جنباً" (wa la junuban): the junub (one in a state of major ritual impurity) is one who has janabah, and janabah has two causes: sexual intercourse, or a wet dream (ihtilam).

"عابري سبيل" (ʿabiri sabil): passing through the mosque, going by without sitting in it.

"الغائط" (al-ghaʾit): a low-lying place for relieving oneself, i.e. defecating there.

"لامستم النساء" (lamastum al-nisa'): you have had intercourse with them.

"فتيمموا صعيداً طيباً" (fa-tayammamu sa'idan tayyiban): intend clean earth.

"عفواً غفوراً" (ʿafuwwan ghafuran): ʿAfuw: does not call to account for every sin; ghafur: abundant in forgiveness of the sins of His servants who turn back to Him in repentance.

Meaning of the noble verse:

There is no doubt that this verse has a cause for its revelation, which is that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him), according to the narration of al-Tirmidhi, hosted a banquet for some of the Companions. They ate and drank, and the time of prayer came, so they stood for it, and one of them went forward to lead them in prayer. He recited the surah al-Kafirun, but he was intoxicated, and he recited: "Say: O disbelievers, I worship what you worship," which is false, and he continued his recitation while dropping the negative particles. So it was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed...﴾, i.e. O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿do not approach prayer﴾, i.e. do not enter into it, while you are ﴿intoxicated﴾ from wine, as it was then permitted and not yet forbidden, ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾ in your prayer, so that your minds are complete, by which you distinguish error from correctness. And do not approach the mosques of prayer to sit in them while you are ﴿in a state of janabah﴾ until you bathe, except for one of you who is ﴿passing through﴾, since the paths of some of them to their homes were past the Prophet's mosque. ﴿And if you are sick﴾ with wounds that water harms, or with an illness that prevents you from using water for ablution or bathing, or if you are ﴿on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women﴾ by lying with them or by touching them with desire, ﴿and you find no water﴾ with which to bathe if you are junub, or to perform ablution if you are in a minor state of impurity, ﴿then seek clean earth﴾, i.e. intend clean earth, ﴿and wipe your faces and hands﴾ with it once, for that suffices you in place of bathing and ablution. If the sick person recovers or water is found, then bathe or perform ablution, and do not perform tayammum, since the concession ends with the disappearance of the illness or the availability of water. As for His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of the verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, He informs of His absolute perfection, describing Himself as pardoning His believing servants when they oppose His command, and as forgiving their sins when they turn back to Him in repentance. For this reason, He, mighty and majestic, did not call them to account for praying while intoxicated and not knowing what they were saying, and He forgave them and sent down this Qur'an as instruction and guidance for them.

Guidance from the noble verse:

Among the guidance of the noble verse:

1- Establishing the principle of abrogation (naskh) of legal rulings in the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

2- The prohibition of a junub remaining in the mosque, and the permissibility of passing through without staying.

3- The obligation of bathing upon the junub, who is one whose janabah has occurred, by having a wet dream and seeing the fluid, or by having intercourse with his wife, inserting his penis into her private part, even if no fluid is emitted.

The manner of bathing: he washes his two hands, saying "Bismillah," intending the lifting of the major impurity. Then he cleanses his private parts and what is around them. Then he performs ablution, washing his hands three times, then rinses his mouth and sniffs water into his nose, and blows it out three times. Then he washes his face and his hands up to the elbows, and wipes his head and ears once. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles. Then he dips his hands in the water and combs through the roots of his hair with his fingers, then pours water over his head with each handful, washing it. Then he pours water over his right side and washes it, then over his left side and washes it, from its top to its bottom. He ensures water reaches his armpits and every place of his body that water does not reach easily, such as the navel and beneath the knees.

4- If a person cannot find water due to rain or the like, he performs tayammum with all parts of the earth: sand, salt-flats, and stones. Tayammum is to strike the earth with his palm and then wipe his face and hands with it, based on the hadith of ʿAmmar (may Allah be pleased with him) in the Sahih.

5- Explanation of Allah's pardon and forgiveness, in that He did not call to account those who prayed while intoxicated.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 44–46:

Explanation of the words:

"Alam tara" (Have you not seen?): Have you not perceived, i.e., with your heart, i.e., known.

Nasiban (a portion): a share and a due.

Yashtaruna al-dalalah (they purchase misguidance): i.e., disbelief in exchange for faith.

Al-a'da' (the enemies): plural of 'aduw (enemy), who is one who stands far from you, wishing you harm and disliking your benefit.

Hadu (they were Jews): it was said of them for their saying: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ [al-A'raf: 156], i.e., repented and returned.

Yuharrifuna (they distort): tahrif (distortion) is inclining speech away from its meaning toward a false meaning for the sake of misleading.

Al-kalim (the words): speech, which is the speech of Allah the Exalted in the Torah.

Wasma' ghayra musma' (and hear without being heard): i.e., "Hear what you say, may Allah not let you hear." This is clear disbelief from them.

Wa-ta'nan fi al-din (and as a slander against the religion): their insulting of the Messenger (ﷺ) is the greatest slander against the religion.

Unzurna (look at us): give us respite until we hear and understand.

Aqwam (more upright): more just and more correct.

La'anahum Allah bi-kufrihim (Allah cursed them for their disbelief): He expelled them from His mercy and removed them far from His guidance because of their disbelief in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Meaning of the verses:

It is narrated that these verses were revealed concerning Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut, one of the great Jewish men in Medina. When he spoke to the Messenger (ﷺ), he twisted his tongue and said, "Ra'ina (our attention to you)," meaning, "Hear us, O Muhammad, until we make you understand." Then he slandered Islam and disparaged it. So Allah the Exalted revealed these three verses up to His saying: ﴿So they do not believe except a little﴾. Here is their explanation:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, purchasing misguidance and wanting you to lose the way?﴾ That is: has it not reached your knowledge and the knowledge of your companions what should make you wonder? Those who were given a portion of the Book, namely Rifa'ah ibn Zayd and his Jewish brethren, were given a share of the Torah, so they recognized the truth of the Islamic religion and the truthfulness of its Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿They purchase misguidance﴾, which is disbelief; they buy it in exchange for faith, by denying the Prophet's descriptions and attributes that are in the Torah, in order to preserve their standing among their people, so that they may lead and be preferred. And they want, along with that, that you, O believers, lose the way, the path of truth and right guidance, which is faith in Allah and His Messenger and acting in obedience to them, for happiness and completion. ﴿And Allah knows best your enemies﴾, who wish you harm and do not wish you benefit; therefore He informs you about them so that you may know them, avoid them, and be saved from their deception and misguidance. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector﴾ for you, on whom you rely and to whom you entrust your affairs, ﴿and sufficient is Allah as a Helper﴾ who will give you victory over them and others, so worship Him and put your trust in Him.

﴿Among those who are Jews, they distort the words from their places﴾: that is, among the Jews are those who distort the words from their places. The words are the speech of Allah the Exalted in the Torah, and distorting them is inclining them away from their intended meaning, or changing and altering them, to mislead people and to turn them away from the truth that they were required to believe in, speak, and act upon. They say to the Prophet (ﷺ), out of disbelief and obstinacy, ﴿We hear and we disobey, and hear without being heard﴾, that is, "May Allah not let you hear." ﴿Ra'ina﴾: a word whose outward form suggests consideration (mura'ah), but whose inward meaning is a slander against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), since the Jews consider it a term of foolishness, and they say it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as abuse and insult. May Allah disgrace them, curse them, and cut off their root. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Twisting their tongues and slandering the religion﴾, that is, they twist their tongues with the word by which they revile, so that it does not appear clearly against them, and by it they slander the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If they had said, "We hear and we obey, and hear, and look at us,"﴾ that is, "wait for us" in place of "ra'ina," it would have been better for them and more upright, meaning more just, more suitable, and more courteous. But they do not say this, because Allah the Exalted has cursed them and deprived them of every success because of their disbelief and deceit, so they do not believe except a little. That is, a faith that does not benefit them because of its scarcity; it does not reform their morals, purify their souls, or prepare them for perfection in this world or in the Hereafter.

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- Clarification of the deceit of the Jews against the believers by working to mislead them, in the time of Prophethood and up to today.

2- In Allah's sufficiency for the believers and His support is what suffices them from seeking that from anyone other than their Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

3- Exposure of the evil intentions and deeds of the Jews toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

4- Little faith does not benefit its possessor and does not profit him in any way.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 47:

Explanation of the words:

Those given the Book (ahl al-kitab): the Jews and the Christians, but what is meant here is the Jews alone and no others.

Confirming what We have sent down: the Qur'an.

Efface faces: We obliterate their traces by erasing the eyes and removing their pupils.

And turn them back on their backs: We make the face into the nape and the nape into a face.

As We cursed the people of the Sabbath: cursing them means transforming them into apes, as a disgrace to them and a humiliating punishment.

And the command of Allah is ever accomplished: the command of Allah means that His decree is bound to happen without doubt, for nothing can overpower Him, may He be exalted.

Meaning of the noble verse:

The context still concerns the Jews living beside the Messenger ﷺ in Medina. In this verse, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, addressed them by the title of knowledge and learning, namely their attribution to the Book, which is the Torah, commanding them to believe in His Book, that is, the noble Qur'an, and in the One to whom it was sent down, Muhammad ﷺ, since belief in what was revealed implies, by necessity, belief in the one to whom it was revealed. He said: ﴿Believe﴾ in the Criterion, which confirms what is with you of the foundations of religion and the descriptions of the Messenger, and the command to believe in him and support him. Hasten to belief and abandon hesitation before there befalls you what befell some of your predecessors, when they were transformed into apes and swine. ﴿Before We efface faces﴾ by removing the pupils of their eyes and the protrusion of their noses, and by closing their mouths, so the faces become napes and the napes become faces, walking backwards. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So We turn them back on their backs, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, that is, those among you who transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath, when they hunted in it though it was forbidden to them, so He transformed them into apes, despised and rejected. ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾, that is, His decree ﴿is accomplished﴾ immediately, without delay or postponement, because nothing can overpower Allah, the Exalted, and He is over all things capable.

Guidance of the verse:

From the guidance of the verse:

1- It is to be expected that a person of knowledge would be closer to guidance, but whoever has been preceded by wretchedness, because of what Allah knows of his choosing evil and persisting in it, will not benefit from knowledge. These Jews, whom Allah called to belief and who did not believe, were not guided by it.

2- The obligation to hasten repentance before the punishment descends and before there befalls a person what he does not like of chastisement and retribution.

3- Transformation may occur in the faces through the transformation of thoughts and minds, so that a person's life is corrupted and worsens; and this is what happened to the Jews of Medina. They broke their covenants, so some of them perished and some were exiled, as a result of their persistence in disbelief and their hostility toward the Messenger ﷺ and the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 48:

Explanation of the words:

"Will not forgive" (لا يغفر): will not erase, and will not leave off holding to account.

"That partners be set up with Him" (أن يشرك به): i.e., that others be worshipped alongside Him, by deeming them divine through love and veneration of them, offering sacrifices to them, and directing acts of worship to them, such as calling upon them, seeking help from them, slaughtering for them, and vowing to them.

"And forgives what is less than that" (ويغفر ما دون ذلك): i.e., what is less than shirk and disbelief, of all other sins and transgressions that are neither shirk nor disbelief.

"For whomever He wills" (لمن يشاء): i.e., for whomever He wills to forgive among all the sinners, other than those guilty of shirk and disbelief.

"Has fabricated a tremendous sin" (افترى إثماً عظيماً): "fabricated" (افترى): invented and lied, by attributing worship to other than the Lord, the Exalted. "Sin" (الإثم): a great and grave sin.

Meaning of the noble verse:

It is narrated that when the saying of God, the Exalted, from surah al-Zumar was revealed, ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God; indeed God forgives all sins﴾ [39:53], a man stood up and said, "And shirk, O Prophet of God?" The Messenger of God ﷺ disliked that, and God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed God does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills﴾. Thus He, the Exalted, informs about Himself that He does not forgive the sin known as shirk and disbelief, while all other sins, great and small, are subject to His will: if He wills, He forgives them to their perpetrator and does not punish him for them, and if He wills, He takes him to account for them and punishes him. Whoever associates partners with God, the Exalted, has fabricated a tremendous lie, since he worships one who does not deserve worship and makes divine one who has no right to be deified; therefore he speaks falsehood and acts upon what is false, and from here his sin is great.

Guidance of the noble verse:

From the guidance of the verse:

1- The gravity of the sin of shirk and disbelief, and that all other sins are beneath them.

2- Shirk is a sin that will not be forgiven for one who dies without repenting of it.

3- Those who commit sins other than shirk and disbelief should not despair of God's forgiveness for them, but should fear Him.

4- Shirk is falsehood, and the one who commits it speaks falsehood and is one who acts upon it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 49–50:

Explanation of the words:

Tazkiyat al-nafs (the purification of the soul): clearing it of sins and wrongdoings.

Yuzakki man yasha' (He purifies whomever He wills): He cleanses from sins whomever He wills of His servants, by granting them success to act in the way that purifies the soul, and by helping them to do so.

Al-fatil (the thread): the white thread in the middle of a date-stone, or the dirt that a person rolls between two fingers from his palm or body, which is the least and most insignificant of things.

Al-kadhib (lying): the failure of a report to correspond with reality.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context returns to speaking about the People of the Book. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger and the believers: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾, and this is a matter that prompts wonder and astonishment, since it is supposed that a person does not praise himself until someone else praises him. The Jews and Christians said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18], and they said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], ﴿They said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [Al 'Imran: 24], and other false claims. When Allah the Exalted denied them this falsehood on which they lived, and which had kept them from faith and from entering Islam, He informed them that He, the Mighty and Majestic, is the One who purifies whomever He wills of His servants, by guiding them to faith and to righteous deeds through which the human soul grows pure. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, Allah purifies whomever He wills, and they will not be wronged even the least bit (fatil)﴾, meaning, the smallest amount: nothing is added to the sins of the servant, nor is anything subtracted from his good deeds. Then Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to marvel at the condition of these Jews and Christians, who lie against Allah the Exalted and fabricate falsehood through those claims mentioned just before. And ﴿sufficient is it as a manifest sin﴾. It immerses its doer in the Fire.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition on a person praising himself with his tongue, and boasting of it, whether seeking leadership, or abandoning worship and obedience on the pretext that he has no need of it because he is pure. And may Allah be pleased with him.

2- Allah praises His servant by commending him in the highest assembly, and purifies him by granting him faith and the enabling of righteous acts, such as prayer, charity and all the lawful acts of obedience, through which the human soul is cleansed and purified.

3- The justice of reckoning and recompense on the Day of Resurrection, based on His saying: ﴿and they will not be wronged even the least bit﴾.

Explanation of the words:

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 56–57:

Explanation of the words:

"Nuslihim naran" (We shall cast them into a Fire): We shall make them enter a Fire in which they will burn.

"Nadijat julooduhum" (Their skins are roasted): they are cooked, become scorched and fall away.

"Liyadhuqu al-adhab" (that they may taste the punishment): so that the punishment continues for them, painful.

"Aziizan hakiman" (Mighty, Wise): Victorious; He punishes whoever deserves punishment.

"Tajri min tahtiha al-anhar" (Rivers flow beneath them): rivers flow through their trees and their palaces.

"Mutahhara" (purified): free from all harm and impurity, absolutely.

"Zillan zaliilan" (dense shade): the dense shade, abundant and lasting, in which there is neither heat nor cold.

Meaning of the two verses:

Following the mention of faith and disbelief in the previous verse, Allah, exalted is He, mentions in these two verses both the threat and the promise: the threat for the people of disbelief and the promise for the people of faith. He, exalted is He, says: "Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs, We will surely cast them into Fire" (i.e., He will make them enter the Fire of Hell, where they will burn and be scorched by it). "Every time their skins are roasted" (i.e., become scorched and fall away), Allah immediately replaces them with other skins, so that their taste of the punishment and their feeling of it is renewed. His saying, exalted is He, "Indeed Allah is ever Mighty and Wise," is a concluding statement whose purpose is to affirm the execution of the threat against them, for the Mighty, the Victorious, is not unable to carry out what He threatens against His enemies, and the Wise in His management punishes those who disbelieve in Him and depart from His obedience. This is what the first verse [56] contains of threat for the people of disbelief.

As for the second verse [57], it contains the glad tidings for the people of faith and righteous deeds, together with avoiding shirk and sins. He, exalted is He, says: "And those who believe and do righteous deeds" (i.e., after abandoning shirk and sins), "We shall admit them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses" (i.e., women of the wide-eyed Houris, purified from everything that harms or diminishes their beauty and loveliness, pure from urine, feces, and menstrual blood). His saying, exalted is He, "And We shall admit them to a shade, dense" (i.e., abundant, sheltering shade that protects them from heat and cold). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once spoke to us about Paradise, saying: "In Paradise there is a tree called the Tree of Eternity; a rider can travel in its shade for a hundred years without cutting through it."

Lessons from the two verses:

1- Disbelief and sins are causes of the punishment of the Hereafter.

2- Clarification of the wisdom in replacing the skins of the people of the Fire: that their feeling of the punishment may endure.

3- Faith and righteous deeds, together with abandoning shirk and sins, are causes of the blessings of the Hereafter.

4- Paradise is the abode of bliss, free from the turbidity of pleasures and happiness within it.

Following the mention of faith and disbelief in the previous verse, Allah, exalted is He, mentions in these two verses both the threat and the promise: the threat for the people of disbelief and the promise for the people of faith. He, exalted is He, says: "Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs, We will surely cast them into Fire" (i.e., He will make them enter the Fire of Hell, where they will burn and be scorched by it). "Every time their skins are roasted" (i.e., become scorched and fall away), Allah immediately replaces them with other skins, so that their taste of the punishment and their feeling of it is renewed. His saying, exalted is He, "Indeed Allah is ever Mighty and Wise," is a concluding statement whose purpose is to affirm the execution of the threat against them, for the Mighty, the Victorious, is not unable to carry out what He threatens against His enemies, and the Wise in His management punishes those who disbelieve in Him and depart from His obedience. This is what the first verse [56] contains of threat for the people of disbelief.

As for the second verse [57], it contains the glad tidings for the people of faith and righteous deeds, together with avoiding shirk and sins. He, exalted is He, says: "And those who believe and do righteous deeds" (i.e., after abandoning shirk and sins), "We shall admit them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses" (i.e., women of the wide-eyed Houris, purified from everything that harms or diminishes their beauty and loveliness, pure from urine, feces, and menstrual blood). His saying, exalted is He, "And We shall admit them to a shade, dense" (i.e., abundant, sheltering shade that protects them from heat and cold). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once spoke to us about Paradise, saying: "In Paradise there is a tree called the Tree of Eternity; a rider can travel in its shade for a hundred years without cutting through it."

Lessons from the two verses:

1- Disbelief and sins are causes of the punishment of the Hereafter.

2- Clarification of the wisdom in replacing the skins of the people of the Fire: that their feeling of the punishment may endure.

3- Faith and righteous deeds, together with abandoning shirk and sins, are causes of the blessings of the Hereafter.

4- Paradise is the abode of bliss, free from the turbidity of pleasures and happiness within it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 58–59:

Explanation of the words:

"An tu'addu al-amanat" (that you render the trusts): the rendering (ada') of a trust means handing it over to the one who entrusted it. Amanat is the plural of amanah, which is whatever a person is entrusted with, whether speech, action, or property.

Al-'adl (justice): the opposite of oppression and of deviation, whether by deficiency or excess.

"Ni'ma ya'izukum" (how excellent is what He admonishes you): ni'ma means "how excellent a thing"; ya'izukum means He commands you to render the trusts and to judge with justice.

"Wa-uli al-amr minkum" (and those in authority among you): uli al-amr (those in authority) are the rulers and the scholars among the Muslims.

"Tanaza'tum fi shay'" (you dispute over something): you differ concerning it, each party wanting to snatch the thing from the hand of the other.

"Rudduhu ila Allah wa-l-Rasul" (refer it back to Allah and the Messenger): that is, to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ).

"Wa-ahsanu ta'wilan" (and better in outcome): better in consequence, since ta'wil of a thing is what it returns to in the end.

Meaning of the two verses:

It is related that the first verse, "Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to their owners," was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi, in whose possession was the key of the Ka'bah, as he was its custodian (sadin). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked him for it on the morning of the Conquest. He prayed two rak'ahs inside the House and came out. Al-'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Give it to me, O Messenger of Allah, so that I may combine the watering (of the pilgrims) and the custodianship." Then Allah revealed this verse and the one after it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the verse to the people, called Uthman ibn Talhah, and gave him the key. However, the lesson lies in the generality of the wording, not in the specificity of the occasion of revelation. Therefore the verse applies to every trust: every person entrusted with something must guard it and look after it until he renders it to its owner. The verse primarily addresses the rulers of the Muslims, by the indication of the words, "And when you judge between people, that you judge with justice," which is equity and the opposite of oppression, and its meaning is delivering rights to those who deserve them from among the individual subjects. His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, how excellent is what He admonishes you with" means that His command to the Muslim nation, rulers and ruled alike, to render trusts and judge with justice is a good thing; and indeed it is so, for the foundation of a dignified life is the upholding of the rendering of trusts and of judging with justice. His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing" contains an exhortation to what is commanded, by instilling in the soul the faculty of observing Allah, for whoever knows that Allah hears his words and sees his deeds keeps straight in his speech, so he does not lie, and in his action, so he does not fall short. This is what the first verse [58] indicates.

As for the second [59]: when Allah commanded the rulers of the Muslims to render the trusts, which are the rights of the subjects, and to judge among them with justice, He commanded the believers, who are under their authority, to obey Him and His Messenger first, and then to obey the rulers, saying: "O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you." Obedience to those in authority is restricted to what is known to be lawful in the Shari'ah; in what is disobedience, there is no obedience by choice, based on the hadith: "Obedience is only in what is good, and there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." His saying, the Exalted: "And if you dispute over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger" is a general address to both the rulers and the subjects. Whenever a disagreement arises concerning a matter of religion or worldly affairs, it is obligatory to refer that matter to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whatever they have judged in, it is obligatory to accept, whether it is sweet or bitter. His saying, the Exalted: "If you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day" indicates that faith entails submission to the decree of Allah and His Messenger, and it implies that referring disputed matters to other than the Shari'ah undermines the faith of the believer. His saying: "That is better and more excellent in outcome" means that referring and returning disputed issues and questions to the Book and the Sunnah is better in state and in final result, because it puts an end to dispute and keeps the nation united, loving one another, and cooperating.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation to return trusts after safeguarding them.

2- The obligation of justice in judgment, and the prohibition of partiality and oppression in it.

3- The obligation to obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and obey the rulers and scholars (fuqaha') of the Muslims, because obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, and obedience to the ruler is obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ), based on the hadith: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys my commander has disobeyed me."

4- The obligation to refer any matter in dispute, whether in belief, worship, or judgment, to the Book and the Sunnah, and the obligation to be content with their ruling.

5- The praiseworthy outcome and the good, happy state in the Muslim nation's referring what it disputes to the Book of its Lord and the Sunnah of its Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 60–63:

Explanation of the words:

Yazʿumūn (they claim): they say, while lying.

Bimā unzila ilayka (what has been sent down to you): the Qur'an; wa-mā unzila min qablika (and what was sent down before you): the Torah.

Ṭāghūt (the false deity, transgressor): everything that is worshipped besides Allah and is content with being worshipped. The intended one here is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, the Jew, or a soothsayer of the soothsayers of the Arabs.

Munāfiqīn (hypocrites): plural of munāfiq (hypocrite), who conceals disbelief and displays faith out of fear of the Muslims.

Yaṣuddūn (they turn away): they turn away from you and likewise turn others away.

Muṣība (calamity): a punishment because of their disbelief and hypocrisy.

In yurīdūn (if they intend): i.e., they do not intend.

Illā iḥsānan (except good): i.e., reconciliation between the disputants.

Wa-tawfīqan (and harmony): bringing together and uniting those who differ.

Fa-aʿrid ʿanhum (so turn away from them): i.e., pardon them and do not hold them to account.

ʿIẓhum (admonish them): command them with what is fitting for them and what is obligatory upon them.

Qawlan balīgan (an eloquent word): a strong speech that reaches the innermost hearts because of its eloquence and clarity.

The meaning of the verses:

It is narrated that a hypocrite and a Jew disputed over something. The Jew said, "Let us go to judgment before Muhammad ﷺ, for he knows that he judges with justice and does not take bribes." The hypocrite said, "Let us go to judgment before Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, the Jew." They went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he ruled in favour of the Jew. Concerning the two of them this verse was revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you﴾, meaning the hypocrite, ﴿and what was sent down before you﴾, meaning the Jew. The interrogative is for wonder: has not the situation of these two men reached your knowledge? ﴿They desire to take their judgment to the false deity﴾, "Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf", or the soothsayer of Juhayna, although Allah had commanded them to reject it. ﴿And Satan desires to lead them far astray﴾, since he made the seeking of judgment from the soothsayer or Kaʿb the Jew seem attractive to them.

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger"﴾, to judge between you, you would see, how strange, the hypocrites turning away from you, fleeing from your judgment, unwilling to be judged by you because of their disbelief in you and their denial of you. ﴿So how will it be when a calamity strikes them﴾, when a disaster befalls them because of their sins? Will they remain turning away from you, or what? ﴿Then they come to you swearing by Allah﴾, saying, "We intended only good in what we did and harmony between the disputants." This is what the three verses indicate. As for the fourth, which is the words of the Most High, ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them a word reaching into their souls﴾, Allah refers to them with "those" because of their remoteness in baseness and degradation. He says, ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾, i.e., of hypocrisy and deviation, so they are exposed to vengeance and evil punishment. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, do not hold them to account. ﴿And admonish them﴾, commanding them to fear Allah and to submit to Him outwardly and inwardly, warning them of the consequence of the evil of their deeds by abandoning judgment before you and seeking judgment from the false deity. ﴿And speak to them, concerning themselves, a word that is eloquent and penetrates their hearts, stirring them and removing their heedlessness, that perhaps they may return.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of seeking judgment from other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, when a scholar of the two is available.

2- The obligation to reject the false deity, whatever its kind.

3- The obligation to call to seeking judgment by the Book and the Sunnah, and the obligation to accept it.

4- The recommendation to turn away from the ignorant and to admonish them with eloquent speech that reaches their hearts and stirs them.

He says, ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾, i.e., of hypocrisy and deviation, so they are exposed to vengeance and evil punishment. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, do not hold them to account. ﴿And admonish them﴾, commanding them to fear Allah and to submit to Him outwardly and inwardly, warning them of the consequence of the evil of their deeds by abandoning judgment before you and seeking judgment from the false deity. ﴿And speak to them, concerning themselves, a word that is eloquent and penetrates their hearts, stirring them and removing their heedlessness, that perhaps they may return.

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of seeking judgment from other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, when a scholar of the two is available.

2- The obligation to reject the false deity, whatever its kind.

3- The obligation to call to seeking judgment by the Book and the Sunnah, and the obligation to accept it.

4- The recommendation to turn away from the ignorant and to admonish them with eloquent speech that reaches their hearts and stirs them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 64–65:

Explanation of the words:

bi-idhni Allah (by the permission of Allah): idhn Allah means His informing of a thing and His commanding of it.

zalamu anfusahum (they wronged themselves): by seeking judgment from the taghut (false authority, i.e. whatever is worshipped or obeyed besides Allah) and by leaving judgment to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

istaghfaru Allah (they asked Allah for forgiveness): they asked Him to forgive them, either by saying "Allahumma righfir lana" (O Allah, forgive us), or by saying "astaghfiru Allah" (I seek Allah's forgiveness).

yuhakkimuka (they make you judge): they make you a judge between them and entrust the matter to you.

fima shajara baynahum (in what has become disputed among them): i.e., they differed concerning it, because the face of truth and correctness in it became mixed with error and falsehood.

haraj (constriction): tightness and discomfort.

mimma qadayta (concerning what you have decided): what you have judged in it.

wa yusallimu (and submit): i.e., they yield to accepting your judgment and submit to it with complete submission.

Meaning of the two verses:

After establishing the error and misguidance of the two who wished to seek judgment from the taghut, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf the Jew, and the two being the Jew and the hypocrite in the preceding verses, Allah, exalted is He, informs in this noble verse that He did not send any messenger from among His messengers, of hundreds, except that He commanded those to whom he was sent to obey him, follow him, and seek judgment from him and make him judge in everything they dispute; that is His command, His decree, and His measure. Whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. As Allah, exalted is He, also informs, those who wronged themselves by seeking judgment from the taghut and turning away from seeking judgment from you, O Messenger, if they had come to you disavowing their sin, seeking Allah's forgiveness for their sins, and you, O Messenger, had asked Allah for forgiveness for them (that is, you had asked Allah, exalted is He, to forgive them), had this occurred from them, that would indicate their repentance, and Allah, exalted is He, would accept their repentance, and they would find Him, mighty and majestic, ﴿Oft-Returning, Most Merciful﴾. This is the meaning of verse [64]: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Oft-Returning, Most Merciful.﴾

As for the second verse [65]: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely.﴾ Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, says ﴿But no﴾, meaning the matter is not as they claim. Then Allah, exalted is He, swears, saying ﴿by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge﴾, O Messenger, meaning they seek your judgment concerning what they have disputed and what has become confused for them of their affairs. Then, after your judgment, they find in their breasts not the slightest doubt about the soundness and justice of your judgment, and in submitting to it and being content with it; this is the meaning of the remaining "haraj" (discomfort) in His saying: ﴿then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely.﴾

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation of obeying the Messenger (ﷺ) in what he commands and forbids.

2- The refutation of one who claims that the verse contains evidence for the permissibility of asking the Messenger (ﷺ) for forgiveness, because the words of the Exalted, ﴿and if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you﴾, were revealed concerning the two men who wished to seek judgment from Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf the Jew and turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He made the acceptance of their repentance conditional upon their coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), seeking Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger's asking forgiveness for them; otherwise there is no repentance for them. As for anyone other than them, his repentance does not depend on coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or on his asking forgiveness for him, and this is a matter of consensus among the Muslims.

3- Every sin, whether great or small, is considered a wronging of the self, and repentance from it is obligatory through seeking forgiveness, regret, and resolving not to return to it under any circumstances.

4- The obligation of seeking judgment from the Book and the Sunnah, and the prohibition of seeking judgment from anything other than them.

5- The obligation of being content with the judgment of Allah and His Messenger and submitting to it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 66–70:

Explanation of the words:

*Kutibna 'alayhim* (كتبنا عليهم): We obligated them and made it binding upon them.

*An uqtulu anfusakum* (أن اقتلوا أنفسكم): That is, the killing of themselves.

*Ma fa'aluhu illa qalilun minhum* (ما فعلوه إلا قليلٌ منهم): That is, the killing was not carried out except by a few of them.

*Ma yu'azuna bihi* (ما يوعظون به): That is, what they are commanded to do and forbidden from.

*Wa ashadda tathbitan* (وأشد تثبيتا): That is, greater in firmly establishing faith in their hearts.

*As-siddiqin* (الصديقين): Plural of *siddiq* (صديق), meaning one for whom truthfulness has prevailed in his words and conduct, owing to his abundant truthfulness and his striving to be truthful.

*Ash-shuhada'* (والشهداء): Plural of *shahid* (شهيد), meaning one who dies in battle; likewise one who bears witness to the soundness of Islam through proof and demonstration.

*As-salihin* (والصالحون): Plural of *salih* (صالح), meaning one who has fulfilled the rights of God Most High and the rights of His servants, whose self is righteous, whose deeds are sound, and whose righteousness outweighs his corruption.

The meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning those people who wished to seek judgment from the *taghut* (طاغوت, false authority), though they had been commanded to reject it. God Most High said: ﴿And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾ That is, by killing some of you by others, as happened to the Children of Israel when they did so; just as if We had decreed upon them that they emigrate from their homes as emigrants in Our cause, ﴿except a few of them.﴾ Then God Most High said, calling them and encouraging them toward guidance: ﴿And if they had done what they were admonished with﴾ — that is, what they were reminded of, by way of encouragement and warning, of God's commands to them to obey and submit — ﴿it would have been better for them and firmer in establishment,﴾ that is, firmer in establishing faith in their hearts and obedience upon their limbs, because faith increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience; a good deed produces a good deed, and an evil deed begets an evil deed. God Most High says: ﴿And We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾ — meaning, if they had responded to Us and done what We commanded them of obedience, and abandoned what We forbade them of sins, We would have given them from Us a great reward on the day they meet Us, and We would have guided them in this world ﴿to a straight path,﴾ namely Islam, which is the path of perfection and felicity in both lives; and their guidance to it is their being granted success to walk in it and not to deviate from it. This is what the verses [66, 67, 68] indicate.

As for verse [69], which is His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger — those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ Ibn Jarir related in his commentary that it was revealed when some of the Companions said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is not fitting for us to be parted from you in this world, for when you are taken from us you will be raised above us and we will not see you." So God Most High revealed: ﴿Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger — those are...﴾ to the end of the verse. What Allah bestowed upon them is faith in Allah, knowledge of Him, Mighty and Majestic, knowledge of what He loves and what He dislikes, and success in doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes — this in the world. As for what He bestowed upon them in the Hereafter, it is the noble neighborhood in the abode of bliss. The *siddiqin* are those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and affirmed everything the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought and reported. The *shuhada'* are the plural of *shahid*, who is one who was killed in the way of Allah. The *salihin* are the plural of *salih*, who has fulfilled the rights of God Most High and the rights of His servants completely and without deficiency. His saying: ﴿And excellent are those as companions﴾ means: excellent are those as companions in Paradise, whom they enjoy seeing and attending their gatherings, because they descend to them, then they return to their lofty dwellings and exalted ranks.

His saying: ﴿That is the bounty from Allah﴾ means that this meeting with those mentioned is by the bounty of Allah, not by their own obedience. And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾ means: Knower of the people of His obedience and the people of His disobedience, and of the obedience of the obedient and the disobedience of the disobedient; and for this reason the recompense is completed, just and merciful.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- God Most High may impose the arduous as a test and trial, such as killing oneself and emigrating from the land, but He does not impose what cannot be borne.

2- Faith increases through acts of obedience and decreases through acts of disobedience.

3- Acts of obedience bear the fruit of strengthened faith and qualify one for entry into the Gardens.

4- Companionship with the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous in Paradise is a fruit of obedience to God and to the Messenger (ﷺ).
