Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 71–73:

Explanation of the words:

Khudhu hidhrakum (خذوا حذركم): al-hidhr and al-hadhar: caution and readiness to ward off what is disliked, according to its measure.

Fanfiru thubat (فانفروا ثبات): al-nafr: going out in haste and agitation. Thubat (ثبات) is the plural of thubah (ثبة), which means a group.

Layubaththi'anna (ليبطّئن): i.e., he will delay going out, so he does not go out.

Musibah (مصيبة): killing, wounds, or defeat.

Shahidan (شهيداً): i.e., present at the battle with them.

Fadl (فضل): victory and booty.

Mawaddah (مودة): companionship and acquaintance that entails affection.

Fawzan 'azhiman (فوزا عظيماً): deliverance from the disgrace of staying behind from jihad, and attaining safety and booty.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution and go out in groups or go out all together﴾. God, may He be exalted, calls His believing servants, who were in a period in which they were preparing for the conquest of Makkah and bringing it into the fold of Islam: take up readiness and preparation, lest you meet your enemy while you are weak, while his strength is greater than yours. ﴿Go out in groups﴾: company after company and group after group. ﴿Or go out all together﴾: under your Muhammadan leadership, according to what the situation requires and what the leadership sees. Then He, who is All-Knowing, informed them that among them, i.e., among their numbers and their fellow members, there is one who will certainly delay from going out to jihad itself and to other things together, because he does not want victory for you, since he is a hypocrite, disbelieving inwardly though Muslim outwardly. He reveals the state of this cheap type of men, saying: ﴿If a calamity strikes you﴾, O sincere believers, ﴿a misfortune﴾: killing, wounding, or defeat, he says, rejoicing that he was not among them and escaped it: God has blessed me, since I was not present with them, so that what befell them did not befall me. ﴿But if a bounty from God comes to you﴾, i.e., victory and booty, ﴿he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection﴾, i.e., acquaintance or connection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them in the battle, so that I might have attained a great success" by being delivered from the disgrace of staying behind and by gaining the spoils and returning safe.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of taking full readiness and preparation upon the Muslim nation, in peace and in war alike.

2- The necessity of complete military expertise and a righteous, believing, wise and knowledgeable leadership.

3- The existence among the Muslims of spiritually defeated, dragging-their-feet, envious people, who are weak in faith; they are not to be regarded or paid attention to.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 74–76:

Explanation of the words:

Sabil Allah (the path of God): the ways that lead to raising the word of God high, by worshipping Him alone, and by no Muslim being persecuted in his religion or on account of his religion.

Yashrun (they sell): they sell, since the word "shira' " (purchase) is also applied to selling.

Al-mustad'afin (the oppressed): the one who is weak in himself, so that others take advantage of his weakness and harm him because of it.

Al-qarya (the town): in the usage of the Qur'an, al-qarya is the great city that gathers people, and what is meant here is the Sacred City of Makkah.

Fi sabil al-taghut (in the way of the false deity): i.e., in supporting polytheism, backing injustice and aggression, and spreading corruption.

The meaning of the two verses:

After God commanded His believing servants to take their precautions (ahbah, i.e., readiness for fighting), He commanded them to fight, saying: ﴿So let those fight in the way of God who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾, i.e., who sell the world in order to win the Hereafter. They are the truly believing ones, who offer their wealth and their lives seeking to win the Abode of the Hereafter. Fight those who do not believe in God nor in meeting Him, after they have been invited to belief in their Lord and repentance towards Him. Then He informed them that whoever fights in obedience to His command, and is then killed, i.e., becomes a martyr, or overcomes the enemy and triumphs, in either case ﴿We will bring him a great reward﴾, which is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise. This is what the first verse [74] indicates.

As for the second verse [75], after God commanded His servants to strive, He urged them to hasten and to enter the battle by saying: ﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you fight not in the way of God﴾, so that He may be worshipped alone and His allies made mighty, ﴿and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children﴾ who are persecuted by the polytheists and tortured on account of their religion, until they cried out and wailed in supplication to their Lord, saying: ﴿Our Lord, take us out of this city whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾, who will take charge of our affairs and suffice us in what concerns us, ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾, who will give us victory over our enemies. What prevents you, O believers, from fighting in the way of God, so that He may be worshipped alone, and so that the oppressed may be freed from the trial the polytheists inflict upon them on account of their religion?

Then in the third verse [76], God informed His believing servants, urging them to fight His enemies and theirs, by saying: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of God﴾, because they believe in Him and in His promise and His threat, ﴿and those who disbelieve fight in the way of the false deity﴾, which is disbelief and injustice, because they do not believe in God Most High nor in the bliss that is with Him, nor in the punishment and retribution that is with Him. ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾, who are the disbelievers, and do not fear them, ﴿indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been﴾ and still is ﴿weak﴾; so he and his allies among the disbelievers will not stand firm before the army of faith, the allies of the Most Merciful.

Guidance of the verses

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of fighting in the way of God, and for the sake of rescuing the oppressed among the believers, in support of truth and the nullification of falsehood.

2- The fighter in the way of God has sold his worldly life and taken the Hereafter in exchange, and what a excellent sale it is.

3- The striver returns with the greatest transaction, whether he is killed or he prevails and triumphs, and that is Paradise.

4- The fear of their enemies should not prevent the believers from striving, for their strength derives from the strength of God, while the plot of Satan is weak.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 77–79:

Explanation of the words:

*Kaffu aydiyakum* (ﷺ... "restrain your hands"): i.e., from fighting, and that was before it was enjoined.

*Kutiba 'alayhimu al-qital* ("fighting was prescribed for them"): it was made obligatory upon them.

*Yakhshawna* ("they fear"): they are afraid.

*Lawla akhkhartana* ("why did You not delay us"): why did You not postpone us.

*Fatilan* ("a speck"): the fatil is a thread that lies in the middle of a date-stone.

*Buruj mushayyadah* ("towers built high"): fortresses built with shid, which is plaster (gypsum).

*Min hasanah* ("good"): the hasanah is that which gladdens, and the sayyi'ah is that which harms.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 80–83:

Explanation of the words:

Ḥafīẓan (a guardian): You watch over their deeds and hold them to account for them.

Ṭā'ah (obedience): That is, our command is obedience to you.

Barazū (they went out): They departed.

Afalā yatadabbarūn (Will they not reflect?): Reflecting upon the Qur'an means reading a verse or verses and repeating them time after time, so as to understand what Allah the Exalted intends by them.

Adhā'ū bihi (they spread it): They divulged it, announcing it to the people.

Yastanbiṭūnahu (they would derive it): They would extract its correct meaning.

Meaning of the verses:

In His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger⁠—﴾ there is a warning to all people that whoever does not obey the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ) has not obeyed Allah the Exalted. The command of the Messenger is the command of Allah, and his prohibition is the prohibition of Allah the Exalted, so there is no excuse for anyone in not obeying the Messenger (ﷺ). His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But whoever turns away⁠—﴾ means turning away from your obedience in what you command and forbid. So leave him and do not pay him any attention, for Allah did not send you to take account of their deeds, to hold them accountable for them, or to recompense them for them. Your duty is only to convey (the message), and you have conveyed it, and so you have established the proof against them.

His saying: ﴿And they say, "Obedience."⁠﴾ That is, those hypocrites who are ill-omened toward you and of poor understanding of what you say say: "Obedience," meaning: our command is obedience to you, that is, we have no say of our own when you speak, nor in what we do when you command. We are obedient to you. ﴿But when they go out⁠﴾ means they leave your assembly, and a group of them adopts something other than what they said and resolved upon in front of you, in your assembly. Allah the Exalted records, through His noble angels who write, what they plot of evil and falsehood. Therefore ﴿turn away from them and rely upon Allah⁠﴾ and do not concern yourself with them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs⁠﴾ — He is your sufficiency and your protector against the evil they plot against you.

His saying, the Exalted, in the third verse [82]: ﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?⁠﴾ He rebukes them for their aversion, their ignorance, and their poor understanding, for if they had reflected upon the Qur'an while it was recited to them and they heard it morning and evening, they would have known that the Messenger is true and that what he brought is true. They would have believed and submitted, their Islam would have been sound, and their hypocrisy, which corrupted their hearts and rotted their opinions, would have ended. Reflecting upon the Qur'an, by contemplating it and repeating its verses time after time, leads to knowing truth from falsehood. The most immediate thing they would have understood, had they reflected, is that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah the Exalted and not the speech of a human being, for if it were the speech of a human being they would have found in it contradiction, discord, and inconsistency. But it is the speech of the Creator of humankind; therefore its words are coherent, its expressions and meanings harmonious, and its verses firm, guiding to happiness and perfection. It is thus truly the word of Allah, and whoever is honored by its being sent down upon him is a true messenger. There is no meaning whatsoever in disbelief after this, nor in persisting in it, nor in hypocrisy toward the Muslims concerning it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction.⁠﴾

His saying: ﴿And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it⁠﴾, which is the fourth verse [83]. Allah the Exalted informs of those afflicted with the sickness of hypocrisy, censuring their spreading of rumors and their moral defeatism, saying: ﴿And when there comes to them a report of security or fear⁠—﴾ that is, when news reaches them from the military expeditions of jihad of victory or defeat, they hasten to spread and broadcast it. This is due to the sickness of their hearts. The news is called a "matter" (amr) because the state of war differs from the state of peace. If it is of victory, expressed by "security," they announce it out of envy or greed; and if it is of defeat, expressed by "fear," they announce it out of panic and fright, because they are cowards, as their description has already passed. Allah said, teaching them and teaching others what the fighters should be like in a state of war: ﴿And if they had referred it back to the Messenger⁠﴾, the supreme commander, ﴿and to those of authority among them⁠﴾, who are the commanders of the fighting expeditions, ﴿those who would investigate it from among them would have known it⁠﴾, that is, they would have extracted the secret of the report and understood its consequences. If it was beneficial, they would have spread it; and if it was harmful, they would have kept it from the public.

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy⁠—﴾ O believers ﴿you would have followed Satan⁠﴾ in accepting those malicious rumors and demoralizing announcements ﴿except for a few⁠﴾ among you, from those of sound opinion and mental discernment, for such people are not stirred by claims nor changed by baseless rumors, like the senior Companions from the Emigrants and the Helpers, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to obey the Messenger (ﷺ), for he is not obeyed for his own sake but for the sake of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

2- The obligation to reflect upon the Qur'an in order to strengthen faith.

3- A sign that the Qur'an is the revelation and speech of Allah, evidenced by its freedom from contradiction and discord in its words and meanings.

4- Establishing the principle that news of war is not to be broadcast except by the supreme command, so that disorder does not arise in the ranks of the fighters and the nation as well.

5- Most people are affected by what they hear, except a few of those of sound mental discernment and political awareness.

His saying, the Exalted, in the third verse [82]: ﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?⁠﴾ He rebukes them for their aversion, their ignorance, and their poor understanding, for if they had reflected upon the Qur'an while it was recited to them and they heard it morning and evening, they would have known that the Messenger is true and that what he brought is true. They would have believed and submitted, their Islam would have been sound, and their hypocrisy, which corrupted their hearts and rotted their opinions, would have ended. Reflecting upon the Qur'an, by contemplating it and repeating its verses time after time, leads to knowing truth from falsehood. The most immediate thing they would have understood, had they reflected, is that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah the Exalted and not the speech of a human being, for if it were the speech of a human being they would have found in it contradiction, discord, and inconsistency. But it is the speech of the Creator of humankind; therefore its words are coherent, its expressions and meanings harmonious, and its verses firm, guiding to happiness and perfection. It is thus truly the word of Allah, and whoever is honored by its being sent down upon him is a true messenger. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction.⁠﴾

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 84–86:

Explanation of the words:

Harrid al-mu'minin (حرض المؤمنين): urge them to jihad and incite them to fight.

Ba's alladhina kafaru (بأس الذين كفروا): their military might.

Wa-ashaddu tankilan (وأشد تنكيلاً): stronger in punishment. Tankil (التنكيل) is striking the wrongdoer with force so that he becomes a lesson to his like, and so that he is deterred from wrongdoing.

Al-shafa'a (الشفاعة): intercession (wasatah) in good or in evil. If it is in good, it is a "good intercession" (hasanah); if it is in evil, it is an "evil intercession" (sayyi'ah).

Kifl minha (كفل منها): a share of it.

Muqit (مقيتاً): having power over it, and a witness over it, guarding it.

Bi-tahiyyah (بتحية): the greeting of Islam, which is "as-salamu 'alaykum wa-rahmatullahi wa-barakatuh."

Aw rudduha (أو ردوها): that is, one says "wa-'alaykumu as-salam."

Hasiban (حسيباً): one who calls to account for deeds and repays them, whether with good or with evil.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains on military policy. In this verse, ﴿So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And urge the believers﴾, the Exalted commands His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to fight the polytheists for the sake of raising the word of Allah, that He alone be worshipped and that the persecution of the believers by the polytheists end. This is what is meant by His words ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾. His words ﴿you are not held responsible except for yourself﴾ mean: your Lord does not burden you except with yourself alone; as for others, you are not obligated to compel them to fight. Rather, urge the believers to fight alongside you, so encourage them to do so and make them eager for it. His words ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾ are a promise from Allah, the Exalted, that He will restrain the might of those who disbelieve by empowering His Messenger and the believers against them, so that they will scatter their strength and defeat them, leaving them with no might or power. This has indeed happened, and to Him belongs all praise and grace. He, the Exalted, is ﴿mightier in might﴾ than every possessor of might, ﴿and mightier in punishment﴾ than others in punishing the wrongdoers among His enemies.

This is what the verse [84] indicates. As for the verse [85], which is His saying, ﴿Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share therein, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a portion thereof. And Allah is ever Witness over all things,﴾ it is an informing from Him, the Exalted, that whoever intercedes with a good intercession, by adding his voice to one who demands a right, or by joining himself to a detachment fighting in the cause of Allah, or by interceding for someone to fulfill his need, the intercessor has a portion of the reward and recompense. Likewise, ﴿whoever intercedes with an evil intercession﴾, by supporting falsehood, or interceding for an act of evil, or for abandoning a good deed, will have a share of the burden, because Allah, the Exalted, is Capable over all things, and Watchful and Knowing. This is what the mentioned verse indicates.

As for the last verse [86], Allah, the Exalted, commands His believing servants to return the greeting of one who greets them with something better than it, or, if not better, then with its equal. So whoever says "as-salamu 'alaykum," the one replying should say "wa-'alaykumu as-salam wa-rahmatullah," and whoever says "as-salamu 'alaykum wa-rahmatullah," the one replying should say "wa-'alaykumu as-salam wa-rahmatullahi wa-barakatuh." His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Reckoner﴾ contains reassurance to the believers that Allah, the Exalted, will reward them for their good deeds and recompense them for it.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The demonstration of the courage of the Prophet (ﷺ), by the evidence that he was commanded to fight alone and did so.

2- It is not the right of a ruler to conscript citizens by compulsion; rather, he should urge them to enlist and encourage them to do so by means of encouragement.

3- The virtue of intercession in good, and the ugliness of intercession in evil.

4- Affirmation of the sunnah of greeting, and the obligation to return it with something better or with its equal.

5- Confirmation of what has come in the Sunnah: for "as-salamu 'alaykum" the Muslim receives ten good deeds, for "wa-rahmatullah" ten good deeds, and for "wa-barakatuh" ten likewise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 87–91:

Explanation of the words:

"Lā ilāha illā Huwa" (there is no god but He): there is no one worthy of worship except Him.

"Fi'atayn" (two groups): two parties; the singular is fi'ah, meaning a group.

"Arkasahum" (He returned them to a state of reversal): al-irtikās (reversal) is the transformation from a good condition to a bad one, such as disbelief after belief or treachery after security, and this is what is meant here.

"Sabīlan" (a way): a path to guiding them.

"Waliyyan wa-lā naṣīran" (a protector or a helper): the walī (protector) is one who takes charge of your affairs, and the naṣīr (helper) is one who supports you against your enemy.

"Yaṣilūn" (they join): they become connected to them by virtue of a covenant of treaty between them.

"Mīthāq" (covenant): a pact.

"Ḥaṣirat ṣudūruhum" (their breasts were constricted): they were straitened.

"Al-silm" (peace): submission and compliance.

"Al-fitnah" (strife): polytheism.

"Thaqiftumūhum" (you found them): you found them within your power.

"Sulṭānan mubīnan" (a clear authority): a clear proof for the permissibility of fighting them.

The meaning of the verses:

When Exalted Allah mentioned in the verses before these that He is al-Muqīt (the Sustainer) and al-Ḥasīb (the Reckoner), that is, the One able to call to account and to recompense, He informed, Mighty and Majestic is He, that He is Allah, there is no god but Him, that is, no one is worshipped besides Him, because of His lordship over His creation, for the true god is the one who is Lord, Creator, Provider, Disposer, in whose hand is everything and to whom everything returns. He also informed that He will gather people on a Day about whose coming there is no doubt, which is the Day of Resurrection.

This is what the noble verse indicates: ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.﴾ Since this is a report that includes a promise and a warning, Exalted Allah affirmed its fulfilment, saying: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ O Allah, truly there is no one more truthful than You.

As for the remaining four verses, namely [88], [89], [90] and [91], they were revealed for a specific cause and address particular matters of warfare. The cause of their revelation was the disagreement of the believers among the Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ) concerning a group of hypocrites who displayed Islam while being deeply involved in alliance with the disbelievers. They may have been in Makkah, or they may have been in Madinah. Some Companions saw that prudence required striking at their hands and ending their hypocrisy, while others saw that they should be left alone and patience shown toward them as long as they claimed faith, in the hope that with the passage of days they would repent. When they disagreed and the dispute about them intensified, Exalted Allah revealed these verses, saying: ﴿So what is wrong with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites, when Allah has returned them to reversal because of what they earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And whoever Allah sends astray, you will never find for him a way.﴾ The meaning of the verse is: what has made you into two groups regarding the hypocrites? Allah has returned them to disbelief because of the great sins they committed. Do you, O Muslims, wish to guide those whom Allah has misguided? Can anyone guide one whom Allah has misguided? How could you, when whoever Allah misguides, according to His practice in misguiding people, has no guide and no way to guidance under any circumstances.

Then Exalted Allah informed about the disposition of those hypocrites concerning whom there was disagreement, saying, in the third verse [89]: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be equal.﴾ That is, they love in their hearts your disbelief so that you may be like them. Implied in this is the consequence that Islam would end and disbelief would appear and prevail.

From here Exalted Allah forbade their alliance until they emigrate, saying: ﴿So do not take from among them allies,﴾ upon whom you rely for support against their brethren in disbelief. The apparent context of this indicates that these hypocrites were in Makkah, and that is so. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾ is because emigration to Madinah cuts off their connection with the abode of disbelief, so their resolve weakens and they return to sincerity in their faith and believe. If they emigrate and then turn away from true faith toward hypocrisy and disbelief, then declare war upon them: ﴿Seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them a protector or a helper,﴾ because with their reversal there is no good in them and they are not to be relied upon.

Then in verse [90], the Lord, Exalted is He, exempted from these hypocrites two categories, so they are not to be taken as captives nor fought. The first category is those whom Exalted Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿except those who join﴾, that is, take refuge ﴿with a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾. By their seeking protection with them and asking them for security, you must grant them security so that you do not break your covenant. The second category is a people whose breasts were constricted from fighting you and from fighting their own people. Allah has returned them to disbelief because of the great sins they committed. Do you, O Muslims, wish to guide those whom Allah has misguided? Can anyone guide one whom Allah has misguided? How could you, when whoever Allah misguides, according to His practice in misguiding people, has no guide and no way to guidance under any circumstances.

Then Exalted Allah informed about the disposition of those hypocrites concerning whom there was disagreement, saying, in the third verse [89]: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be equal.﴾ That is, they love in their hearts your disbelief so that you may be like them. Implied in this is the consequence that Islam would end and disbelief would appear and prevail.

From here Exalted Allah forbade their alliance until they emigrate, saying: ﴿So do not take from among them allies,﴾ upon whom you rely for support against their brethren in disbelief. The apparent context of this indicates that these hypocrites were in Makkah, and that is so. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾ is because emigration to Madinah cuts off their connection with the abode of disbelief, so their resolve weakens and they return to sincerity in their faith and believe. If they emigrate and then turn away from true faith toward hypocrisy and disbelief, then declare war upon them: ﴿Seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them a protector or a helper,﴾ because with their reversal there is no good in them and they are not to be relied upon.

Then in verse [90], the Lord, Exalted is He, exempted from these hypocrites two categories, so they are not to be taken as captives nor fought. The first category is those whom Exalted Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿except those who join﴾, that is, take refuge ﴿with a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾. By their seeking protection with them and asking them for security, you must grant them security so that you do not break your covenant. The second category is a people whose breasts were constricted from fighting you and from fighting their own people. These are the ones who did not find it acceptable to fight you or to fight their people. If they withdraw from you and do not fight you, then do not seize them or kill them, and be patient with them, for had Allah willed, He would have empowered them over you and they would have fought you. This second category is the one meant by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿or who come to you with their breasts constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people. And if Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you.﴾ Since Exalted Allah has restrained them from you, restrain yourselves from them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace,﴾ that is, peace and truce, ﴿then Allah has not made for you any way against them﴾ to seize them or fight them.

Beside these there is another category, whose ruling Exalted Allah mentioned in the fifth and last verse, His saying: [91] ﴿You will find others﴾ other than the two previous categories, ﴿who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their own people.﴾ They are thus playing on both ropes, as the saying goes. ﴿Every time they are returned to strife,﴾ that is, to polytheism, ﴿they are plunged back into it,﴾ that is, they fall into it reversed, for they are hypocrites: when they are with you they worship Allah alone, and when they are with their people they worship idols, merely because of a call they are summoned to and answer, and so they revert to polytheism. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Every time they are returned to strife, they are plunged back into it.﴾ And His saying: ﴿So if they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace,﴾ that is, if they do not refrain from fighting you and offer you peace, which is submission and compliance to you, and restrain their hands from fighting you in action, ﴿then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. Those We have given you clear authority against them.﴾ That is, a clear proof for the permissibility of seizing and killing them wherever you have power over them and in whatever circumstance. This is what the five verses indicate, with the knowledge that restraint from fighting polytheists has been abrogated by the verses of Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah), except that the ruler of the Muslims may adopt this system when there is need for it, for it is a divine system which no one has adopted and then been ruined or lost, but this applies outside the Arabian Peninsula, for it is not fitting that two religions should coexist within it.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation of affirming Allah's Oneness in worship.

2. Belief in resurrection and recompense.

3. A wise plan for dealing with the hypocrites according to circumstances and conditions.

4. Confirmation of abrogation (naskh) in the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 92–93:

Explanation of the words:

"Illa khata'an" (except by mistake): that is, except by a killing by mistake, which is that one does not intend to kill, such as one who shoots at game and hits a person.

"Raqaba" (a neck): that is, a slave, whether male or female.

"Musallama" (handed over): paid in full and complete.

"Illa an yassaddaqu" (unless they forgo it): that is, they give it as charity to the killer, so they do not demand it and do not take it from him.

"Mithaq" (covenant): a covenant made firm by oaths.

"Muta'ammidan" (deliberately): intending to kill him, while being unjust to him.

The meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in the preceding verses the fighting of the hypocrites, when it is permissible and when it is not, it was fitting to mention the killing of a believer who is sincere in his faith, whether by mistake or deliberately, and the explanation of its ruling. So in the first verse [92] He, exalted is He, mentioned that it is not fitting for a believer to kill a believer except in the case of error. As for deliberate killing, it does not come from him and is not possible for him while he is a believer, because faith is a light that reveals how ugly the crime of killing a believer is, and what lies behind it of the anger and punishment of Allah, exalted is He. So he does not undertake it. Except in the case of error, for this occurs and happens. The ruling for one who kills by mistake is that he must free a believing slave, male or female, and pay the blood-money (diyah) to the heirs of the slain, unless they forgo it, so they do not demand it and do not accept it. The blood-money is one hundred camels, or one thousand dinars of gold, or twelve thousand dirhams of silver. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake [must free a believing slave and pay blood-money to his family, unless they forgo it]﴾. If the slain is a believer but from a people who are enemies of the Muslims and at war with them, then the obligation on the killer is to free a believing slave only, since blood-money is not given to an enemy who would use it to fight the Muslims. And if the slain is from a people of disbelievers, and he is a believer, or a disbeliever but there is a treaty between us and his people, then the killer must free a slave and pay blood-money handed over to his family. Whoever does not find a slave, then he must fast two consecutive months; that is his repentance, according to His saying: ﴿But whoever does not find [a slave], then fasting two consecutive months as repentance from Allah. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, Knowing of what achieves the benefit of His servants, Wise in His legislation, so He legislates only what is beneficial and not harmful, and what achieves good in the present and the outcome.

This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second [93], it establishes the ruling for one who kills a believer deliberately and unjustly: that expiation does not avail him anything, because Allah, exalted is He, has decreed for him the curse and eternal abiding in Hell, as He said: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, abiding eternally therein, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and prepared for him a great punishment﴾. However, blood-money or retaliation (qisas) is binding unless the heirs of the blood pardon. If they pardon retaliation and accept blood-money, they receive it; and if they demand retaliation, retaliation is carried out, since this is their right. As for the right of Allah, exalted is He, the slain is His servant whom He created to worship Him. Whoever kills him, Allah, the Lord of the servant, is his adversary, and He has threatened him with the most severe and dreadful punishments, and Allah forbid. That is His right. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, abiding eternally therein, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and prepared for him a great punishment﴾.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Clarification that the true believer does not commit deliberate killing of a believer.

2- Clarification of the penalty for accidental killing, which is freeing a slave and paying blood-money handed over to the family.

3- If the slain is a believer but from a people of disbelieving combatants, the penalty is freeing a slave and no blood-money.

4- If the slain is from a people between whom and the Muslims there is a covenant, the obligation is blood-money and freeing a slave.

5- Whoever does not find a slave fasts two consecutive months.

6- Deliberate unjust killing requires one of two things: retaliation or blood-money, according to the wish of the heirs of the blood. If they pardon, that is their right, and their reward is with Allah, exalted is He. The punishment of the Hereafter is a threat: if He wills, He carries it out, and if He wills, He pardons it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 94:

Explanation of the words:

"Idha darabtum" (when you go forth): you set out striking the earth with your feet, as warriors (ghuzat) and travelers.

"Fa-tabayyanu" (then verify): then be certain, so that you do not kill a Muslim whom you take to be a disbeliever.

"Al-salam" (the peace): submission and surrender.

"Tabtaghun" (you seek): you desire.

"Mann Allah 'alaykum" (Allah has bestowed favor upon you): by guidance, so that you were guided and became Muslims.

Meaning of the noble verse:

It is related that a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and encountered a man driving sheep from the tribe of Banu Sulaym. When he saw them, he greeted them, saying, "As-salamu 'alaykum." They said to him, "You only said it out of taqiyya (dissimulation), to protect yourself and your property," and they killed him. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning, when you set out as travelers for raiding and jihad. ﴿Then verify﴾ regarding those you meet on your way, whether they are Muslims, so that you refrain from them, or disbelievers, so that you fight them. ﴿And do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace: "You are not a believer"﴾, meaning one who has declared his Islam to you by the testimony of faith or by the greeting of peace, ﴿seeking the goods of worldly life﴾ by that, meaning its transient wares. So if your aim is the spoils, then with Allah are abundant spoils. So obey Him, make your intention and deeds sincerely for Him, and He will provide for you, grant you spoils, and give you better than what you hope for and aspire to. His saying ﴿Thus were you before﴾ means: like this man whom you killed out of desire for his sheep, you were concealing your faith out of fear of your people. ﴿Then Allah conferred favor upon you﴾ by making His religion manifest and granting you victory, so you no longer had to conceal your religion. Therefore, verify in the future, and do not kill anyone until you are certain of his disbelief. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ is a concluding statement carrying both promise and warning: promise for those who obey, and warning for those who disobey, since the necessary implication of His being All-Knowing of deeds is that He will call to account for them and recompense them, and He is over all things Competent.

Guidance of the verse

Among the guidance of the verse:

1- The legitimacy of traveling in the way of Allah for raiding and jihad.

2- The obligation of verification and clarification in matters where error would cause grave harm.

3- The blame of desire for this world, especially when it conflicts with piety.

4- Taking admonition from the condition of others and learning from similar events.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 95–96:

Explanation of the words:

Ulu al-darar (those with a harm/affliction): they are the blind, the lame, and the sick.

Darajah (a degree): a high rank in Paradise.

Al-husna (the best reward): Paradise.

The meaning of the two verses:

It is narrated that when this verse was revealed in this form, ﴿Those who sit at home among the believers, other than those with a harm, are not equal to those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their selves...﴾ and so on, Ibn Umm Maktum (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "How (can it be), O Messenger of Allah, when I am blind?" He had not moved away before ﴿other than those with a harm﴾ was revealed, and it was inserted between the two parts of ﴿Those who sit at home among the believers﴾ and ﴿and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their selves﴾.

The meaning of the verse: Allah, exalted is He, denies that those who strive with their wealth and their selves are equal in reward and rank with Him to those who do not strive, out of stinginess with their wealth and attachment to their own selves. Allah, exalted is He, excepts those with legitimate excuses, such as the sick and the like; for them is the reward of the strivers even though they do not strive, because of the goodness of their intentions and their inability. Therefore He said, ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best reward﴾, which is Paradise. As for His saying, ﴿Allah has preferred the strivers with their wealth and their selves over those who sit at home﴾, that means: Allah has preferred the strivers with their wealth and selves over those who sit at home with an excuse by a degree, even though all of them will have Paradise, which is the best reward. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Allah has preferred the strivers with their wealth and their selves over those who sit at home﴾ refers to those without an excuse, ﴿a great reward﴾, which is the high degrees together with forgiveness and mercy, because Allah, exalted is He, has always been, from eternity and to eternity, Forgiving and Merciful; therefore He forgave them and showed them mercy. O Allah, forgive us and have mercy on us along with them.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Explaining the excellence of those who strive over other believers who do not strive.

2- People with legitimate excuses attain the reward of the strivers if they have a desire to strive but are unable to do so because of the excuses that afflict them, while the strivers in fact have a degree that is specific to them, not shared by those with excuses.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 97–100:

Explanation of the words:

Tawaffahum (توفاهم): their souls are seized at the end of their terms.

Zalimi anfusihim (ظالمي أنفسهم): by abandoning emigration (hijrah) when it had become obligatory upon them.

Fi-ma kuntum (فيم كنتم): "In what were you?" That is, in what matter of your religion were you?

Masiran (مصيراً): a refuge and a dwelling.

Hilah (حيلة): the ability to change one's situation.

Muragaman (مراغماً): a place and abode for one's emigration, by which one humbles and disgraces those who used to harm him in his home.

Si'ah (وسعة): in provision (rizq).

Waqa'a ajruhu 'ala Allah (وقع أجره على الله): his reward in his emigration has become binding upon Allah, the Exalted.

Meaning of the verses:

Since emigration is among the effects of jihad, it was fitting to mention those who stay behind from it, whether out of necessity or without necessity. So the Exalted addressed emigration and its rulings in these verses, saying: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾, by abandoning emigration and remaining in a land of humiliation, where the enemy oppresses them, prevents them from their religion, and stands between them and the worship of their Lord. To these who wrong themselves, the angels say at the time of taking their souls: ﴿In what were you?﴾ They ask this question because their souls are defiled and dark, since they were not purified through righteous deeds. They reply, making excuses: ﴿We were oppressed in the land﴾, so we were unable to purify our souls through faith and righteous deeds. The angels then reply to their words: ﴿Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could have emigrated therein?﴾ and worshipped your Lord? Then Allah announces His judgment concerning them with His words: those are the distant ones, ﴿whose refuge is Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾, a place to which they go and a dwelling in which they settle.

Then the Exalted made an exception for those with valid excuses, just as He made an exception for them regarding staying back from jihad in the verses before this, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿except the oppressed among men, women, and children﴾. The oppression of men is by illnesses, and of women and children by the weakness inherent in them. These are the ones who ﴿are not able to devise a plan﴾, that is, have no ability to change their situation or move, because of their weakness, ﴿nor are they guided to a way﴾ to the land of emigration, due to their lack of knowledge of the roads and routes. The Exalted gives them hope and expectation with His words: ﴿For those, Allah may pardon them﴾, the ones mentioned, so He will not hold them to account, will forgive them some of what they fell short in, and will show mercy to them for their weakness. And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.

This is what the three verses indicate.

As for the fourth verse [100], Allah the Exalted informs in it that whoever emigrates in His cause, not for a worldly gain he may obtain or a woman he may marry, will find by Allah's permission in the earth a path to go to, a home to settle in, and abundant provision, by which he humbles his enemy who persecuted him until he emigrated from his land. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find on earth many [alternatives] and abundance﴾. Then Allah the Exalted informed that whoever leaves as an emigrant in the cause of Allah, that is, for the sake of His worship and the support of His religion, and then dies on the way of his emigration, even if he does not reach the land of emigration, his reward has become binding upon Allah, and He will fulfill it for him in full, without diminution, and Allah will forgive him any previous shortcoming and show mercy to him, admitting him into His Paradise. For Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has certainly become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of emigration when the believers are prevented from worshipping their Lord, for He created them only for that.

2- Abandoning emigration is one of the major sins, and its doer deserves to enter the Fire.

3- Just as the obligation of jihad falls from those with valid excuses, the obligation of emigration falls from them too.

4- The virtue of emigration in the cause of Allah, the Exalted.

5- Whoever dies on the way of his emigration is given the full reward of an emigrant, without diminution, which is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 101–104:

Explanation of the words:

ضربتم في الأرض (Darabtum fi al-ard): i.e., travelling, a journey of qasr (shortening), which is four barids, that is forty-eight miles.

إن تقصروا من الصلاة (In taqsuru min al-salah): that you pray the two midday prayers two rak'ahs each, and the evening prayer two rak'ahs, because of its length.

إن خفتم أن يفتنكم (In khiftum an yaftinakum): this came out in the form of the usual case, so fear is not a condition for shortening the prayer; the condition is only travel.

حذرهم (Hadharahum): caution and readiness for whatever the enemy may bring about.

وأسلحتكم (Wa aslihatakum): plural of silah, that with which one fights, of various kinds of weapons.

لا جناح عليكم (La junah 'alaykum): i.e., there is no constraint upon you and no hardship in laying down weapons out of necessity.

قضيتم الصلاة (Qadaytum al-salah): you performed it and finished from it.

فإذا اطمأننتم (Fa-idha atma'nantum): i.e., the fear has gone and tranquility has been attained through safety.

كتاباً موقوتا (Kitaban mawqutan): an obligation having a specific time in which it is performed, neither preceding it nor delayed beyond it.

ولا تهنوا (Wa la tahinu): i.e., do not weaken.

تألمون (Ta'lamun): you feel pain (tata'allamun).

Meaning of the verses:

On the occasion of migration, and travel being among its requirements, the Exalted mentioned the concession of shortening the prayer during travel, by reducing the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when you travel in the land﴾ i.e., you journey in it as travellers, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ i.e., no fault or sin, ﴿in shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may afflict you﴾. The Sunnah has explained that the traveller shortens the prayer even if he is safe, so this condition is only the usual case. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾, a concluding statement intended to establish the enmity of the disbelievers towards the believers, and therefore this concession was legislated for them.

This is what the first verse [101] indicates. As for the two verses after it, they explained the prayer of fear and its form: the army divides into two groups. One group stands facing the enemy, and another group prays with the leader one rak'ah. The imam remains in his place, and they complete for themselves one rak'ah, then give the salam and stand facing the enemy. The group that had been standing facing the enemy comes, and the imam leads them in one rak'ah, then gives the salam, and they complete for themselves one rak'ah and give the salam. In both states they hold their weapons and do not lay them on the ground, lest the enemy attack them while they are unarmed and inflict heavy losses upon them. This is the meaning of His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their arms. Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you﴾, meaning the group facing the enemy, to protect them from it. ﴿And let another group who have not prayed come forward and pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their arms﴾. And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would neglect your arms and your belongings so they could attack you in one assault﴾. This statement was brought to explain the reason for praying in groups one after another, and the command to take precaution and carry weapons during prayer. From here the Exalted granted them a concession: if they were sick, or had wounds, or if there was rain that made it difficult for them to carry arms, they could lay down their weapons. So the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you if there is discomfort from rain or if you are ill, to lay down your arms; but take your precaution﴾. And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾ is a concluding statement to an omitted speech indicated by the context; its implied sense may be: "Indeed, the disbelievers are treacherous, their side cannot be trusted, and therefore Allah has prepared for them a humiliating punishment." The apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun to indicate the cause of evil and corruption, which is disbelief.

And His, the Exalted, saying in verse [103]: ﴿So when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾. He, the Exalted, commands the believers to remember Him at all times, especially at the time of meeting the enemy, because of the spiritual strength in that which overcomes and defeats material forces. So the mujahidun do not suffice with remembrance of Allah only in prayer; rather, when they have completed the prayer, they do not abandon the remembrance of Allah in any state. And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿So when you are secure, establish prayer﴾ means: when fear has gone, security has settled, and souls are at rest, establish the prayer with its limits, conditions, and pillars, complete and whole, without the lightening that was present in a state of fear, when one may pray a single rak'ah, or pray by gesture and sign only, which occurs when the mujahidun are locked in combat with their enemies. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been enjoined upon the believers as a decree of specified times﴾ is a reason for the command to establish prayer; it informs that prayer is obligatory upon the believers and that it is fixed to times in which it is to be performed and not otherwise.

And His, the Exalted, saying in verse [104]: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy﴾, i.e., do not be weak in seeking the enemy to bring defeat upon them. And do not make excuses for not pursuing them by claiming that you are in pain from your wounds. ﴿If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer as you suffer; but you hope from Allah﴾ of victory and great reward ﴿that which they do not hope for﴾. So you are more deserving of patience, endurance, and persistence in fighting them until victory over them. And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ contains encouragement for the believers to continue jihad, because their knowledge that Allah, the Exalted, knows their conditions and the circumstances surrounding them, and is Wise in His legislation through commands and prohibitions to them, reassures them of good outcome and of victory over their enemies.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The legitimacy of the prayer of shortening, a concession which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) affirmed by his word and his deed, so it became a confirmed Sunnah that should not be abandoned.

2- The legitimacy of the prayer of fear and the explanation of its manner.

3- The emphasis on congregational prayer, such that it is not abandoned even in the time of fear and fighting.

4- The desirability of remembering Allah after the prayer and in every state: standing, sitting, and lying down.

5- Affirmation of the obligation of prayer and the necessity of performing it at its appointed times.

6- The prohibition of weakness and feebleness in facing the enemy's war, and seeking help in fighting it through remembrance of Allah and hope in Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 101–104:

Explanation of the words:

ضربتم في الأرض (Darabtum fi al-ard): i.e., travelling, a journey of qasr (shortening), which is four barids, that is forty-eight miles.

إن تقصروا من الصلاة (In taqsuru min al-salah): that you pray the two midday prayers two rak'ahs each, and the evening prayer two rak'ahs, because of its length.

إن خفتم أن يفتنكم (In khiftum an yaftinakum): this came out in the form of the usual case, so fear is not a condition for shortening the prayer; the condition is only travel.

حذرهم (Hadharahum): caution and readiness for whatever the enemy may bring about.

وأسلحتكم (Wa aslihatakum): plural of silah, that with which one fights, of various kinds of weapons.

لا جناح عليكم (La junah 'alaykum): i.e., there is no constraint upon you and no hardship in laying down weapons out of necessity.

قضيتم الصلاة (Qadaytum al-salah): you performed it and finished from it.

فإذا اطمأننتم (Fa-idha atma'nantum): i.e., the fear has gone and tranquility has been attained through safety.

كتاباً موقوتا (Kitaban mawqutan): an obligation having a specific time in which it is performed, neither preceding it nor delayed beyond it.

ولا تهنوا (Wa la tahinu): i.e., do not weaken.

تألمون (Ta'lamun): you feel pain (tata'allamun).

On the occasion of migration, and travel being among its requirements, the Exalted mentioned the concession of shortening the prayer during travel, by reducing the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs. The group that had been standing facing the enemy comes, and the imam leads them in one rak'ah, then gives the salam, and they complete for themselves one rak'ah and give the salam. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 105–109:

Explanation of the words:

*bima arakaAllah* (by what Allah has shown you): i.e., by what He taught you through revelation.

*khasiman* (a disputant): i.e., one who argues intensely, to a great degree of contention.

*tujadil* (you dispute): i.e., you contend.

*yakhtanuna anfusahum* (they betray themselves): i.e., they try to betray their own souls.

*yastakhfuna* (they seek to hide): i.e., they seek to conceal themselves from people.

*wa huwa ma'hum* (while He is with them): by His knowledge and His power.

*yubayyitun* (they plot): i.e., they devise a matter in secrecy, with deceit and treachery.

*wakilan* (a guardian): the *wakil* is one who acts on behalf of another to accomplish a purpose.

Meaning of the verses:

It is related that these verses were revealed concerning Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq and his brothers. He had stolen a coat of mail from the house of a neighbour of his called Qatadah, and he deposited it with a Jew called Zayd ibn al-Samin. When Ta'mah was accused and he and his brothers feared the disgrace, they threw the charge onto the Jew and said, "He is the thief." They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and swore to the innocence of their brother, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed them and was about to cut off the Jew's hand because of the testimony of the Banu Ubayriq against him. Then the verses were revealed declaring the Jew's innocence and condemning Ta'mah. When Ta'mah was exposed, and since he was a hypocrite, he declared his apostasy, fled to Makkah the Honoured, and broke into a wall of a house to steal; the wall fell on him and he died beneath it as a disbeliever.

This is the explanation of the verses of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, O Messenger, ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, i.e., by what He has taught you and made you know, not by a mere opinion that someone else, one of the treacherous, had formed. And his Lord, exalted is He, rebuked him by saying: ﴿And do not be a advocate for the treacherous﴾, i.e., one who disputes on their behalf. So Allah, exalted is He, branded the Banu Ubayriq with treachery, because they betrayed themselves by repelling the accusation from themselves with their false oaths. ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what you intended of punishing the Jew, ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, so He will forgive you what you intended and have mercy upon you. ﴿And do not dispute on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, in that they accused the Jew falsely and deceitfully, ﴿indeed, Allah does not love one who is a betrayer and sinful﴾, like Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq. ﴿They conceal themselves from the people﴾, out of shame before them, ﴿but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah﴾, and are not ashamed before Him, and He, exalted is He, is with them at the time when they were plotting how to escape the accusation by attaching it to the innocent Jew, and they resolved to swear to the innocence of their brother and the accusation of the Jew. This speech is something Allah, exalted is He, does not approve. And His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing﴾: what Ta'mah did of stealing the coat of mail and placing it with the Jew, then their accusing the Jew, and their swearing to the innocence of their brother, all of this took place under the knowledge of Allah, and Allah encompasses it. Glorified is He, the God who is All-Knowing, Mighty.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in the worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, i.e., O people, ﴿you argued on their behalf﴾, today in this worldly life, to repel from them the accusation of theft. ﴿But who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, one who undertakes their defence on a Day when no soul can avail another soul anything and the matter is entirely with Allah. This address is directed at those who stood beside the Banu Ubayriq to repel the accusation from them, so Allah rebuked them by His saying: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf﴾. The verse thus contains a severe reproach, so that no one would stand after this in such a shameful position.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- It is not permissible to judge by other than what Allah has sent down in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ).

2- It is not permissible to stand beside treacherous wrongdoers in support of them.

3- The obligation of seeking forgiveness for sin, whether great or small.

4- The obligation to detest the treacherous sinner, whoever he may be.

5- The recommendation of admonition and reminder of the events of the Day of Resurrection.

*tujadil* (you dispute): i.e., you contend.

*yakhtanuna anfusahum* (they betray themselves): i.e., they try to betray their own souls.

*yastakhfuna* (they seek to hide): i.e., they seek to conceal themselves from people.

*wa huwa ma'hum* (while He is with them): by His knowledge and His power.

*yubayyitun* (they plot): i.e., they devise a matter in secrecy, with deceit and treachery.

*wakilan* (a guardian): the *wakil* is one who acts on behalf of another to accomplish a purpose.

Meaning of the verses:

It is related that these verses were revealed concerning Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq and his brothers. He had stolen a coat of mail from the house of a neighbour of his called Qatadah, and he deposited it with a Jew called Zayd ibn al-Samin. When Ta'mah was accused and he and his brothers feared the disgrace, they threw the charge onto the Jew and said, "He is the thief." They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and swore to the innocence of their brother, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed them and was about to cut off the Jew's hand because of the testimony of the Banu Ubayriq against him. Then the verses were revealed declaring the Jew's innocence and condemning Ta'mah. When Ta'mah was exposed, and since he was a hypocrite, he declared his apostasy, fled to Makkah the Honoured, and broke into a wall of a house to steal; the wall fell on him and he died beneath it as a disbeliever.

This is the explanation of the verses of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, O Messenger, ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, i.e., by what He has taught you and made you know, not by a mere opinion that someone else, one of the treacherous, had formed. And his Lord, exalted is He, rebuked him by saying: ﴿And do not be a advocate for the treacherous﴾, i.e., one who disputes on their behalf. So Allah, exalted is He, branded the Banu Ubayriq with treachery, because they betrayed themselves by repelling the accusation from themselves with their false oaths. ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what you intended of punishing the Jew, ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, so He will forgive you what you intended and have mercy upon you. ﴿And do not dispute on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, in that they accused the Jew falsely and deceitfully, ﴿indeed, Allah does not love one who is a betrayer and sinful﴾, like Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq. ﴿They conceal themselves from the people﴾, out of shame before them, ﴿but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah﴾, and are not ashamed before Him, and He, exalted is He, is with them at the time when they were plotting how to escape the accusation by attaching it to the innocent Jew, and they resolved to swear to the innocence of their brother and the accusation of the Jew. This speech is something Allah, exalted is He, does not approve. And His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing﴾: what Ta'mah did of stealing the coat of mail and placing it with the Jew, then their accusing the Jew, and their swearing to the innocence of their brother, all of this took place under the knowledge of Allah, and Allah encompasses it. Glorified is He, the God who is All-Knowing, Mighty.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in the worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, i.e., O people, ﴿you argued on their behalf﴾, today in this worldly life, to repel from them the accusation of theft. ﴿But who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, one who undertakes their defence on a Day when no soul can avail another soul anything and the matter is entirely with Allah. This address is directed at those who stood beside the Banu Ubayriq to repel the accusation from them, so Allah rebuked them by His saying: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf﴾. The verse thus contains a severe reproach, so that no one would stand after this in such a shameful position.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- It is not permissible to judge by other than what Allah has sent down in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ).

2- It is not permissible to stand beside treacherous wrongdoers in support of them.

3- The obligation of seeking forgiveness for sin, whether great or small.

4- The obligation to detest the treacherous sinner, whoever he may be.

5- The recommendation of admonition and reminder of the events of the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 110–113:

Explanation of the words:

Su' (evil): Su': that which harms the self or others.

Aw yazlim nafsahu (or wrongs himself): Wronging the self: by committing sins and perpetrating transgressions.

Ithm (sin): Ithm: that which is harmful to the self and corrupting.

Bari' (innocent): Bari': one who has not committed a crime for which he has been accused.

Ihtamala buhtanan (bears a slander): Tahammala buhtanan: that is, a lie which bewilders the one it is thrown at.

Al-Kitab wal-Hikmah (the Book and the Wisdom): al-Kitab: the Qur'an, and al-Hikmah: the Sunnah.

Meaning of the verses:

This passage follows on from the preceding one concerning the incident of Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, and it carries God's mercy toward those who were drawn into standing alongside the traitor, Ibn Ubayriq. God informs them that whoever does evil that harms another, or wrongs himself by committing some sin, and then repents to God by seeking His forgiveness and turning to Him, God will accept his repentance and forgive him. This is the meaning of His words in verse [110]: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning He will forgive him and show him mercy.

His words ﴿And whoever earns a sin﴾, i.e., any sin, minor or major, ﴿then he earns it only against himself﴾, for it is the self that is stained by it and held accountable for its consequence if He does not forgive it. Another's self is not held accountable for it. ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing﴾, i.e., of the sins of His servants, ﴿Wise﴾, i.e., in recompensing them for their sins, so He does not hold a soul accountable for other than what it has earned, and He does not leave a soul that has earned [sin] unaccountable.

In verse [112], God informs that whoever commits a wrong against someone, or earns a sin and throws it at an innocent person who is free of it, has borne a grave burden which may cast him into the Fire of Hell. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And whoever earns a fault or sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾.

In verse [113], God addresses His Messenger, bestowing favour upon him for the grace and mercy He has granted him, saying: ﴿And if not for the favour of Allah upon you and His mercy, a faction of them would have resolved to mislead you, but they mislead none except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all﴾. The faction mentioned by God is the Banu Ubayriq, the brothers of Ta'mah. His words ﴿but they mislead none except themselves﴾: as He, Mighty and Majestic, said, their misguidance returns upon them, whereas the Messenger will not be harmed by it. His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you has been magnificent﴾ are a favour from God upon His Messenger, that He sent down to him the Qur'an, the greatest and most guiding of books, and taught him wisdom, which is what was revealed to him of the secrets of the noble Book, and the knowledge and insights revealed to him, all of which are light and clear guidance, and taught him divine knowledge that he had not known before. By this His favour upon His Messenger was magnificent. So to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the principle that repentance erases what came before it, and whoever repents, Allah accepts his repentance.

2- The gravity of the sin of one who lies against the innocent and accuses the trustworthy of treachery.

3- The influence of speech upon souls, to the point that the Messenger ﷺ nearly was misled by the Banu Ubayriq into clearing the traitor and condemning the innocent, but Allah protected him.

4- The consequence of wrongdoing returns upon the wrongdoer.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 114–115:

Explanation of the words:

Najwahum (their secret talk): al-najwa (secret conversation) is speaking privately; najwahum means their discussions which some of them confide to others.

Aw ma'ruf (or a good deed): al-ma'ruf (what is good and known) is that which the Shari'ah has recognized and permitted, or recommended, or made obligatory.

Ibtigha'a mardat Allah (seeking the pleasure of Allah): that is, seeking the pleasure of Allah, i.e., to obtain the good pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Nu'tihi (We will give him): We will grant him. Al-ajr al-'azim (the great reward): Paradise and the lasting bliss within it.

Yushaqiq al-Rasul (opposes the Messenger): he opposes him, cuts himself off from him, and is hostile to him, like one who stands on one side while the other stands on the opposite side.

Wa yattaba' ghayr sabil al-mu'minin (and follows other than the way of the believers): that is, he departs from the consensus (ijma') of the Muslims.

Nuwallihi ma tawalla (We will leave him to what he has chosen): We will forsake him, leaving him to what he has taken up of falsehood, evil and error, until he perishes therein.

Nuslihi Nar Jahannam (and burn him in the Fire of Hell): that is, We will cause him to enter the Fire and burn therein.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context still concerns the Banu Ubayriq. In the first verse [114], Allah, Exalted, informs that there is no good in much of their secret talk, because of their hypocrisy and the evil of their inner intentions, except in the talk of one who enjoins charity given to a Muslim in need, or a good deed which the Lawgiver has recommended or made obligatory of righteousness and kindness, or reconciliation between people in order to preserve harmony and affection among the Muslims. Then Allah, Exalted, informs that whoever does what has been mentioned of charity, good deeds and reconciliation between people, seeking the pleasure of Allah, Exalted, He will surely reward him with the best reward, which is Paradise, the abode of peace, for there is no reward greater than a reward that is Paradise.

This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second [115], Allah, Exalted, threatens the likes of Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, saying, may His majesty be remembered: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, that is, contradicts and is hostile to him, ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾, that is, after he has known that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, who came with guidance and the religion of truth. Then he, along with his hostility to the Messenger, departs from the community of the Muslims and follows other than their way, this wretched loser. ﴿We will leave him to what he has chosen﴾, that is, We will leave him in his disbelief and error, forsaking him in this world, then ﴿We will burn him in Hell﴾, where he will be scorched, and wretched is the destination, Hell, to which a person goes and in which he remains forever.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of a private conversation between two to the exclusion of a third, since this is established in the Sunnah.

2- Secret gatherings contain no good, except a gathering held to collect charity, or to enjoin good, or to reconcile disputing Muslims.

3- The prohibition of departing from Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah and following the misguided sects that represent Islam only in narrow circles, such as the Rafidah and others.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 116–121:

Explanation of the words:

"An yushrika bihi" (that He be associated with): that He be worshipped alongside other than Him, of His creatures, with any form of worship whatsoever.

"In yad'una" (they do not invoke): i.e., what they invoke.

"Illa inathan" (except females): plural of unthā (female), because the deities are feminine; or "except dead things," because the dead is called by the word unthā, on the common ground of lacking any benefit.

"Mariden" (defiant): meaning one who rebels against good and seduces to corruption.

"Nasiban mafrudan" (a specified portion): a particular share, or a known allotment.

"Falayubattunna" (they will surely cut off): i.e., they will surely slit.

"Khalq Allah" (the creation of Allah): the creature of Allah, i.e., what Allah the Exalted has created.

"Ash-shaytan" (the Devil): the wicked, cunning one who calls to evil, whether he be a jinn or a human.

"Yumanniihim" (he arouses in them desires): he makes them wish for this and that, in order to distract them from righteous deeds.

The meaning of the verses:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ is a statement from Him, the Exalted, about Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, that He will not forgive him, because he died in shirk. As for his brothers who did not die as polytheists, their matter is with Allah, the Exalted: if He wills, He forgives them, and if He wills, He punishes them, like the rest of the perpetrators of sins other than shirk and kufr. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾ means he has strayed from the path of salvation and happiness by his great distance from the truth, and that is by his associating others, of His creatures, with his Lord, the Exalted.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They invoke instead of Him none but females﴾ is an explanation of the ugliness of shirk and the evil state of its people. He, the Exalted, informs that the polytheists worship only dead things that neither hear, nor see, nor speak, nor understand, since their idols are dead, and everything dead is feminine, in addition to their names being feminine, such as al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat and Na'ilah. Likewise, in reality they invoke a defiant devil, since it is he who called them to worship idols, so they worshipped them; thus they are, in the inner reality, worshippers of the Devil and not of the idols. Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they invoke none but a defiant devil﴾, cursed by Allah and driven to despair when he refused to prostrate to Adam. ﴿He said, "I will surely take from among Your servants a specified portion"﴾, meaning a great number of them who will worship me and not worship You; they are known and recognized by their disobedience to You and their obedience to me.
