Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 122:

Explanation of the words:

"Āmanū" (believed): they affirmed belief in Allah and His Messenger.

"Wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt" (and did righteous deeds): acts of obedience, since every act of obedience to Allah and His Messenger is a righteous deed.

"Qīlā" (a statement): that is, a saying.

The meaning of the noble verse:

When Allah, the Exalted, explained the recompense of polytheism and of the polytheists, the worshippers of Satan, He explained in this verse the recompense of monotheism and of the monotheists, the servants of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic. He, the Exalted, will admit them after their death into gardens beneath which rivers flow, from beneath their palaces and trees, and that their abiding therein is decreed by the permission of their Lord; they will never come out of it. Their Lord has promised them this as a true promise, and there is none more truthful in promise or in speech than Allah, the Exalted.

Lessons of the verse

From the lessons of the verse:

1- Sincere faith and sound, righteous action are the key to Paradise and the cause of entering it.

2- The truthfulness of Allah's promise, and the truthfulness of His saying, Mighty and Majestic.

3- The obligation on the servant to keep his promises, because breaking a promise is a sign of hypocrisy, according to the hadith: "And when he promises, he breaks it." 4- The obligation of truthfulness in speech and narration, because lying is a sign of hypocrisy, according to the hadith: "And when he speaks, he lies."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 123–126:

Explanation of the words:

Amaniyyakum (your wishful desires): plural of umniyyah (wishful desire), which is what a person determines in himself and longs for, but which is generally difficult to achieve.

Ahl al-kitab (People of the Book): the Jews and the Christians.

Su'an (evil): everything that harms through sins and wrongdoings.

Waliyyan (protector): one who takes charge of his affairs and repels what is disliked.

Naqiran (a speck): the naqir is a small pit on the back of a date stone.

Millat Ibrahim (the religion of Abraham): worshipping Allah alone, without partner, in accordance with what Allah has legislated.

Khalilan (intimate friend): the khalil is the beloved whose love penetrates the pathways of the soul; it is greater than the habib (beloved).

Muhituan (encompassing): in knowledge and power, since the whole universe is under His dominion and revolves by His power and knowledge.

Meaning of the verses:

It is narrated that this verse was revealed when a Muslim and a Jew quarrelled and boasted against each other. The Jew claimed that their prophet, their book and their religion came before the prophet, book and religion of the Muslims, and therefore they were superior. The Muslim refuted him with what is true, and Allah judged between them by His saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful desires﴾, O Muslims, ﴿nor by the wishful desires of the People of the Book﴾, meaning the Jews and Christians. That is, the matter is not decided by wishes, and the matter in this case is rather Allah's sunnah concerning the effect of voluntary action upon the soul, either by purification or by corruption. Whoever does evil, of shirk and disobedience, will be repaid according to it, just as whoever does good, of tawhid and acts of obedience, will be repaid according to it. Evil corrupts the soul and deprives it of companionship with the righteous, while tawhid and righteous deeds purify it and qualify it for companionship with the righteous and keep it far from companionship with the wicked. As for His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾, this is because Allah's sunan, like His rulings, cannot be changed or altered by anyone; rather they proceed as they are. So no one benefits the person of evil, and no one harms the person of good deeds. As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even as much as a speck﴾, this affirms His sunnah concerning the effect of acquisition upon the soul, and the recompense according to the state of the soul, in purity and purification or in corruption and defilement. Whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer purifies his soul, whether male or female, and thereby becomes qualified to enter Paradise, and he will not be wronged even a speck, let alone more than that, great or large.

His saying: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾ is an honouring by Him, the Exalted, and a preference of the Islamic religion over all other religions, since it is founded upon submitting one's face to Allah, with all the limbs following it and revolving in the orbit of obedience to Allah, together with complete excellence (ihsan), which is perfecting worship and performing it in the manner Allah has prescribed, and following the religion of Abraham by worshipping Allah alone and rejecting all other deities. His saying ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾ further affirms the excellence of Islam, which is the religion of Abraham, whom his Lord took as an intimate friend.

His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing﴾ is, in addition, an announcement of the vastness of Allah's dominion, the vastness of His knowledge, power and bounty. It removes what might be suspected from the intimate friendship of Abraham, namely that Allah is in need of Abraham or has any need for him. He informs that to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, by creation and by ownership, and Abraham is among that. How then could He be in need of him, or require someone like him, when He is the Lord and Owner of all things?

Guidance from the verses:

1- What is with Allah is not attained by wishful desire, but by faith and righteous deeds, or piety, patience and excellence.

2- Recompense is the natural result of action, and this is the meaning of ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ and ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise﴾.

3- The excellence of Islam over all other religions.

4- The honour of Abraham, peace be upon him, through his Lord taking him as an intimate friend.

5- Allah's independence from all His creatures, and the dependence of all His creatures upon Him, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 127–130:

Explanation of the words:

Yastaftunaka (they ask you for a ruling): they ask you for a legal opinion concerning women and their inheritance.

Wa ma yutla alaykum (and what is recited to you): what is recited to you in the Qur'an.

Ma kutiba lahunna (what was prescribed for them): what was made obligatory for them of dowries and inheritance.

Bil-qist (with justice): with fairness.

Nushuzan (ill-will): haughtiness and disobedience.

Wa uhdirat al-anfusu al-shuhha (and souls have been made to be prone to stinginess): human souls have been created with stinginess, which never leaves them.

Fa tadharuha ka-l-mu'allaqa (so you leave her as one suspended): so you leave her neither married nor divorced.

Min sa'atihi (from His abundance): from His wide provision.

Wa kana Allahu wasi'an hakiman (and God is All-Encompassing, All-Wise): abounding in grace and wise, He gives His grace according to His knowledge and wisdom.

The meaning of the verses:

Each of these four verses carries a specific legal ruling. The first [127] was revealed in response to questions from some Companions about the rights of women, what they are entitled to and what is owed by them, because the custom prevailing in the Jahiliyyah completely denied women and children inheritance, and orphans were not given consideration or full protection of their rights. Therefore the first verses of this surah were revealed, establishing the right of women and children to inheritance and urging the preservation of orphans' property. The questions multiplied, perhaps some Qur'an would be revealed in answer to them, and their souls were agitated when it was revealed, so this noble verse returns them to what is at the beginning of the surah, and that it is the final judgment on the matter, so there is no further review after it. God, Exalted, said while addressing His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿They ask you concerning women﴾, meaning: they continued asking you about women, that is, concerning what is due to them and what is owed by them of rights such as inheritance and dowry and so on. Say to them, O Messenger: ﴿God gives you a ruling concerning them﴾, and He has already given you a ruling concerning them and has explained to you what is due to them and what is owed by them. And His saying, Exalted: ﴿And what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women, whom you do not give what was prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry﴾, meaning: what is recited to you concerning orphan women at the beginning of the surah is sufficient for you, and you do not need anyone else to give you a ruling, for it has made clear to you that whoever has an orphan girl under his guardianship who is unattractive, and he does not desire to marry her, let him give her her property and let him marry her to someone else, and let him marry whomever he wishes. It is not lawful for him to keep her in his house for the sake of her property. And if she is beautiful and he wishes to marry her, let him give her the dowry of her equals and not withhold anything of her dowry. His saying ﴿and the oppressed among the children﴾, meaning: He has already given you a ruling by what is recited to you of the verses at the beginning of the surah concerning the oppressed among the children, for He has given them their full right in the verse ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [An-Nisa': 11], and so on.

Why these repeated reviews and questions? And His saying: ﴿and that you establish justice for orphans﴾, meaning: what is recited to you at the beginning of the surah commanded you to act justly toward orphans and be fair in their property, so return to His saying: ﴿And give the orphans their property, and do not substitute the bad for the good, and do not consume their property along with your own property. Indeed, that is a great sin﴾ [An-Nisa': 2]. And His saying at the end of the verse: ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it﴾ is an exhortation to them to do good by kindness to the two weak ones, the woman and the orphan, in addition to fulfilling their rights in full and not infringing upon them.

This is what the noble verse ﴿They ask you…﴾ etc. indicates.

As for the second verse [128]: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between them, and settlement is best﴾. It contains a just and merciful ruling and a firm divine guidance: that when a wife anticipates from her husband ill-treatment, that is haughtiness toward her, or aversion from her, whether because of her advanced age or her lack of beauty, and he has married another woman over her, it is possible for them to reach a settlement that preserves her staying in her house honored and respected, so she relinquishes to him some of her right in the bed and some of what was obligatory for her. This is better for her than separation. Therefore He, Exalted, said: ﴿and settlement is best﴾. His saying ﴿and souls have been made prone to stinginess﴾ means that stinginess is inherent in the human soul and does not leave it, and the woman is like the man in this, except that the woman is more reluctant and stingy regarding her share in the bed and her other rights from her husband. Therefore the husband should take this into account, and so He said: ﴿And if you do good﴾, O husbands, to your wives, ﴿and fear God﴾ concerning them, ﴿so do not deprive them of what is their right in the bed and otherwise, for God will repay you with excellence for excellence and good for good, for He is ﴿Acquainted with what you do﴾.

This is what the verse [128] indicates. As for the third verse [129], which is His saying, Exalted: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely [away from one] and leave her [as it were] suspended. And if you amend and fear God, indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, it contains a great truth: the husband's inability to be equitable among his wives who are under his marriage. However much he strives for justice and seeks it, he will never reach its ultimate limit. The justice meant here is in love and intercourse. As for division, clothing, food and kind treatment, this is within his capacity, and since God knew this about His servant, He allowed him this and did not hold him accountable for his inclination of the soul, as the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "O God, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not." What is forbidden to the husband is complete inclination toward one of his wives to the exclusion of the rest, because that leads to the believing woman being in a state where she is neither married enjoying marital rights nor divorced so that she may marry another man and be happy with her rights with him. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿so you leave her as one suspended﴾. And His saying: ﴿And if you amend﴾, meaning, O husbands, in your actions and in the division among your wives, ﴿and fear God in that﴾, so do not incline completely, and do not act unjustly in what you are able to be just in. He, Exalted, will forgive you what you were unable to accomplish due to your weakness, and will have mercy on you in your worldly life and your Hereafter, for God, Exalted, was and still is Forgiving to the repentant and Merciful to the believers.

This is what the third verse indicates. As for the fourth verse [130], which is His saying, Exalted: ﴿And if they separate, God will enrich each of them from His abundance, and God is ever All-Encompassing and Wise﴾, God, Exalted, promises the spouses who were not granted success in reconciling, because each of them is stingy with his or her property and unwilling to yield anything of it, that if they separate in a fair manner, He will enrich each of them from His abundance, and He is the All-Encompassing, the Wise. So God gives the woman a husband better than the one she left, and likewise gives the man a wife better than the one he separated from, since reconciliation between them was impossible.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the principle of inheritance for women and children, preserving the property of orphans, and the prohibition of consuming it.

2- The recommendation of reconciliation between spouses when remaining together is impossible without it.

3- Since equality between spouses in love and intercourse is impossible, the Lawgiver does not hold one accountable for it, and requires only equality in bed, food, drink, clothing, and kind treatment.

4- Encouragement toward reconciliation, piety, and doing good deeds.

5- Separation between spouses, if based on reconciliation and piety, brings good, sooner or later.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 131–134:

Explanation of the words:

"And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth": that is, creation, dominion, disposal and management.

"And We have instructed": We made a covenant with them concerning this, that is, concerning taqwa (God-consciousness).

"Those who were given the Scripture": the Jews and the Christians.

"Al-Wakil (the Disposer of affairs)": the one to whom the whole matter is entrusted and who manages it in the best manner.

"Reward of this world": the recompense of works done for it.

"Reward of the Hereafter": the recompense of works done for it, which is Paradise.

"Hearing and seeing": Samee' (All-Hearing) of the words of His servants, Baseer (All-Seeing) of their deeds, and He will recompense them for them with good or evil.

The meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, blessed and exalted, promised each of the two separated spouses enrichment from the other, He mentioned that He owns whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and therefore He is able to enrich them both, by the vastness of His dominion and the greatness of His bounty. Then He addressed the whole community with the noble address, including the Banu Ubayriq, saying: ﴿And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, meaning the Jews, the Christians and others, instructing them to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so that they do not oppose Him or depart from His obedience by abandoning what He made obligatory or doing what He forbade. Then He informed them that even if they disbelieve, as Ta'mah disbelieved and apostatized, that does not harm Him in the least, because He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. And how could it, when to Him belongs everything in the heavens and the earth of beings and creatures, and He is their Lord, their Owner, and the One who disposes of them.

This is what the first verse [131] contains. As for the second verse [132], Allah repeats in it the declaration of His right to praise and self-sufficiency, because He owns all that is in the heavens and the earth, and because He is their Sustainer over them, and sufficient is He as Guardian and Disposer.

In the third verse [133], Allah informs that He is able to remove the entire human race and replace it with others, and He is over all things competent. So He said: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away, O mankind, and bring others﴾, and that is due to His great power and the sufficiency of His being the Disposer.

In the fourth and last verse in this context [134], Allah says, encouraging His servants toward what is with Him of good in this world and the Hereafter: whoever desires by his work the reward of this world, ﴿then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾. So the servant should not restrict his work to the reward of this world, for he knows that the reward of the Hereafter is also with Allah; let him seek both rewards together from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by faith, taqwa and excellence in conduct. He will recompense him for his deed and will not diminish it for him, because of His knowledge and power. ﴿And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing﴾. Whoever is so, no fear of the loss of his deeds accompanies him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The instruction to taqwa, by abandoning shirk and sins after faith and doing righteous deeds.

2- Allah's independence from all His creation.

3- Allah's power to remove all people and bring others in their place.

4- The obligation of sincerity in work for Allah, and the prohibition of seeking the Hereafter by seeking worldly gain.

"Reward of this world": the recompense of works done for it.

"Reward of the Hereafter": the recompense of works done for it, which is Paradise.

"Hearing and seeing": Samee' (All-Hearing) of the words of His servants, Baseer (All-Seeing) of their deeds, and He will recompense them for them with good or evil.

The meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, blessed and exalted, promised each of the two separated spouses enrichment from the other, He mentioned that He owns whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and therefore He is able to enrich them both, by the vastness of His dominion and the greatness of His bounty. Then He informed them that even if they disbelieve, as Ta'mah disbelieved and apostatized, that does not harm Him in the least, because He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. As for the second verse [132], Allah repeats in it the declaration of His right to praise and self-sufficiency, because He owns all that is in the heavens and the earth, and because He is their Sustainer over them, and sufficient is He as Guardian and Disposer.

In the third verse [133], Allah informs that He is able to remove the entire human race and replace it with others, and He is over all things competent. He will recompense him for his deed and will not diminish it for him, because of His knowledge and power. ﴿And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing﴾. Whoever is so, no fear of the loss of his deeds accompanies him.

1- The instruction to taqwa, by abandoning shirk and sins after faith and doing righteous deeds.

2- Allah's independence from all His creation.

3- Allah's power to remove all people and bring others in their place.

4- The obligation of sincerity in work for Allah, and the prohibition of seeking the Hereafter by seeking worldly gain.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 135–137:

Explanation of the words:

*Qawwamin* (قوامين): plural of *qawwam*, one who frequently stands firm in justice.

*Bil-qist* (بالقسط): with justice, which is uprightness and even-handedness between the disputing parties.

*Shuhada'* (شهداء): plural of *shahid*, meaning witness.

*Al-hawa* (الهوى): the inclination of the soul towards a thing and its desire for it.

*Talwu* (تلووا): that is, you twist your tongues with the utterance, distorting it so that the testimony is not completed in its proper form.

*Tu'ridu* (تعرضوا): you abandon the testimony, or some of its words, so that the ruling is nullified.

Meaning of the verses:

God the Exalted says in this verse [135]: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice⦆, that is, with justice, ﴿witnesses for God⦆. For by your testimony a right passes from one person to another, since your Lord has appointed you as His witnesses on earth, through whom rights are rendered to their people. On this basis, establish testimony for God, even if it is against yourselves, your parents, or those closest to you, and whether the one against whom testimony is given is rich or poor. Let neither the wealth of the rich nor the poverty of the poor lead you to distort or conceal the testimony, for God is closer to both of them, and He gives and withholds by your testimony. So establish it, and that is sufficient for you. Know that if you twist your tongues with the testimony, distorting it and taking it out of fulfilling what follows from it, or you turn away from it, abandoning it or leaving out some of its words so that its meaning is corrupted and its effect is nullified, then God is aware of your deed and of other than it, and He will recompense you for it, punishing you in this world or in the Hereafter. Beware!

This noble verse applies first and foremost to those who testified for the sons of Ubayriq as being Muslims and righteous. It is also an address to the believers until the Day of Resurrection, and it is the greatest verse in this regard, so let the believers fear God in their testimony.

As for the second verse [136]: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in God⦆. It is addressed to the People of the Book in particular and to all believers in general. For the believers, it calls them to strengthen their faith so that they may reach the level of certainty. As for the People of the Book, it is a call to them to adopt correct faith, because the faith they hold is not sound; therefore they were called to correct belief, and it was said to them: ﴿believe in God and His Messenger⦆, Muhammad, ﴿and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger⦆, which is the noble Qur'an, ﴿and the Book which He sent down before⦆, which is the Torah and the Gospel, because the Jews do not believe in the Gospel. Then He informed them, warning them, that ﴿whoever disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has strayed⦆ from the path of guidance and happiness, ﴿a far straying⦆, whose guidance is not to be hoped for. Accordingly, he will perish and suffer an everlasting loss.

Then, in the verse after this [137], God the Exalted informed them, confirming the judgment of loss contained in the preceding verse, and said, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved⦆ in Muhammad ﷺ, his Book, and what he brought, ﴿God would not⦆, that is, it is not in God's way that He should forgive them, nor guide them to a path by which they would be saved and made happy. Let the Jews and Christians beware of this and remember it, for otherwise, eternal dwelling in the Fire of Hell is binding upon them, and none is destroyed before God except one who is destined for destruction.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of justice in judgment and testimony.

2- The prohibition of false testimony, and the prohibition of withholding testimony from one upon whom it has become obligatory.

3- The obligation of persisting in faith, strengthening it, and dying upon it.

4- An explanation of the pillars of faith, which are belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day.

5- The apostate is given three days to repent, and otherwise is killed as a disbeliever, derived from His saying: ﴿then believed, then disbelieved⦆.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 138–141:

Explanation of the words:

Bashshir al-munafiqin (give glad tidings to the hypocrites): al-bishara (glad tidings) is news that affects the skin of the one who receives it, whether good or bad. Al-munafiq (the hypocrite) is one who conceals disbelief and displays faith out of taqiyya (dissimulation, i.e., concealing one's belief under pressure) in order to protect his blood and property.

Awliya' (allies): they show them love and support against the believers.

Al-izza (honour): dominance and protection.

Yustahza' biha (they are mocked): they are denigrated, belittled, denied and rejected.

Yakhudu (they engage): they speak about another topic of conversation.

Mithluhum (like them): that is, in disbelief and sin.

Yatarabbasuna bikum (they wait for you): they wait to see when a defeat or breakdown will befall you, so that they may then declare their disbelief.

Nasib (a share): that is, of victory; it is described as a "share," a small portion, because their victory over the believers is rare.

Nastahwidh 'alaykum (we gained dominance over you): that is, we took control over you and protected you from the believers if they fought you.

Sabilan (a way): that is, a path to humiliating them, enslaving them and dominating them.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Give the hypocrites the tidings that there is for them a painful punishment﴾. God Most High commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to inform the hypocrites using the expression "tidings," because what is conveyed will distress their faces: it is a painful punishment, which may occur in this world through humiliation, degradation and killing, while in the Hereafter it is the worst and most severe punishment, and it is necessary for them because of the corruption of their souls and the darkness of their spirits. Then God Most High described them with their basest and worst qualities, saying: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾, so they give their love, support and loyalty to the disbelievers and withhold these from the believers. This is because their hearts are disbelieving and sinful; faith has not entered them, and the practice of Islam has not illuminated them. Then God Most High rebuked them, censuring their ignorance, saying: ﴿Do they seek honour with them?﴾ That is, do they seek honour, meaning protection and dominance, from the disbelievers? Are they ignorant, or blind, so that they do not recognise [the truth]? ﴿Indeed, all honour belongs to God﴾. Whoever God honours is honoured, and whoever He humiliates is humiliated. Honour is sought through faith and righteous deeds, not through disbelief, evil and corruption. This is what the first two verses [138] and [139] indicate.

As for the fourth verse [140], God Most High disciplines the believers by reminding them of what He sent down to them in Surat al-An'am, where He forbade them to sit with the people of falsehood when they engage in disparaging God's signs and His religion. He Most High said: ﴿When you see those who engage in mockery of Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in another topic of discourse. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-An'am: 68]. God Most High instructed His Messenger and the believers with this discipline while they were in Mecca before the Hijra, since Surat al-An'am is Meccan. When they emigrated to Medina, hypocrisy emerged and the hypocrites had private gatherings in which they criticised the believers and engaged in discussing God's signs with mockery and derision. God Most High reminded the believers of what He had sent down to them in Mecca, saying: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another topic of discourse. Indeed, in that case you would be like them﴾, that is, if you are content to sit with them while they engage in mockery of God's signs, ﴿like them﴾ in sin, crime and also in punishment. ﴿Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾. So, do you wish to be with them in Hell? If you say no, then do not sit with them.

Then God Most High mentioned another attribute of the hypocrites, which conveys warning against them, aversion and hatred of them, saying: ﴿Those who wait in suspense over you﴾, that is, they await misfortunes for you and watch for opportunities. ﴿If there is a victory for you from God﴾, that is, a triumph and spoils, they say: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾, so give us a share of the spoils. ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾ in victory, they say to them: ﴿Did we not gain dominance over you﴾, that is, take control over you, ﴿and protect you from the believers﴾ from fighting you? So give us some of what you have seized. Thus the hypocrites hold the staff in the middle; whichever side prevails, they are with it. Surely the curse of God is upon the hypocrites. The believers have nothing but patience, for the problem of the hypocrites is difficult to resolve; God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbelievers who are openly dominant, God Most High will never grant them a way over the believers, neither for their extermination and annihilation, nor for their humiliation and domination over them, so long as the believers are sincere in their faith. This is what God Most High concluded the noble verse with, when He said: ﴿And God will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers.

2. The motive that leads people to take disbelievers as allies is the desire for honour and the removal of humiliation; this is false, for honour belongs to God and is sought only from Him, through faith and adherence to His way.

3. The prohibition of sitting with the people of falsehood when they engage in criticism, mockery and derision of God's signs.

4. Contentment with disbelief is disbelief, and contentment with sin is sin.

5. God Most High guarantees the honour and protection of sincere believers, so that He does not give His enemies power over them to annihilate them, or to humiliate them and dominate them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 142–143:

Explanation of the words:

Yukhadi'un Allah (they deceive Allah): by displaying what He loves, which is faith and acts of obedience, and concealing disbelief and acts of disobedience.

Wa huwa khadi'uhum (and He is the one who deceives them): by veiling them and not exposing them, and by not sending punishment upon them.

Yura'un (they show off): that is, they display acts of obedience before the believers as though they were believers, while they are not believers.

Mudhabdhabin (wavering): that is, they waver between the believers and the disbelievers, so they incline to whichever side is strong and they are with it.

The meaning of the two verses:

He, the Exalted, informs that the hypocrites, in their private conduct, deceive Allah, the Exalted, by displaying faith in Him and in His Messenger while they are not believers. Deception means that you show the one you deceive what he loves from you and conceal from him what he dislikes. Allah, the Exalted, has dealt with them in kind: He has shown them what they love and has concealed from them what He dislikes for them, which is the punishment prepared for them, sooner or later. He also informs about them that when they stand up to perform the prayer, they stand lazily and sluggishly, because they do not believe in the reward of the Hereafter. Therefore they show off their good deeds to the believers, so that they will not accuse them of disbelief. Likewise, they do not remember Allah except a little, both within the prayer and outside it, and that is because of their lack of faith in Allah and their lack of love for Him. He also informs that they are wavering between disbelief and faith, and between the believers and the disbelievers: they do not settle with the believers in faith, nor do they settle with the disbelievers and hypocrites. Thus they are constantly in hesitation and regret. This is the state of one whom Allah has led astray, for whoever Allah leads astray, there is no way to guide him.

Lessons from the two verses:

From the lessons of the two verses:

1- Explanation of the characteristics of the hypocrites.

2- The ugliness of showing off and the blame of those who show off.

3- Blame for abandoning the remembrance of Allah and reducing it, given His command to increase it in His words: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41].

4- Blame for indecision and wavering in all matters.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 144–147:

Explanation of the words:

"Sultanan mubinan" (a clear authority): a manifest proof for punishing you.

"Al-dark al-asfal" (the lowest level): al-dark is like a floor (tabaq), and al-darakah is like a degree (daraja).

"Wa aslahu" (and they reform): what they had corrupted of beliefs and deeds.

"Wa'tasimu billah" (and hold fast to Allah): hold fast to His religion and put your trust in Him.

"Wa akhlasu dinahum lillah" (and devote their religion to Allah): free themselves from hypocrisy (nifaq) and polytheism (shirk).

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns Allah the Exalted guiding the believers to what honours them, perfects them and makes them happy. In this verse [144], He addresses them by the title of faith, which is the spirit through which there is life, and forbids them from taking the disbelievers as allies (awliya') instead of the believers. He says: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. Taking them as allies means showing them affection, supporting them, trusting them, relying on them and cooperating with them. Since the matter carries complete danger for them, Allah the Exalted threatened them by saying: ﴿Do you wish to give Allah a manifest authority against you?﴾ That is, He would abandon you, and set His enemies, the disbelievers, over you, so they would uproot you, or subdue and humiliate you and rule over you. Then He warned them against hypocrisy seeping into their hearts, so He made them hear His just judgment concerning the hypocrites, who are the heads of sedition among them, saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾. So the lowest stratum of Hell is the abode of the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, and they will never find for themselves any ally or helper. Then, out of mercy toward His servants, blessed and exalted is He, He opens the door of repentance wide for the hypocrites and says to them: ﴿Except those who repent﴾ to their Lord, believe in Him and in His Messenger with true faith, ﴿and reform﴾ their deeds, ﴿and hold fast to Allah﴾ and shake off their hands from the hands of the disbelievers, ﴿and devote their religion to Allah﴾, so they no longer show off to anyone with their deeds. Those who have risen to this level of perfection are with the believers; their reward is one, and Allah will soon grant the believers a great reward, which is honour in this world and happiness in the Hereafter.

Finally, in verse [147], the Exalted affirms His independence from His creation and His exemption from desire for vengeance. Whenever His servant, however much he transgresses, does evil, disbelieves and wrongs, if he repents, reforms, believes and gives thanks, He does not punish him with the least punishment, for there is no need for Him to torment His servants. So He, Mighty and Majestic, says while addressing His servants: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing﴾. He does not lose the good deed with Him. Indeed, He thanked the prostitute who gave water to a thirsty dog, so He forgave her and admitted her into Paradise.

Lessons from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers.

2- When believers disobey their Lord and take disbelievers as allies, Allah empowers their enemies over them, and they suffer humiliation at their hands.

3- Repentance erases what came before it, so that the penitent from sin is like one who has no sin, whatever sin has overcome him.

4- Allah the Exalted does not punish the grateful believer, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, for faith and gratitude are a person's safety.

"Wa aslahu" (and they reform): what they had corrupted of beliefs and deeds.

"Wa'tasimu billah" (and hold fast to Allah): hold fast to His religion and put your trust in Him.

"Wa akhlasu dinahum lillah" (and devote their religion to Allah): free themselves from hypocrisy (nifaq) and polytheism (shirk).

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns Allah the Exalted guiding the believers to what honours them, perfects them and makes them happy. In this verse [144], He addresses them by the title of faith, which is the spirit through which there is life, and forbids them from taking the disbelievers as allies (awliya') instead of the believers. He says: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. Taking them as allies means showing them affection, supporting them, trusting them, relying on them and cooperating with them. Since the matter carries complete danger for them, Allah the Exalted threatened them by saying: ﴿Do you wish to give Allah a manifest authority against you?﴾ That is, He would abandon you, and set His enemies, the disbelievers, over you, so they would uproot you, or subdue and humiliate you and rule over you. Then He warned them against hypocrisy seeping into their hearts, so He made them hear His just judgment concerning the hypocrites, who are the heads of sedition among them, saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾. So the lowest stratum of Hell is the abode of the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, and they will never find for themselves any ally or helper. Then, out of mercy toward His servants, blessed and exalted is He, He opens the door of repentance wide for the hypocrites and says to them: ﴿Except those who repent﴾ to their Lord, believe in Him and in His Messenger with true faith, ﴿and reform﴾ their deeds, ﴿and hold fast to Allah﴾ and shake off their hands from the hands of the disbelievers, ﴿and devote their religion to Allah﴾, so they no longer show off to anyone with their deeds. Those who have risen to this level of perfection are with the believers; their reward is one, and Allah will soon grant the believers a great reward, which is honour in this world and happiness in the Hereafter.

Finally, in verse [147], the Exalted affirms His independence from His creation and His exemption from desire for vengeance. Whenever His servant, however much he transgresses, does evil, disbelieves and wrongs, if he repents, reforms, believes and gives thanks, He does not punish him with the least punishment, for there is no need for Him to torment His servants. So He, Mighty and Majestic, says while addressing His servants: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing﴾. He does not lose the good deed with Him. Indeed, He thanked the prostitute who gave water to a thirsty dog, so He forgave her and admitted her into Paradise.

Lessons from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers.

2- When believers disobey their Lord and take disbelievers as allies, Allah empowers their enemies over them, and they suffer humiliation at their hands.

3- Repentance erases what came before it, so that the penitent from sin is like one who has no sin, whatever sin has overcome him.

4- Allah the Exalted does not punish the grateful believer, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, for faith and gratitude are a person's safety.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 148–149:

Explanation of the words:

Al-su' (evil speech): that which causes harm to the one spoken about or to whom an action is done.

Sami'an 'aliman: Hearing the statements and knowing the deeds.

In tubdu (if you show): that you display and do not conceal.

Ta'fu 'an su' (you pardon an evil): meaning you do not hold it against him.

The meaning of the two verses:

He, may He be exalted, informs that He does not love the public mention of evil, and it follows from this that His believing servants must dislike what their Lord dislikes and love what He loves; and this is the condition of allegiance (wilayah), which is agreement and not opposition. When He, may He be exalted, forbade His servants the public mention of evil in the most eloquent expression and the most beautiful manner, He made an exception for the wronged person, for he may voice his grievance before the ruler in order to have the injustice lifted from him. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing and Knowing﴾ - (and still) - ﴿Hearing and Knowing﴾. Indeed, let him beware, so that he does not disobey by an evil act or by an evil word. Then He summoned His believing servants to do good, whether in secret or openly, and to pardon the one who has done evil, saying: ﴿If you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an evil, then indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾. So the doer of good will be rewarded with good, whether he displayed it or concealed it, and the one who pardons will be pardoned when his foot slips and he commits with his hand or tongue what makes him deserving of blame; he will be thanked by Allah for his earlier pardon, and so He pardons him. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The prohibition of publicly mentioning evil, and likewise of mentioning it secretly; it is not lawful for any believing man or woman to utter what hurts hearts and souls, except in the case of complaint and the exposure of injustice, and nothing else.

2- The recommendation of doing good, and that doing it secretly is like doing it openly; its reward is not diminished by public display nor increased by secrecy.

3- The recommendation of pardoning a believer when evil appears from him, and whoever pardons, Allah will pardon him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 150–152:

Explanation of the words:

"And His messengers" (wa-rusulihi): al-rusul is the plural of rasul (messenger), and they are a great multitude. It is said their number is three hundred and fourteen messengers.

"A way" (sabilan): that is, a path between disbelief and faith. There is no path in between except one of two: faith or disbelief. Whoever believes in all the messengers is the believer, and whoever believes in some and disbelieves in others is a disbeliever, like one who believes in none of them.

"And they did not differentiate" (wa-lam yufarriqu): as the Jews differentiated, believing in Musa (Moses) and disbelieving in ʿIsa (Jesus) and Muhammad (ﷺ), and as the Christians differentiated, believing in Musa and ʿIsa and disbelieving in Muhammad (ﷺ). They are therefore disbelievers.

"Their rewards" (ajurahum): the reward of their faith in the messengers of Allah and their righteous deeds, which is Paradise, the abode of bliss.

Meaning of the verses:

The Most High informs, establishing His judgment upon the Jews and the Christians as true disbelief about which there is no doubt. He says: indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to take between that, that is, between disbelieving in some and believing in others, a way (sabilan), that is, a path by which they reach a false and corrupt doctrine, which is choosing among the messengers of Allah: whomever they wish to believe in, they believe in, and whomever they do not wish to believe in, they disbelieve in and do not believe. By this they have disbelieved with a disbelief that is beyond doubt. For them, through this, is a humiliating punishment, by which they are humiliated and abased as recompense for their arrogance and evil deeds. The Most High said: ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. He thus recorded disbelief upon them three times: the first time by His saying ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾, the second by His saying ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾, and the third by His saying ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾, where He did not say "and We have prepared for them," but rather used the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, to record disbelief upon them and to point to the cause of the ruling, which is disbelief.

This is what the second verse [151] contains. As for the third verse, His saying ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾, it is contrasted with the verse before it in its wording and its meaning. The first verse contained the ruling of disbelief upon the Jews and the Christians and the humiliating punishment for them, while the second contained the ruling of the faith of the Muslims and the enduring bliss for them, which is what their Lord promised them by His saying ﴿Those, He will give them their rewards, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. So He forgave them their sins and showed them mercy by admitting them into the abode of His honor among His friends.

Lessons of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Establishing the disbelief of the Jews and the Christians, because of the corruption of their beliefs and the invalidity of their deeds.

2- The disbelief of whoever denies Allah and His messenger, even in one matter of what it is obligatory to believe in.

3- The invalidity of the faith of one who believes in some of the messengers and disbelieves in others.

4- The validity of the religion of Islam and the invalidity of Judaism and Christianity, since the Most High threatened the Jews and the Christians with a humiliating punishment, and promised the believers the full payment of their rewards, forgiveness and mercy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 153–154:

Explanation of the words:

*Jahrah* (جهرة): openly, that we see and witness with our own eyes.

*As-sa'iqah* (الصاعقة): a sharp sound and a violent quaking by which they were struck senseless.

*Bi-zulmihim* (بظلمهم): because of their wrongdoing in asking for what was not fitting.

*Ittakhadhu al-'ijl* (اتخذوا العجل): that is, they took it as a god and worshipped it.

*Fa-'afawna 'an dhalik* (فعفونا عن ذلك): that is, He did not hold them accountable for it.

*Sultanan mubinan* (سلطاناً مبيناً): a clear proof and complete authority by which He overcame His enemies.

*Wa-rafa'na fawqahumu al-Tur* (ورفعنا فوقهم الطور): that is, the Mount of Tur at Sinai.

*Adkhulu al-bab sujjadan* (ادخلوا الباب سجداً): that is, bowing humbly and submissively before God, in thanks for His blessings upon them.

*La ta'addu* (لا تعدوا): do not transgress, that is, do not go beyond what has been set as a limit for you, by turning from the work you were commanded to do to something else within it.

*Mithaqan ghalizan* (ميثاقا غليظا): a firm covenant, confirmed by oaths.

The meaning of the two verses:

When the Lord, exalted is He, censured the People of the Book for their saying, "We believe in some of the messengers and disbelieve in others," since the Jews believed in Moses and disbelieved in Jesus, and the Christians believed in Jesus and disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), just as the Jews also disbelieved in him, He mentioned to His Messenger that when the Jews ask you to send down to them a book from heaven, do not be surprised at their saying and do not concern yourself with it, for this is their custom and their habit. They had asked Moses before you for something greater than this, saying to him, "Show us God openly," so they angered God, the Exalted, and the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on. They took the calf as a god to worship in Moses' absence from them, and this came from them after they had witnessed the clear signs, for God split the sea for them, delivered them, and drowned their enemy. Despite this, God pardoned them and gave their prophet a clear authority, yet this did not change their nature. This is what the first verse [153] contains, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. They asked Moses for even more than that, saying, "Show us God openly." So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf after the clear signs had come to them, but We pardoned that, and We gave Moses a clear authority.﴾ As for the second verse [154], God informed us that He raised the Mount above them as a threat and a warning, because they refused to commit themselves to acting upon what is in the Torah. When the mountain was raised above them, they feared, and so they pledged, giving a covenant by that, but they broke it, as the report of that will come later. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We raised the Mount above them for their covenant.﴾ And His saying: ﴿And We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating..."﴾ This was when Joshua son of Nun, the servant of Moses, entered the city of Jerusalem as a conqueror. God revealed to him that he should command the Children of Israel to enter the city gate humbly and submissively, thanking God for the blessing of the conquest. Instead of obeying and entering the gate bowing humbly, they entered it crawling on their buttocks, out of deceit and obstinacy, and we seek God's refuge. And His saying: ﴿... And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾ meaning: We forbade them to hunt on the Sabbath, but they transgressed the prohibition and hunted in disobedience and rebellion. And His saying: ﴿... And We took from them a firm covenant﴾ meaning: that they would act upon what We legislated for them, as lawful and unlawful, in the Torah. Despite this, they disobeyed, rebelled, and defied. Therefore it is no wonder that they ask you, to test your mission and so that they might believe in you, to send down to them a book from heaven.

This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, in verse [154]: ﴿And We raised the Mount above them for their covenant, and We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating," and We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath..."﴾ That is, do not go beyond what We made lawful for you to what We made unlawful for you. ﴿... And We took from them a firm covenant...﴾.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The obstinacy of the People of the Book toward the Islamic call, and their disbelief in it while knowing that it is a call to truth.

2- Clarification of the vile qualities of the Jews and the wickedness that clung to them throughout their lives.

3- The Jews' breaking of covenants and pledges became a nature for them that never leaves them, and therefore it is obligatory not to trust in their covenants and pledges.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Fa-bima naqdihim* (﴿فبما نقضهم﴾): The *ba'* is causative, meaning "because of" their breaking. *Naqd* means undoing a covenant after it has been established.

*Bi-ghayri haqq* (﴿بغير حق﴾): Without any justification for killing them, and there was never any justification for killing the prophets.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 163–166:

Explanation of the words:

Inna awhayna ilayka (Indeed, We have revealed to you): al-wahy (revelation) is swift, hidden notification. God's revelation to His prophets is His informing them of what He wills to make them know of matters of religion and others.

Al-Asbat (the Tribes): the sons of Ya'qub, peace be upon him.

Zaburan (Psalms): the Zabur is one of the divine books, which He sent down to His prophet Dawud, peace be upon him.

Qad qasasnahum alayka (We have related them to you): In Surah al-An'am, eighteen messengers are mentioned, and seven are mentioned in other surahs: Muhammad (ﷺ), Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, Dhu'l-Kifl, Idris and Adam.

Hujjah (argument): an excuse with which they may plead before their Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

Meaning of the verses:

It is reported that when the Jews heard what Allah had revealed concerning them in the preceding verse, they denied that this was revelation and said, "Allah has revealed nothing to anyone except Musa." Allah refuted their claim with His words: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nuh and the prophets after him...﴾, so He mentioned a number of prophets. Then He said, "and messengers": that is, We sent messengers, "whom We have related to you before", meaning He related to him their names and some of what happened to them with their peoples, and they conveyed the call of their Lord; and He sent messengers whom He did not relate to him. And beyond that, He spoke to Musa directly, causing him to hear speech without any intermediary. So how can the Jews deny this and claim that Allah has sent down nothing to any human, when He sent them as messengers, bringing good news to whoever believed and did righteous deeds of Paradise, and warning whoever disbelieved and associated partners and did evil of the Fire? He did this only to remove the argument of the people on the Day of Resurrection, so that they would not say, "Our Lord, You did not send us a messenger." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾, that is, after their sending. ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty﴾, prevailing, not opposed in anything He wills, ﴿Wise﴾ in His actions and His management. This is some of what the three verses [163–165] contain. As for the fourth verse [166], which is His words: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels also bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as a witness.﴾

It is reported that a group of Jews gathered before the Prophet ﷺ, and he informed them that he was the Messenger of Allah, truly and in fact, and invited them to believe in him and in the true religion he had brought. They said: "Who will testify for you to the prophethood, since prophets appear at one time, so some of them testify for others? And who testifies for you?" So Allah sent down His words: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you...﴾, meaning: sending down a Book to you is His testimony for you to prophethood and messengership. He sent it down with His knowledge that you are fit for being chosen and sent, and with everything that humanity needs for its completion and happiness, since it contains the greatest legislation, which humanity, even if it all gathered, would be unable to produce the like of. Is this not sufficient as testimony for you to prophethood and messengership? Indeed, yes. And the angels also bear witness. ﴿...And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾, so do not seek a testimony after His testimony, if they had understanding.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the principle of divine revelation.

2- The first of the messengers was Nuh, peace be upon him, and the last of them was Muhammad ﷺ.

3- Affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, Exalted.

4- Explanation of the wisdom in sending messengers, which is to remove the argument against people on the Day of Resurrection.

5- The testimony of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and of the angels to the prophethood and messengership of the Seal of the Prophets ﷺ.

6- What the Qur'an contains of legislation, and of knowledge and sciences gathered between its covers, is the greatest testimony to the prophethood and messengership of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 167–170:

Explanation of the words:

Kafaru wa sadd (disbelieved and averted): kafaru: they denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ; wa sadd: they turned people away from faith in him ﷺ by sowing the seeds of doubt.

Kafaru wa zalamu (disbelieved and wronged): they denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, and they wronged themselves by remaining in their denial, out of envy and jealousy toward the Arabs, that there should be among them a messenger who would bring them out of darkness into light.

Al-Rasul (the Messenger): this is Muhammad ﷺ in his mission, the truthful one in his call.

Fa-amanu khayran lakum (then believe; it is better for you): that is, your belief would be better for you.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, established the proof for the message of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through His own testimony to his prophethood, the testimony of His angels, and the testimony of the Qur'an to the divine knowledge and insights it contains, He then informed, exalted is He, that those who disbelieved and averted from the way of Allah, namely the Jews, have gone astray in a far-reaching error, from which return to the truth may be nearly impossible. This is what the first verse [167] contains. As for the second verse [168], He informed that those who disbelieved and wronged, who are also the Jews, Allah would not forgive them nor guide them to any path, except the path of Hell. This rests upon His established way with His creation: when a person disbelieves out of obstinate denial and adds wrongdoing to disbelief, no readiness remains in him to accept divine guidance. No path remains for him that could be hoped for him to travel except the path of Hell, in which he will abide forever. His saying, exalted is He, at the end of the verse, ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, affirms that the entry of such Jews into Hell and their abiding there is not a difficult matter for Allah, nor something He finds hard to do, but rather is easy. As for the last verse [170], it contains a divine proclamation addressed to all people, polytheists and People of the Book alike: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you﴾, the complete and final one, has come to you with the true religion from your Lord. So believe in him; it is better for you. And if you refuse and turn away, preferring evil to good and misguidance to guidance, then know that to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, by creation, dominion, and disposal, and He will recompense you for what you have chosen of disbelief and misguidance: Hell, and evil is the destination. For He is All-Knowing of those who answered His call and believed and obeyed, and of those who turned away, disbelieved, and disobeyed; All-Wise in placing recompense in its fitting place. Thus He does not repay the good-doer with evil, nor the evil-doer with good.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The worst disbelief is that which is accompanied by averting from the way of Allah and by wrongdoing, and this is the disbelief of the Jews, may Allah protect us.

2- It is the way of Allah, exalted is He, that when a servant goes far into error and sinks deeply into evil and corruption, repentance becomes nearly impossible for him, so he dies in that state and is destroyed.

3- The Muhammadan message is universal for all people, the white and the yellow among them.

4- Affirmation of the attributes of knowledge and wisdom for Allah, exalted is He, and by their necessity the just and merciful recompense is accomplished.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 171–173:

Explanation of the words:

O People of the Book (ya ahl al-kitab): here this refers to the Christians.

Do not go to excess in your religion (la taghlu fi dinikum): al-ghuluw (excess) means going beyond the proper limit in something. Jesus, peace be upon him, is the servant of Allah and His messenger, but they went to excess regarding him and said that he is God.

The Messiah (al-Masih): this is Jesus, peace be upon him. He was given the title al-Masih because he was "masseh" (wiped clean) of sins, meaning he had no sin at all.

His word which He cast (kalimatuhu alqaha): that is, the word of Allah the Exalted to him, "Be" (﴿كُنْ﴾), and he was. Alqaha ila Maryam: he conveyed it to her and delivered it to her, and it was the words of the angels to her: "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary."

And a soul from Him (wa ruhun minhu): that is, Jesus came about by the breathing of Gabriel, the spirit of Allah, into the opening of her garment.

Guardian (wakilan): one who protects and a witness, all-knowing.

Will never disdain (lan yastankif): will not refuse to be a servant of Allah out of pride and arrogance.

Will be arrogant (wa yastakbir): he sees himself as greater than what he was asked to say or do, out of self-admiration and conceit.

A protector or a helper (waliyyan wa la nasiran): that is, on the Day of Resurrection they will not find a protector to defend them, nor a helper to aid them so that they do not enter the Fire and are not punished therein.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues with the People of the Book. In the first verse [171], the Lord, blessed and exalted, addressed the Christians by the title of the Book, which is the Gospel, and forbade them from excess in their religion, such as extremism and over-strictness, like monasticism and abstaining from women, and whatever else of innovations to which excess leads. He also forbade them from saying about Allah, blessed and exalted, other than the truth, which is attributing a son to Him, exalted He is far above that by a great exaltation. He informed them that Jesus was never anything but the messenger of Allah and His word which He cast to Mary, when He sent Gabriel to her and gave her the good news that Allah would grant her a pure boy. He breathed, and he is the spirit of Allah, into the opening of her garment, so Jesus came about by the word of creation, which is "Be" (﴿كُنْ﴾), and because of that breathing of the spirit of Allah, Gabriel, peace be upon him. So Jesus is not Allah, nor the son of Allah. So return to the truth and believe in Allah and His messengers, Gabriel, Jesus, and Muhammad ﷺ, and do not say falsehood and vanity: "Allah is the third of three gods." Cease this false saying; your ceasing will be better for you in state and outcome. Indeed Allah, glory be to Him, is one God, without partner, without equal, and without a son. Glory be to Him; He is exalted, majestic, and magnified above having a son. He had no consort, and He had no need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, in creation, dominion, judgment, and management. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is sufficient as a guardian, a witness, and all-knowing. So Allah the Exalted is sufficient for you as Lord and God, for He suffices you in everything that concerns you, so do not turn to other than Him and do not seek anyone besides Him.

This is what the first verse [171] indicates. As for the second [172] and third [173] verses, Allah the Exalted informed that His servant and messenger, the Messiah, peace be upon him, will never disdain to worship Allah and to be attributed to Him by the title of servanthood, so it is said "the servant of Allah and His messenger." Even the near angels, let alone others, do not disdain worshipping Allah the Exalted or the title of servanthood, for they are the servants of Allah and His angels. Then Allah the Exalted threatened every person who disdains His worship and is arrogant toward it among all people, that He will gather them all and call them to account for their deeds. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, believing in His divinity alone and worshipping Him alone with the kinds of worship He prescribed for them, which are the righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty; the good deed is multiplied tenfold, and it may be multiplied up to seven hundredfold.

As for those who disdained and were arrogant, that is, pride and arrogance led them to not accept the truth and return to it, and they persisted in false belief and corrupt action, Allah the Exalted will punish them with a painful punishment, that is, a painful one, and they will not find for themselves, besides Him, any protector or helper, so their end will be the punishment of eternity as recompense for what they used to do.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1. The prohibition of excess in religion, for it is among the causes that lead to innovation and misguidance.

2. The prohibition of speaking about Allah the Exalted without knowledge, absolutely, and speaking about Him other than the truth in particular.

3. Clarification of the correct belief concerning Jesus, peace be upon him: that he is the servant of Allah and His messenger, who came about by the word of Allah and the breathing of Gabriel, peace be upon him.

4. The prohibition of disdaining the truth and being arrogant in accepting it.

5. Clarification of the otherworldly recompense, which is either bliss or hellfire.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verses 174–175:

Explanation of the words:

Burhan (proof, argument): Burhan means a decisive proof, and what is meant here is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Nuran mubinan (a clear light): this is the Noble Qur'an.

Wa-i'tasamu (and hold fast): that is, hold firmly to the Qur'an and to the laws (shara'i') it carries.

Fi rahmatin minhu (in mercy from Him): Paradise.

Sirat (a path): a way that leads them to the nearness of their Lord in the abode of honour.

Meaning of the two verses:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, calls out to all people, polytheists, Jews and Christians, informing them and establishing the proof against them that He has sent to them His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the shining proof and the decisive evidence for the existence of God, His knowledge and His power, and for the obligation to believe in Him and His messengers and the necessity of worshipping Him by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger. He has sent down to him His Book, which is healing, sufficient, guiding, and a clear light, by which God guides whoever follows His good pleasure to the paths of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light. Thereby God has left the people with no excuse, and has cut off from them every pretext and argument. They are then of two kinds: believer and disbeliever. As for those who believed in God as Lord and God, and in His Messenger as prophet and messenger, and held fast to the Qur'an, making lawful what it makes lawful, unlawful what it makes unlawful, affirming its reports, and adhering to its manners, these are the ones whom He will admit into His mercy and bounty. That is by delivering them from the Fire and admitting them into the Gardens, and that is the great triumph, as God said: "Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed." As for those who disbelieved in Him, His Messenger and His Book, their destination is known and their recompense is established, so there is no need to mention it: it is deprivation and loss.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The Islamic call is a general call, addressed equally to the white and the yellow.

2- The term "proof" (burhan) is applied to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), because of his unlettered state and his perfection, in which no human can hope to rival him, it is a proof of the existence of God, His knowledge and His mercy.

3- The Qur'an is a light, because through it one attains guidance to the path of salvation and the ways of happiness and perfection.

4- The price of happiness and entry into Paradise is faith in God and His Messenger, belief in meeting Him, and righteous deeds, which is holding fast to the Book and the Sunnah, expressed by the term i'tisam.

The Lord, blessed and exalted, calls out to all people, polytheists, Jews and Christians, informing them and establishing the proof against them that He has sent to them His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the shining proof and the decisive evidence for the existence of God, His knowledge and His power, and for the obligation to believe in Him and His messengers and the necessity of worshipping Him by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger. He has sent down to him His Book, which is healing, sufficient, guiding, and a clear light, by which God guides whoever follows His good pleasure to the paths of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light. Thereby God has left the people with no excuse, and has cut off from them every pretext and argument. They are then of two kinds: believer and disbeliever. As for those who believed in God as Lord and God, and in His Messenger as prophet and messenger, and held fast to the Qur'an, making lawful what it makes lawful, unlawful what it makes unlawful, affirming its reports, and adhering to its manners, these are the ones whom He will admit into His mercy and bounty. That is by delivering them from the Fire and admitting them into the Gardens, and that is the great triumph, as God said: "Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed." As for those who disbelieved in Him, His Messenger and His Book, their destination is known and their recompense is established, so there is no need to mention it: it is deprivation and loss.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The Islamic call is a general call, addressed equally to the white and the yellow.

2- The term "proof" (burhan) is applied to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), because of his unlettered state and his perfection, in which no human can hope to rival him, it is a proof of the existence of God, His knowledge and His mercy.

3- The Qur'an is a light, because through it one attains guidance to the path of salvation and the ways of happiness and perfection.

4- The price of happiness and entry into Paradise is faith in God and His Messenger, belief in meeting Him, and righteous deeds, which is holding fast to the Book and the Sunnah, expressed by the term i'tisam.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 4, verse 176:

Explanation of the words:

Yastaftunaka (they ask you for a ruling): they seek your decision concerning such-and-such.

Yuftikum (He explains to you): He clarifies for you what is unclear to you regarding the matter of the kalalah.

Al-kalalah (the one who leaves no heirs in the direct line): a man dies leaving neither a child nor a grandchild, and leaves only a brother or a sister.

Al-hazz (share): the portion.

An tadillu (lest you go astray): so that you do not err, that is, make mistakes in the division of the estate.

Meaning of the noble verse:

This verse is called the verse of the kalalah. The verses of inheritance are four. The first concerns the child and the parent: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [An-Nisa: 11]. The second concerns the husband and wife: ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave﴾ [An-Nisa: 12], etc. And concerning the maternal siblings: ﴿And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister﴾ [An-Nisa: 12], etc. These two verses came earlier, at the beginning of Surat an-Nisa. The third is this one: ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾, etc. It concerns the inheritance of brothers and sisters when one of them dies leaving no child and no grandchild, and this is the meaning of kalalah. The fourth is at the end of Surat al-Anfal, and it concerns the relatives by blood (dhawu al-arham), namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [Al-Anfal: 75].

This verse was revealed when some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, asked about the kalalah. So Allah, exalted is He, said: They ask you, O Messenger, about the kalalah. Say to the askers: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah. This is His ruling: if a man dies, whether male or female, leaving no child and no grandchild, and has a full sister or a sister by the father, she has half of what he left. He also inherits from her if she has no child and no grandchild. If there are two sisters, they have two-thirds of what he left. If there are brothers and sisters, men and women, that is, males and females, then the male has the share of two females. After Allah, exalted is He, explained how the one who dies as a kalalah is inherited from, He said, explaining the wisdom of this clarification: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾, that is, so that you do not go astray in the division of estates, thereby missing the truth and acting unjustly in the division of your wealth. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, so nothing is unknown to Him and nothing is hidden from Him. How could it be otherwise, since He has encompassed everything in knowledge, glory be to Him; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

Guidance from the noble verse:

From the guidance of the noble verse:

1- The permissibility of asking one who knows when one does not know, in order to obtain the knowledge one seeks.

2- Affirmation of the existence of Allah, exalted is He, as All-Knowing, All-Powerful, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and confirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), since the Companions' question and the Lord's answer through His revelation sent down to His Messenger establish and confirm this.

3- Explanation of the division of the estate of one who dies as a kalalah, whether man or woman. A single sister has half of what her brother leaves; two sisters have two-thirds; brothers together with sisters: the male has the share of two females. A brother inherits from his sister if she has no child and no grandchild; brothers and sisters inherit from their sister, the male receiving the share of two females, if she leaves no child and no grandchild.
